Updated README and docs/focrq-format examples plus robot schema/health/version goldens. Verification passed: python3 scripts/check_focrq_format.py; cargo +nightly fmt --check; cargo +nightly test cli::tests --lib; cargo +nightly test robot::tests --lib; cargo +nightly test quant::focrq --lib; cargo +nightly test native_engine::weights::tests --lib; cargo +nightly test --test cli_robot_golden; git diff --check on touched files. scripts/check.sh passed docs/oracle/ledger scripts, cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and full cargo test (573 lib passed, 1 ignored; all integration/doc tests passed). Final ubs --diff stalled silently and was interrupted; follow-up filed as bd-3omg.

title: OcrEngine owning one asupersync Runtime: sync main, ShutdownController, spawn_blocking+timeout, single-forward concurrency discipline
description:
# OcrEngine owns the asupersync Runtime (P0-engine-runtime)

## BACKGROUND / WHY
G6 requires the library API to be **synchronous and blocking** — the async runtime is an owned implementation detail, never leaked to the host. The proven integration pattern from `franken_whisper` (plan §3.3, the asupersync-mega-skill, doctrine #5) is layered and is THE pattern to copy. Getting this frame right in Phase 0 prevents the frankensearch deadlock saga (5 commits to converge) from recurring.

## CURRENT STATE
`src/lib.rs` has an `OcrEngine { _private: () }` stub with `new()` and a `recognize` that returns NotImplemented. `src/main.rs` is already a sync `fn main()->ExitCode` that parses clap and maps `err.exit_code()`. `orchestrator.rs` exists as a skeleton (P0-crate-layout). asupersync + ctrlc deps are COMMENTED in Cargo.toml. This bead wires the runtime and the sync facade for real (empty pipeline body — the model forward is Phase 1).

## WHAT TO DO (concrete deliverable, verified facts transcribed)
1. **Uncomment + pin deps** in `Cargo.toml`: `asupersync = { version = ">=0.3.5, <0.4", default-features = false }` (local /dp/asupersync = 0.3.5), `ctrlc = "3.4"`.
2. **`OcrEngine` OWNS exactly one `Runtime`**, built with: `RuntimeBuilder::new().worker_threads(2).blocking_threads(1,4).thread_name_prefix("focr").build()` (plan §3.3). Store the `Runtime` (and its `Handle`) in `OcrEngine`. The single `OcrModel` lives behind an `Arc` + `Weak` global cache (lib.rs/native_engine `mod.rs` doc already references this); Phase 0 the model is absent so this is a placeholder.
3. **Public methods stay SYNC**: internally `runtime.handle().spawn(async {...})` then `runtime.block_on(handle)`. Callers see a blocking API. `OcrEngine::recognize(&self, image_path)` runs the (empty Phase-0) pipeline via this path and returns `NotImplemented` from the empty stage, proving the sync facade works.
4. **CPU-bound stages run via `spawn_blocking` wrapped in a timeout**: `asupersync::time::timeout(wall_now(), budget, Box::pin(spawn_blocking(op)))` for per-page/per-stage budgets, env-overridable (`FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_<STAGE>_MS`). Phase 0 wires the wrapper with a no-op `op` to prove the budget/cancellation plumbing compiles and fires (a timeout test).
5. **`ShutdownController` in sync `main`**: install a Ctrl+C `ShutdownController` (ctrlc) in `main`/`run(cli)`, thread a `Copy` `CancellationToken` (deadline + global ShutdownController) into the engine; `checkpoint()` boundaries threaded into the (Phase-0 empty) per-page / per-decode-step loops. Cancellation is **cooperative** — `spawn_blocking` keeps running on drop, so the token must go INTO the closure.
6. **Streaming results** scaffold: per-page text streams to the robot/NDJSON consumer via `std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel` (bounded) + `std::thread`; main loops `recv_timeout(~40ms)` until `worker.is_finished()`, then drains and `join()`s. Phase 0 wires an empty worker that immediately finishes, proving the loop.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE (measured evidence)
- **`fn main()` stays SYNCHRONOUS — no `#[asupersync::main]`.** Runtime lives BELOW main, inside the engine, never spanning the process (plan §3.3). This is what makes the library embeddable (G6).
- **Intra-op math parallelism is the frankentorch kernel's OWN rayon pool, NOT asupersync tasks.** asupersync is orchestration + cancellation + IO; the heavy GEMMs saturate cores via the kernel's pool. Pin the rayon global pool to physical cores; constrain blocking concurrency to EXACTLY ONE live forward (the sequential page loop) so only one N-core fan-out ever runs. Small `blocking_threads` (1,2)–(1,4) is a guard, not the mechanism.
- **HARD RULE (the deadlock-proof template, doctrine #5):** NEVER nest rayon under a held lock; NEVER nest a second asupersync runtime inside a task. The engine owns exactly one runtime; the model forward fans out across all cores internally; the outer page/document loop is **sequential** and calls the blocking facade. This is the durable fix the frankensearch deadlock saga converged on after 5 commits.
- **"Streaming per-page" = streaming the OUTPUT of a sequentially-processed page, never concurrent forwards** (which would oversubscribe rayon N×).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- **Kill-switch / deadlock watchdog:** the `many_pages_without_deadlock` CI watchdog test (pages ≫ pool) hangs on regression — its scaffold lands in P0-test-harness; this bead must make the concurrency frame such that that watchdog can pass once the forward lands.
- Runtime capacity certificate (a later gauntlet artifact): streaming uses bounded channels (backpressure, never unbounded growth); errors/cancellation map to an `Outcome`-style result internally (not panics across the FFI-free boundary). Phase 0 wires the bounded channel correctly.
- Do not spawn a `num_cpus` rayon fan-out per worker; one global rayon pool sized to physical (P-)cores; asupersync blocking pool stays tiny.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `OcrEngine::new()` builds and owns one `Runtime`; `Drop` shuts it down cleanly (no leaked threads — assert via a thread-count check or runtime shutdown).
- Public API is sync/blocking; no `async fn` leaks to the public surface (compile-checked: `recognize` is a plain `fn`).
- A Ctrl+C / per-stage-timeout aborts at the next `checkpoint()` boundary (test with a no-op stage that sleeps past budget → returns `FocrError::Timeout`).
- Bounded streaming channel never grows unbounded (test with a slow consumer; backpressure observed).
- No nested runtime, no rayon-under-lock (structural; verified by P0-test-harness watchdog scaffold).

## TESTS REQUIRED
- `engine_owns_single_runtime_and_drops_clean` — construct/drop, assert no leaked `focr`-prefixed threads.
- `spawn_blocking_timeout_fires` — a stage whose `op` sleeps past a tiny budget returns `Timeout` (exit code 5); structured log records stage name, budget, elapsed.
- `cancellation_token_into_closure_aborts` — set the ShutdownController, assert the checkpoint loop exits with `Cancelled` (exit code 6).
- `bounded_stream_backpressure` — slow consumer; the bounded `sync_channel` blocks the worker rather than growing.
- All tests emit **structured JSON-line logs** (the project mandates comprehensive tests with great logging): one line per event with `{test, phase, stage, elapsed_ms, outcome}`.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
`depends_on P0-crate-layout` (needs `orchestrator.rs` + the module skeleton + the Cargo.toml frame). Downstream: P0-robot-skeleton (streaming events), P0-test-harness (the deadlock watchdog), and every Phase-1 forward bead build on this engine frame.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## ADDENDUM (review2): wire the rayon global pool + FOCR_THREADS budget (it is named in the rationale but missing from the deliverable)

The rationale below already says 'Pin the rayon global pool to physical cores' and 'constrain blocking concurrency to EXACTLY ONE live forward', but the WHAT-TO-DO never actually initializes the pool or reads the budget. Plan §3.3 + §7.5 make this a real Phase-0 deliverable (the AF-5 / USL pool-sizing of §6.9 plugs in later, but the *single, physical-core-pinned* pool and the `FOCR_THREADS` override exist from Phase 0):

7. **Initialize exactly ONE global thread/CPU budget at engine construction**, read ONCE via `OnceLock`: `FOCR_THREADS` (env, §7.5) else the **physical** (P-)core count (NOT logical/`available_parallelism` — hyperthreads oversubscribe int8 GEMMs). Phase 0 has no frankentorch rayon pool yet (kernels are Phase 1), so Phase 0 wires the *budget value* + its `OnceLock` reader and a documented doc-comment, so that when the kernel pool lands in Phase 1 it is sized from this one source. Do NOT call `num_cpus`-wide fan-out per worker; the asupersync blocking pool stays tiny `(1,2)–(1,4)`; the (future) kernel pool is the single N-core fan-out.
8. **Expose the budget to the robot surface**: `robot health` reports the resolved `threads` budget and `robot backends` reports `logical_cpus` (already) PLUS the chosen `threads`/physical-core figure — both read from this single source (P0-robot-skeleton consumes it). This closes the gap where `robot health`'s documented 'threads budget' field had no producer.

**Rationale:** one budget source prevents the §3.3 oversubscription failure mode (rayon N× per concurrent forward) and gives §6.9/AF-5 a single knob to refine. **Test:** `thread_budget_reads_env_then_physical` — set `FOCR_THREADS=3`, assert the budget is 3; unset, assert it equals the physical-core count and is read exactly once (OnceLock). Structured log `{env_threads, physical_cores, resolved_budget}`.

(2) FOCR_THREADS budget — OnceLock, env else num_cpus physical (never logical); exposed as 'threads' on robot health AND backends (golden re-blessed w/ the value scrubbed host-independent). (3) Bounded streaming scaffold stream_pages (sync_channel, sequential producer, recv_timeout drain, worker join w/ error propagation). (4) Four named tests all green first-run: engine_owns_single_runtime_and_drops_clean, cancellation_token_into_closure_aborts (exit-6 contract asserted), bounded_stream_backpressure (max in-flight <= capacity+slack), thread_budget_reads_env_then_physical. title: Robot NDJSON skeleton + robot schema/health/backends emitting valid versioned JSON
description:
# Robot NDJSON skeleton + schema/health/backends (P0-robot-skeleton)

## BACKGROUND / WHY
G5 (agent-ergonomic) requires a **robot subcommand emitting versioned NDJSON events with a self-describing `robot schema`**, stable exit codes, `--json` everywhere, deterministic output under fixed sampling. Robot mode is the agent-first surface: line-oriented NDJSON, one JSON object per line, every line carrying `schema_version`, easy to pipe, no human decoration mixed with machine output (AGENTS.md Agent Ergonomics Requirements). This bead hardens the Phase-0 seed into a valid, contract-shaped surface that later phases extend.

## CURRENT STATE
`src/robot.rs` has `ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1`, `EVENT_KINDS = ["run_start","stage","page","run_complete","run_error"]`, `robot_schema()` returning a self-describing JSON, and one unit test. `src/cli.rs` already routes `Robot{Schema,Health,Backends}`: Schema emits `robot_schema()`; Health emits a minimal `{schema_version, status:"scaffold", ready:false, ...}`; Backends emits `{schema_version, simd_tiers:{selected:null,available:[],status:...}, logical_cpus}`. `emit()` prints one JSON object per line. This bead makes health/backends report **real Phase-0 truth** and seeds the event payload shapes.

## WHAT TO DO (verified facts transcribed)
1. **`robot schema`** — keep self-describing; expand to enumerate each event type's payload fields (per plan §7.3): `run_start`, `stage` (carries `stage` name, `seq`, `elapsed`, `budget`), `page` (per-page text/bbox as it completes — streaming), `run_complete`, `run_error` (carries the stable exit code). Every emitted line carries `schema_version` (the `ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` const). Keep it compact single-line JSON for agent parsers.
2. **`robot health`** — report real Phase-0 diagnostics: `model_present` (via `native_model_available()` from P0-model-resolution — cheap header sniff, no tensor load), the searched model dirs (`$FOCR_MODEL_DIR`, `~/.cache/franken_ocr/models`), `logical_cpus`, `threads` budget, schema_version, and a `ready` flag (false until the forward lands). Replace the hard-coded `"model_present": false`.
3. **`robot backends`** — report `logical_cpus` (already), and the SIMD tier surface shape: `simd_tiers.selected` stays `null` in Phase 0 with `status` noting runtime detection lands in Phase 3 (plan §6.2). Real tier detection (AMX>VNNI-512>VNNI-256>AVX2>scalar on x86; SMMLA>SDOT on ARM; scalar floor) is a Phase-3 bead — Phase 0 must leave a stable, parseable shape it can fill.
4. **NDJSON event-stream scaffold**: define the event-emission helper(s) that the engine's `sync_channel` worker feeds (`run_start` → `stage`* → `page`* → `run_complete` | `run_error`). Phase 0 wires an empty run that emits `run_start` then `run_error{code:1, "NotImplemented"}` (since the forward is Phase 1), proving the stream shape end-to-end.
5. **`focr ocr --robot` / `focr robot run`**: route to the streaming NDJSON path (engine worker thread + bounded channel, P0-engine-runtime). Phase 0 emits the empty-run event sequence.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Stable versioned schema; bump `ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` on any breaking change.** Agents pin to it.
- **Deterministic where possible** (G5): under fixed sampling (`temperature=0` greedy) same image+args → byte-identical output; a determinism gate asserts this (Phase 1+). Phase 0 the empty run is trivially deterministic.
- **No human decoration in robot mode** (AGENTS.md): stdout is data-only JSON lines; human markdown only in non-robot `focr ocr`.
- **`robot schema` self-describes the contract**; a contract test validates emitted events against a frozen JSON schema fixture (P0 seeds the fixture; full contract tests are Phase 5).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Do not let a `run_error` payload diverge from `FocrError::exit_code()` — the error code in the NDJSON MUST equal the process exit code (error.rs is the single source).
- Keep every line independently parseable (no multi-line JSON, no trailing human text).
- The schema is a forward contract: additive fields are fine; removing/renaming a field is a `ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `focr robot schema` emits one valid JSON object with `schema_version` and an entry per event kind incl. payload field lists.
- `focr robot health` emits valid JSON with real `model_present`, searched dirs, `logical_cpus`, `threads`, `schema_version`.
- `focr robot backends` emits valid JSON with `logical_cpus` and the stable (null-selected) `simd_tiers` shape.
- `focr ocr --robot` on a missing model emits `run_start` then `run_error` with `code:3` (ModelNotFound) — or `code:1` if forward-not-implemented — on one line each, all carrying `schema_version`.
- Every emitted line round-trips through `serde_json::from_str`.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit: `robot_schema` advertises all `EVENT_KINDS` with payload fields (extend existing test).
- Unit: `health_reports_model_absence` — with `FOCR_MODEL_DIR=/nonexistent`, `model_present` is false and searched dirs listed.
- Integration `robot_contract_smoke` (in `tests/robot_contract.rs`): spawn `focr robot schema|health|backends`, assert each line parses and carries `schema_version`; validate `schema` against a frozen JSON schema fixture (`tests/fixtures/robot_schema.json`). Structured logging per assertion.
- Integration `robot_ocr_empty_stream`: `focr ocr --robot <missing>` emits the documented event sequence on stdout (one JSON/line), exit code matches the `run_error` payload code.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
`depends_on P0-crate-layout` (robot.rs/cli.rs frame), `P0-engine-runtime` (the streaming `sync_channel` worker + event emission), `P0-model-resolution` (`native_model_available()` for `model_present` and the searched-dir list in health).

The fixture is the SCHEMA contract (event kinds + payload field lists), regenerated only via the explicit workflow.

title: fsqlite RunStore + _meta versioned schema + forward migrations + JSONL audit export/import
description:
# fsqlite RunStore + _meta schema (P0-runstore)

## BACKGROUND / WHY
The project persists durable local **run state + telemetry** via `fsqlite` (frankensqlite) — **NEVER `rusqlite`** (AGENTS.md, plan §4.1). This backs `focr runs [--id|--limit|--format plain|json|ndjson]` (query run history) and `focr sync export-jsonl|import-jsonl` (locked, atomic, one-way audit export/import). A versioned `_meta` schema with forward migrations means the on-disk store can evolve without breaking older binaries' reads. This is the honesty/telemetry substrate (G7) — every run, its parity receipt, and its perf ratios are recorded.

## CURRENT STATE
`storage.rs` and `sync.rs` exist as skeletons (P0-crate-layout). fsqlite deps are COMMENTED in Cargo.toml. No store, no `_meta`, no migrations yet. The `runs` and `sync` subcommands are not yet on the CLI surface (cli.rs has Ocr/Convert/Robot/Doctor only).

## WHAT TO DO (verified facts transcribed)
1. **Uncomment + pin deps** in `Cargo.toml`: `fsqlite = { path = "../frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite" }`, `fsqlite-types = { path = "../frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-types" }`, plus `uuid = { version="1", features=["serde","v4"] }`, `sha2 = "0.10"`.
2. **`RunStore` on fsqlite** (`storage.rs`): open/create the store at a resolved path (`~/.cache/franken_ocr/runs.db` or `$FOCR_RUN_STORE`); a `runs` table (run_id UUID, started_at, finished_at, input_path, mode, quant, model_version_tag, exit_code, status); telemetry rows (per-stage elapsed/budget). Phase 0: schema creation + insert/select for an empty/placeholder run; the rich telemetry columns are filled as the forward lands.
3. **`_meta` versioned schema + forward migrations**: a `_meta` table (schema_version, created_at, franken_ocr_version, **model_version_tag**) — the model_version_tag comes from the E-PM1 truth pack (pinned HF/GitHub source hashes + `source_sha256`). On open, run forward migrations from the stored `schema_version` to the binary's; refuse to open a store whose `schema_version` exceeds the binary's (forward-only, no downgrade), mapping to `FocrError::FormatMismatch` (exit 7).
4. **`focr sync export-jsonl|import-jsonl`** (`sync.rs`): locked, atomic, one-way **audit** export of runs to JSONL and import back (re-create/replay). Use file locking + atomic rename (write temp, fsync, rename). This mirrors the beads JSONL audit story.
5. **`focr runs`** subcommand: add `Runs { id: Option<...>, limit: Option<usize>, format: {plain,json,ndjson} }` to `cli.rs`, query `RunStore`, emit per `--format`.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **fsqlite, never rusqlite** (doctrine / G3 no-C-FFI default — fsqlite is the pure-Rust SQLite). Hard requirement.
- **`_meta` versioned, forward-migrating** — early dev, no users, no tech debt (AGENTS.md): do migrations the right way, no compatibility shims; a future binary migrates an older store forward, never the reverse.
- **model_version_tag from the truth pack** — every run records WHICH pinned model it ran against (E-PM1 hashes), so a perf/parity claim in the ledgers is traceable to the exact model version (the artifact-graph provenance mandate, plan §8.4).
- **One-way audit export** — JSONL is the human-auditable, git-trackable record; export is locked + atomic so a concurrent run never corrupts it.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- **No nested rayon under a held lock** applies to the store too — never call a rayon kernel while holding a store lock.
- Atomic write discipline: temp file in the same dir, fsync, atomic rename; never partial-write the JSONL.
- A store-version mismatch must produce a clear, actionable `FormatMismatch` error (exit 7), not a panic.
- Concurrent runs: file lock with a timeout; a stuck lock must not hang the process (map to a clear error).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `RunStore::open` creates the store + `_meta` if absent, runs forward migrations otherwise; refuses a too-new store with `FormatMismatch` (exit 7).
- A run can be inserted and queried by id/limit; `--format {plain,json,ndjson}` each emit valid output (ndjson = one JSON/line with schema_version).
- `focr sync export-jsonl` then `import-jsonl` round-trips the run set byte-stably (canonicalized ordering); export is atomic (no partial file on simulated crash).
- `_meta.model_version_tag` is populated from the truth-pack hash when available.
- Uses `fsqlite` (grep confirms NO `rusqlite`).

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit: `meta_schema_created_and_versioned`; `forward_migration_applies`; `too_new_store_refused_with_format_mismatch`.
- Unit: `run_insert_and_query_by_id_and_limit`.
- Integration `sync_jsonl_roundtrip` (real fsqlite store in a tempdir, NO mocks): insert N runs → export-jsonl → import into a fresh store → assert equal; assert atomicity (export to a temp, rename). Structured JSON-line logs per step.
- Integration `runs_format_matrix`: each `--format` emits parseable output; ndjson lines carry `schema_version`.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
`depends_on P0-crate-layout` (storage.rs/sync.rs frame + Cargo.toml). Soft dep on E-PM1 for the `model_version_tag` value (the column exists regardless; it is populated once the truth-pack hash is available — handled gracefully as `unknown` until then).
close_reason: DONE 2026-07-06. RunStore on fsqlite (src/storage.rs — grep-clean: the only 'rusqlite' match is the doc comment forbidding it): _meta versioned single-row (schema_version/created_at/franken_ocr_version/model_version_tag), forward-only migrations w/ explicit seam, too-new store REFUSED w/ FormatMismatch exit 7 (asserted); runs table keyed by uuid-v4. title: Error / exit-code type hardening: stable contract, robot parity, Timeout/Cancelled/FormatMismatch wiring
description:
# Error / exit-code type (P0-error-exit-codes)

## BACKGROUND / WHY
Stable exit codes are a **public contract** (G5, plan §7.4): `robot run_error` carries the same code in its payload, and agents branch on them. Existing codes must never be renumbered. This bead hardens the already-good `error.rs` into the full Phase-0 contract and guarantees robot/exit-code parity.

## CURRENT STATE
`src/error.rs` already defines `FocrError` with variants Usage→2, ModelNotFound→3, InputDecode→4, Timeout→5, Cancelled→6, FormatMismatch→7, NotImplemented→1, Other→1, plus `FocrResult<T>` and a passing `exit_codes_are_stable` test. `main.rs` maps `err.exit_code()` to `ExitCode`. The verified exit-code table (plan §7.4): `0` success · `1` generic error · `2` usage/CLI error · `3` model not found/not resolvable · `4` input decode error · `5` budget/timeout exceeded · `6` cancelled (Ctrl+C) · `7` format/version mismatch (`.focrq`).

## WHAT TO DO
1. **Confirm + freeze the table** as the single source of truth (the codes above). Document each code in a doc-comment block (already partially present) and add a `pub const` or a `#[doc]` table that the robot schema can reference.
2. **Robot parity**: ensure the `robot run_error` payload's `code` field is produced FROM `FocrError::exit_code()` (no second copy of the numbers). Add a helper `fn run_error_event(err: &FocrError) -> serde_json::Value` in robot.rs that reads `err.exit_code()` + `err.to_string()` + `schema_version`.
3. **Wire the new-in-engine variants**: `Timeout` (from `asupersync::time::timeout`, P0-engine-runtime), `Cancelled` (from the ShutdownController/CancellationToken), `FormatMismatch` (from RunStore `_meta` version check P0-runstore, and later `.focrq` header). Phase 0 must have a code path that can produce each (even if behind a test-only trigger) so the mapping is exercised end-to-end.
4. **`From` conversions**: keep `#[from] anyhow::Error` → Other→1; add ergonomic constructors where needed. Do NOT add a catch-all that hides a real category.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Codes are a frozen public contract** — agents branch on them; the same number appears in the process exit and in `run_error.code`. One source (error.rs) for both.
- **Distinct categories** — Timeout (5) vs Cancelled (6) vs FormatMismatch (7) are separate so agents can react (retry-with-bigger-budget vs user-aborted vs convert-again).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Never renumber an existing code (would break agents pinned to it).
- `NotImplemented` maps to 1 (generic) in Phase 0 — acceptable; it is not a separate public code.
- A panic must never replace a clean exit code; map error categories, don't `unwrap`.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `FocrError::exit_code()` returns the §7.4 table exactly (existing test passes + extended).
- `robot run_error` payload `code` == process exit code for every variant (single-source proof).
- Each of Timeout/Cancelled/FormatMismatch is reachable and produces its code in both the process exit and a robot event.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Extend `exit_codes_are_stable` to assert the full table incl. that NotImplemented==Other==1.
- `robot_error_code_matches_exit_code` — for every variant, `run_error_event(&err)["code"] == err.exit_code()`.
- An integration test that triggers a real Timeout (P0-engine-runtime no-op stage past budget) and asserts process exit 5 AND robot `run_error.code==5`.
- Structured logging: each test logs `{variant, exit_code, robot_code}`.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
`depends_on P0-crate-layout`. Tightly coupled to P0-engine-runtime (Timeout/Cancelled producers) and P0-robot-skeleton (run_error payload), P0-runstore (FormatMismatch on `_meta`) — those beads consume this contract.

# convert / ocr / doctor stubs (P0-stubs-convert-ocr-doctor)

## BACKGROUND / WHY
Phase 0 must present the full CLI surface so agents/humans see the real command shape, while the heavy work (model forward, weight transformer, self-repair) returns a **clear, actionable** error pointing at the phase that lands it. Agent-ergonomic errors that name the next step are part of G5. PDF input is **intentionally absent** — v1 is image-only (plan §7.7).

## CURRENT STATE
`cli.rs` already has the three stubs: `Ocr` → `NotImplemented("focr ocr — the model forward lands in Phase 1 ... §10")`; `Convert` → `NotImplemented("... weight transformer lands in Phase 2 ... §5")`; `Doctor` → `NotImplemented("... lands in Phase 5 ... §7")`. `Ocr` already has `image: PathBuf`, `--json`, `--robot`; `Convert` has `input`, `-o output`, `--quant {int8,int4}`. This bead refines the surfaces (arg completeness, validation, doctor capability reflection) without implementing the work.

## WHAT TO DO (verified facts transcribed)
1. **`focr ocr <image>` surface** — confirm v1-image-only (no `pdf` arg anywhere on the surface, plan §7.7). Add (as parsed-but-unused-until-Phase-1) the real args from the reference `infer()` signature so the surface is complete: `--base-size 1024`, `--image-size 640`, `--crop-mode` (Gundam vs Base), `--max-length 32768`, `--temperature 0.0`, `--no-repeat-ngram 35` (env `FOCR_NO_REPEAT_NGRAM`), `--ngram-window` (128 single / 1024 multi). Validate args in `to_request()` (e.g. reject negative sizes) and return `NotImplemented` from the engine call, not from arg parsing (so usage errors are exit 2, not-implemented is exit 1).
2. **`focr convert` surface** — add `--arch {generic,aarch64-smmla,x86-vnni,x86-amx}` (the `.focrq` pre-packing target, plan §5.4) alongside `--quant {int8,int4}`. Keep returning `NotImplemented("... Phase 2 §5")`.
3. **`focr doctor` surface** — Phase 0 stub that returns `NotImplemented("... Phase 5 §7")`, BUT shape it as the world-class-doctor pattern will need: it MUST be idempotent + reversible + capability-reflecting later. Phase 0: emit (with `--json`) a `{capabilities:[...], checks:[...], status:"scaffold"}` shape so the contract is visible; actual checks (model resolution, format version, perms) land in Phase 5.
4. **`--json` everywhere**: every subcommand accepts `--json` for machine output (G5).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Surface-complete now, implemented later** — agents discover the real flags in Phase 0; the FeatureUniverse/SurfaceMatrix (gauntlet) can already account every flag as `present|partial|missing|excluded`.
- **Usage errors (bad args) = exit 2; not-implemented = exit 1** — distinct categories so agents don't confuse a CLI mistake with a missing feature.
- **PDF excluded by design** (plan §7.7): a pure-Rust raster at byte-parity with MuPDF is unscoped and any pixel mismatch blows the L0 preprocessing parity gate; PDFs are rasterized out-of-band. `pdf` never appears on the surface.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Don't let parsed-but-unused args silently no-op once Phase 1 lands — wire them into `OcrRequest` so they're ready.
- `--quant`/`--arch` defaults must be explicit and documented.
- Doctor must never (even later) make a destructive change without backup/reversibility — Phase 0 just declares the capability shape.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `focr ocr --help` / `convert --help` / `doctor --help` show the complete flag surface; no `pdf` anywhere.
- Bad args → exit 2 (Usage); the not-yet-implemented body → exit 1 (NotImplemented), with a message naming the landing phase + plan section.
- `--json` accepted on each; `doctor --json` emits the `{capabilities, checks, status}` shape.
- `convert --arch` accepts the four pre-packing targets.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit: `ocr_args_validate` (negative size → Usage/exit 2); `convert_arch_enum_parses`; `no_pdf_on_surface` (assert help text has no `pdf`).
- Integration: spawn each stub, assert exit code + message contains the landing-phase pointer; `doctor --json` parses to the declared shape.
- Structured logging per assertion (`{cmd, args, exit_code, message_head}`).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
`depends_on P0-crate-layout` (cli.rs) and `P0-error-exit-codes` (Usage vs NotImplemented categories).

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## ADDENDUM (review2): extend the surface audit to `runs` / `sync` / `robot run`

This bead audits `ocr`/`convert`/`doctor` for surface-completeness, the Usage(exit 2)-vs-NotImplemented(exit 1) split, `--json` everywhere, and the no-`pdf` invariant. P0-runstore ADDS the `runs [--id|--limit|--format plain|json|ndjson]` and `sync export-jsonl|import-jsonl` subcommands (plan §7.2), and P0-robot-skeleton routes `ocr --robot` / `robot run`. Those surfaces must obey the SAME conventions, so extend the audit (the FeatureUniverse/SurfaceMatrix accounts EVERY surface, §8.5):

5. **`runs` / `sync` surface conventions** — confirm `runs --format {plain,json,ndjson}` and `sync export-jsonl|import-jsonl` accept `--json` where applicable (ndjson lines carry `schema_version`), bad args → exit 2 (Usage), and (Phase 0, before the store is fully wired) any not-yet-implemented body → exit 1 with a landing-phase pointer. No `pdf` anywhere on these surfaces either.
6. **`robot run` / `ocr --robot` routing** — assert the streaming NDJSON path is reachable and `--json`/`--robot` are mutually coherent (one human, one machine surface), per §7.3.
7. **Help-text completeness gate** — extend `no_pdf_on_surface` to scan the FULL `--help` tree (all subcommands incl. runs/sync/robot), not just ocr, so a stray `pdf` token anywhere fails.

**Tests (additive):** `runs_and_sync_args_obey_exit_categories`; `full_help_tree_has_no_pdf`; `robot_run_routes_to_streaming`. Structured logging per assertion `{cmd, args, exit_code, message_head}`.

title: Model resolution (no network at runtime): resolve_model + native_model_available header sniff + actionable errors
description:
# Model resolution, no network at runtime (P0-model-resolution)

## BACKGROUND / WHY
G3 forbids **network at inference time**: the model is resolved from local paths only. `resolve_model(spec)` finds a model by existing path OR short name searched across an ordered, env-driven dir list, failing with an **actionable** error that lists every searched dir (plan §7.5). `native_model_available()` does a cheap header sniff (magic bytes), no tensor load — used by `robot health`/`backends` and the model-gated test harness to decide skip-vs-run.

## CURRENT STATE
No resolution code exists yet. `robot health` hard-codes `model_present: false`. `scripts/fetch_model.sh` downloads the model out-of-band. This bead implements resolution + the sniff so health/backends report truth and the test harness can gate.

## WHAT TO DO (verified facts transcribed)
1. **`resolve_model(spec) -> FocrResult<PathBuf>`** (in `native_engine/mod.rs` per plan §4.1): if `spec` is an existing path, use it; else treat it as a short name and search, in order: `$FOCR_MODEL_DIR`, `~/.cache/franken_ocr/models`, (and any other documented defaults). On failure return `FocrError::ModelNotFound` (exit 3) whose message **lists every directory searched** (actionable). **No network** — resolution is filesystem-only.
2. **`native_model_available(path) -> bool`** — cheap header sniff: read the first few bytes and check the magic (`.focrq` magic `b"FOCRQ\0"` for converted weights; the safetensors header length+JSON for the raw shard). **No tensor load** — just the magic/header, fast enough to call on every `robot health`.
3. **Env overrides** (plan §7.5): `FOCR_MODEL_DIR`, `FOCR_THREADS`, `FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_*_MS`, `FOCR_QUANT` (int8/int4/f32 select if multiple `.focrq` present), `FOCR_FORCE_ARCH` (override SIMD dispatch for testing). Each numerics-affecting lever is read once via `OnceLock`, documented in its own doc-comment, defaulted, with an opt-out. Phase 0 wires `FOCR_MODEL_DIR` + `FOCR_QUANT` selection; the budget/arch ones are stubbed for later phases.
4. **Wire into `robot health`** (P0-robot-skeleton consumes this): `model_present` = `native_model_available(resolve_model(default_spec))`, plus the searched-dir list.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **No network at runtime** (G3) — download is strictly out-of-band (`fetch_model.sh`); the binary never fetches.
- **Actionable failure** — listing every searched dir turns a 'model not found' into a one-glance fix (set `FOCR_MODEL_DIR`).
- **Cheap sniff, no tensor load** — `robot health` must be instant; we only check magic bytes / header, never mmap+parse the 6.67 GB blob.
- **Single canonical artifact, many packings** — if multiple `.focrq` (per-arch / per-quant) are present, `FOCR_QUANT` selects; the loader later warns on `arch_target` mismatch and falls back to generic packing.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Tilde/home expansion must be robust cross-platform (no naive `~` left literal).
- A `.focrq` whose `format_version` exceeds the binary's → `FormatMismatch` (exit 7) — that check lives in the loader (Phase 2); resolution only sniffs the magic.
- Symlinks/relative paths: canonicalize before reporting the searched list.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `resolve_model(existing_path)` returns it; `resolve_model(short_name)` searches the ordered list; missing → `ModelNotFound` (exit 3) listing every searched dir.
- `native_model_available` returns true on a valid `.focrq`/safetensors header, false on garbage, WITHOUT loading tensors (assert it does not read more than a header's worth of bytes).
- No network call anywhere (grep: no http/reqwest at runtime).
- `robot health` reports real `model_present` + searched dirs.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit: `resolve_existing_path`; `resolve_short_name_search_order`; `missing_lists_searched_dirs`; `sniff_rejects_garbage`; `sniff_accepts_focrq_and_safetensors_headers` (using tiny fixture headers, no full model).
- Unit: `env_quant_selection_picks_focrq`.
- Integration: `health_reports_truth_with_FOCR_MODEL_DIR` (point at a tempdir with/without a fixture header).
- Structured logging: each test logs `{spec, searched_dirs, resolved, present}`.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
`depends_on P0-crate-layout` (native_engine/mod.rs) and `P0-error-exit-codes` (ModelNotFound/FormatMismatch). Consumed by P0-robot-skeleton (health) and P0-test-harness (skip-vs-run gating).

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## ADDENDUM (review2): FOCR_THREADS ownership clarification

This bead enumerates `FOCR_THREADS` among the env levers but defers its wiring. Per the review2 addendum on P0-engine-runtime, the `FOCR_THREADS` `OnceLock` reader + physical-core default now lands in P0-engine-runtime (it owns the runtime/thread budget). This bead owns `FOCR_MODEL_DIR` + `FOCR_QUANT` selection. Ensure there is **exactly one** `OnceLock` per env lever across the two beads (no duplicate readers) — `FOCR_THREADS` lives in the engine/runtime module, `FOCR_MODEL_DIR`/`FOCR_QUANT` in resolution. Add a doc-comment cross-reference so an implementer does not re-read `FOCR_THREADS` here.
close_reason: Completed the remaining Phase-0 model-resolution contract. The resolver now keeps filesystem-only behavior, searches missing relative specs under FOCR_MODEL_DIR plus the documented user cache, treats each FOCR_MODEL_DIR entry as either a direct artifact/package or a search root, reports search dirs to robot health, and honors FOCR_QUANT by preferring quant-specific short-name .focrq candidates such as unlimited-ocr.int4.focrq before generic candidates. native_model_available remains a bounded header sniff for .focrq or safetensors and robot health now emits model_spec, model_search_dirs, model_present, and the single-source model license notice. Added/extended tests for direct FOCR_MODEL_DIR artifacts, default basename search, quant-specific candidate selection without mutating process env, and the scrubbed robot_health golden. Verification passed: cargo fmt --check; rustfmt +nightly --edition 2024 --check src/native_engine/mod.rs src/cli.rs tests/cli_robot_golden.rs; git diff --check on touched files; cargo check --all-targets; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test (587 lib tests, all integration tests, doctests green); focused resolver and robot-health tests; ubs --only=rust on src/native_engine/mod.rs, src/cli.rs, and tests/cli_robot_golden.rs all reported 0 critical issues; runtime network grep over src and Cargo.toml found no reqwest/ureq/curl/http/hf_hub/huggingface hits; br dep cycles count 0.

title: Model-gated test harness: skip-with-SUCCESS without weights, prove-native-path-ran, many_pages_without_deadlock watchdog scaffold
description:
# Model-gated test harness (P0-test-harness)

## BACKGROUND / WHY
The conformance ladder is the heart of this project, but CI must stay green **without** the 6.67 GB weights. The mandated pattern (AGENTS.md Testing Policy, plan §8.3): **model-gated e2e** — skip-with-SUCCESS when the model is absent, AND prove the native path actually ran (point any fallback at `/nonexistent`). Plus the `many_pages_without_deadlock` concurrency watchdog (pages ≫ pool) that hangs on regression — the durable architectural check that the deadlock saga must not recur. Phase 0 stands up this harness so every later phase plugs tests into it.

## CURRENT STATE
No `tests/` harness files exist yet beyond what P0-robot-skeleton adds. The plan names `tests/conformance_harness.rs`, `tests/native_engine_e2e.rs` (model-gated), `tests/robot_contract.rs`, `tests/fixtures/`. This bead creates the harness shell + the gating + the watchdog scaffold (real e2e bodies are Phase 1+).

## WHAT TO DO (verified facts transcribed)
1. **Model-gating helper** (shared test util): `fn model_gate() -> Option<PathBuf>` calls `native_model_available(resolve_model(...))`; if absent, the test logs a structured `{test, gated:true, reason:"model absent"}` line and returns `Ok(())` (skip-with-SUCCESS — CI green). Use this in `tests/native_engine_e2e.rs`.
2. **Prove-the-native-path-ran**: when running the native path, point ALL fallbacks at `/nonexistent` (env), so if the engine silently fell back it would error — proving the real path executed. Encode this as a harness convention.
3. **`many_pages_without_deadlock` watchdog** (`tests/conformance_harness.rs` or a dedicated `tests/concurrency_watchdog.rs`): a test that drives the engine over **pages ≫ pool** (e.g. dozens of empty/placeholder pages through the sequential outer loop) under a CI timeout; on a nested-rayon-under-lock / nested-runtime regression it **hangs** (CI timeout = failure). Phase 0 uses the empty Phase-0 pipeline so the watchdog is real and passes now, and stays a tripwire as the forward lands.
4. **Structured logging mandate**: every test emits JSON-line logs (`{test, phase, stage, elapsed_ms, gated, outcome}`) — the project mandates comprehensive tests with great logging (AGENTS.md). Wire a tiny test-only logger (tracing-subscriber json or hand-rolled) so logs are machine-parseable.
4b. **Benches skip gracefully**: `benches/` (criterion: vision_encode, decode_token, end_to_end, gauntlet) exit 0 when the model fixture is absent (plan §9.6) — Phase 0 stands up the empty bench shells with the skip-guard.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Skip-with-SUCCESS, never skip-silently-fail** — CI without weights is green; a present-model CI runs the real e2e. The gate is explicit and logged.
- **Prove the native path ran** (fallbacks→`/nonexistent`) — guards against a green test that secretly took a stub path.
- **The deadlock watchdog is architectural, not a per-kernel patch** (doctrine #5) — single model + sequential outer loop, forward fans out internally; the watchdog catches any regression to nested-rayon-under-lock.
- **Great logging** — structured JSON lines so failures are diagnosable and the gauntlet can ingest them.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- The watchdog must have a real CI timeout (so a hang = fail, not an infinite CI job).
- Don't let the gate hide a real failure: a present model that errors must FAIL, only an ABSENT model skips.
- Keep test fixtures tiny (header bytes, not the 6.67 GB blob) so the repo stays light; the real golden corpus + per-layer reference fixtures come from E-PM1 / Phase 1.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- With no model present, `cargo test` is green and the gated tests log `gated:true`.
- With a model present (or a fixture), the gated path runs and fallbacks point at `/nonexistent` (proving the native path).
- `many_pages_without_deadlock` passes on the current sequential frame and would hang on a nested-rayon/nested-runtime regression (verified by construction; documented).
- All tests emit parseable JSON-line logs.
- `cargo bench` (or `--no-run`) skips gracefully without the model.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- `model_gate_skips_green_when_absent` (the gate itself).

title: conformance.rs seed: L0–L5 tolerance structs, parity/invariant validator traits, rollout stages
description:
# conformance.rs seed (P0-conformance-seed)

## BACKGROUND / WHY
Parity gate FIRST, perf second (G1>G2, doctrine #1). The conformance machinery (the L0–L5 ladder, tolerance structs, parity/invariant validators) is the spine of correctness. Phase 0 seeds the types so Phase 1 plugs real validators in. The tolerances themselves must be DERIVED from the oracle's own nondeterminism floor (E-PM1 / plan §8.2), never hand-guessed or inherited.

## CURRENT STATE
`conformance.rs` exists as a skeleton (P0-crate-layout). No tolerance structs or validators yet.

## WHAT TO DO (verified facts transcribed — the L0–L5 ladder, plan §8.2)
1. **Tolerance structs** for the parity ladder:
   - **L0 preprocessing** — exact (gray pad 127,127,127; ratio selection; `[-1,1]` normalize via `(x-0.5)/0.5` after `[0,1]`; tile geometry).
   - **L1 per-op** — cosine ≈ 1.0 (≥ 0.9999 f32; documented int8 tolerance).
   - **L2 per-layer** — cosine ≈ 1.0; max-abs-diff ledgered.
   - **L3 logits** — within int8/int4 quant tolerance; **argmax must match** where reference deterministic. (Tolerance is MEASURED from the oracle variance, NOT the inherited frankensearch `0.055` — that is a BERT-reranker figure on a different shape/depth.)
   - **L4 token** — decoded token sequence EXACT under greedy where reference deterministic.
   - **L5 end-to-end OCR** — exact-match where deterministic; aggregate CER / TEDS / Formula-CDM within a documented budget.
   Represent these as a `Tolerances` struct with per-gate fields (`cosine_min`, `max_abs_diff`, `logit_tol`, `argmax_must_match`, `cer_budget`, ...) and a `default_tolerances()` seed (placeholder numbers clearly marked TODO-derive-from-oracle, gated on E-PM1).
2. **Validator traits**: a `ParityGate` trait (`name`, `level: L0..L5`, `validate(subject, oracle) -> GateResult`) and an `Invariant` trait (e.g. KV-cache-never-exceeds-`L·(m+128)`, int8-i32-accumulator-never-overflows, same-input-determinism, SIMD==scalar bit-identical). Phase 0 declares them with no-op/placeholder impls.
3. **Rollout stages** enum (the staged-quantization gates referenced in plan §10 Phase 2: 2a FFN-only, 2b attention int8, 2c lm_head int8) so later phases attach a parity receipt per stage.
4. **Determinism gate** type: same-input-twice → identical output (asserted Phase 1+; the type exists now).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Tolerances DERIVED from the oracle's nondeterminism floor** (plan §8.2): the HF reference is non-deterministic across torch thread counts / BLAS reduction order at the logit-tie level (bf16, 129280-vocab argmax). So L4 'exact' is defined only over the prefix the oracle reproduces identically, and L3 logit tolerance comes from the measured oracle variance. Phase 0 leaves these as TODO-from-E-PM1 placeholders, NOT hard numbers.
- **Discrete output bit-exact, continuous values within tolerance** (the frankensearch `parity_logits_and_ranking_match_reference` shape): decoded text bit-exact where deterministic; logits only within a documented quant tolerance; a separate determinism gate.
- **Invariants as e-processes later** (gauntlet §8.5): the KV/overflow/determinism/SIMD invariants become anytime-valid e-processes; Phase 0 just declares the trait.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Do NOT bake the inherited `0.055` as a default — mark it clearly as a placeholder requiring E-PM1's measured floor.
- Multi-page metamorphic property is subtle (R-SWA cross-page dependence, OQ-13): do NOT assert 'multi-page = sum of single-page parses'. Phase 0 leaves the multi-page invariant unspecified pending OQ-13.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `Tolerances` struct + `default_tolerances()` compile; placeholder numbers are clearly TODO-marked with a pointer to E-PM1/§8.2.
- `ParityGate` + `Invariant` traits compile with placeholder impls; the L0–L5 levels are enumerated.
- A unit test constructs the tolerance struct and asserts the level enum spans L0–L5.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit: `tolerances_default_constructs`; `parity_levels_span_L0_to_L5`; `invariant_trait_object_dispatches`.
- Structured logging in tests.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
`depends_on P0-crate-layout` (conformance.rs). Soft dep on E-PM1 for the real tolerance numbers (oracle nondeterminism floor + measured int8 budget) — Phase 0 uses TODO placeholders, Phase 1 fills them. Consumed by E-VERIFY and all Phase-1 parity beads.

title: focrq format doc still describes unsupported partial QInt4 groups
description: docs/focrq-format.md says QInt4 scale count uses ceil(shape[1] / group_size) and describes zero-padded final partial groups, but the reader and quantizer require group_size to divide k exactly. That doc drift can mislead converter/kernel work into emitting artifacts the committed reader rejects. Align the format doc with the implemented exact-division contract: group_size must divide k, scale count is n * (k / group_size), and there is no partial-group padding in v1.
close_reason: Aligned docs/focrq-format.md QInt4PerGroup rules with implemented reader/writer/quantizer contract: group_size must be 16 or 32, k must be an exact multiple of group_size, scale count is n*(k/group_size), and v1 has no partial-group padding. Verified with scripts/check_focrq_format.py, git diff --check, and rg for stale ceil/partial-padding wording.

title: Perf: fused [3*1280,1280] qkv GEMV for decode (fewer dispatches, keep block-parallelism)

title: Demonstrated int4 footprint arithmetic: per-section byte accounting in the converter
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
Plan §12 is explicit: the int4 footprint target (≈1.8-2.9 GB) is a **demonstrated** number, not an assumed one — 'the converter prints the realized per-section footprint'. And the arithmetic is non-trivial: the high-precision set kept BF16 dominates (vision tower ≈ 774 MiB; `embed_tokens` 129280x1280 ≈ 330 MB bf16; untied `lm_head` ≈ 330 MB bf16 unless int8'd; projector/router/norms small). NVFP4 keeping embeddings+lm_head+vision in BF16 already lands at 2.93 GB, so **hitting <2.9 GB with int4 experts may require int8 lm_head and possibly embeddings** — choices OUTSIDE the validated recipe, gated by CER + kill-switch + DISCREPANCIES. This bead makes the footprint real and the gap visible.

## WHAT TO DO
- Make `focr convert` print (and emit as NDJSON / `.focrq` header metadata) the **realized per-section footprint**: vision tower bytes, embed_tokens bytes, lm_head bytes, router/norms bytes, int4 expert bytes, int8 (v_proj/down_proj/dense-down) bytes, scales bytes, total.
- **Demonstrate the arithmetic** for each candidate config: pure-int4-experts + all-BF16-high-precision (expect ~2.9 GB, near NVFP4); +int8 lm_head (saves ~165 MB); +int8 embeddings (saves ~165 MB, out-of-recipe). Show which combination closes <2.9 GB and at what CER cost (cross-ref P4-tail-risk-gate).
- **bf16→f16 saves NOTHING** (both 2 bytes) — state this so nobody 'optimizes' it; any f16 narrowing is a lossy DISCREPANCIES entry, never a default.
- Cross-check: realized total vs the AF-1 budget B passed to `--optimize-bits` (the allocator's budget must match the realized footprint).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Demonstrated, not assumed** (§12) — the whole point is honest footprint accounting, since the BF16 high-precision set dominates and the naive 'int4 = small' intuition is wrong here.
- **int8 lm_head / embeddings are out-of-recipe levers** — gated by CER, kill-switch, DISCREPANCIES; the footprint print makes their byte-savings vs CER-cost trade explicit.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- The int4 footprint includes the **per-group scales** (g=16 → one f32 per 16 weights ≈ +0.25 byte/weight ≈ +2 bits/weight) — so int4-g16 is ~4.25 bpw + the int8 minority + bf16 bulk. Account scales explicitly; they are why Q4_K_M is ~4.5-4.9 bpw not 4.0.
- Don't claim <2.9 GB unless the arithmetic closes AND the CER gate passes for whatever out-of-recipe choices it required.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The converter prints a per-section byte table + total for any `--quant int4 [--optimize-bits]` run.
- The arithmetic for each candidate config is demonstrated (committed in PERF_LEDGER/docs), showing the path to ≤2.9 GB and its CER cost.
- Scales bytes accounted; bf16-vs-f16 no-op stated; realized total cross-checked vs AF-1 budget.

## TESTS REQUIRED
Unit: the per-section byte accounting sums to the actual `.focrq` payload size; scales bytes match group_size; the int8-lm_head/embeddings savings match expectation. Integration (model-gated): real-weights footprint print matches the on-disk `.focrq` size byte-for-byte. NDJSON logging of the byte table.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
- `P4-convert-int4`: needs the int4 records whose bytes it accounts.
- `P4-af1-bit-allocator`: the realized footprint must reconcile with AF-1's budget B.

title: Tests: AF-1 water-filling frontier, proof obligation, deterministic fallback
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
AF-1 is an adaptive controller; per the Alien-Artifact Engineering Contract it cannot ship without proving its deterministic fallback and its proof obligation. This bead is that proof harness.

## WHAT TO DO
- **Frontier correctness (unit, synthetic D_t(b)):** for hand-constructed distortion curves, assert the λ-sweep traces a monotone (bits↑ ⇒ distortion↓) frontier and that at each λ the per-tensor choice minimizes `D_t(b)+λ·bits_t(b)`; assert the chosen λ exactly meets the budget B.
- **Water-filling order:** assert bits go to the steepest `∂D/∂bits` tensors first (e.g. dense down_proj, v_proj appear before flat expert gate/up).
- **Proof obligation (model-gated):** allocated-config CER ≤ uniform-config CER at equal footprint on the dense-numeric corpus; if not, assert the deterministic fallback engages and a NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE entry is written.
- **Fallback:** with `--optimize-bits` absent → uniform Q4_K_M-class allocation; with a forced proof failure → fallback engages.
- **AF-2 coupling:** assert the allocated config's CVaR_0.1 is within budget (no mean-improving, tail-worsening solution accepted).
- **Structured logging:** NDJSON of the chosen table, per-tensor marginal-D-per-bit, realized footprint, allocated vs uniform CER + CVaR.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
Frontier monotone + budget-exact; water-filling order correct; proof obligation met or fallback engaged+ledgered; tail bound respected.

## TESTS REQUIRED
This IS the test bead (unit synthetic + model-gated integration).

title: Model-gated e2e test runner — skip-with-SUCCESS without the 6.67GB weights, PROVE the native path ran when present
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The Unlimited-OCR checkpoint is a **single 6.67 GB bf16 shard** (`model-00001-of-000001.safetensors`, total_size=6,672,212,480 bytes, 2710 tensors) that CANNOT live in CI. But e2e tests must exist and must be meaningful when a developer DOES have the weights. The AGENTS.md Testing Policy is explicit: "**model-gated e2e** (skip-with-SUCCESS without the 6.67 GB weights; prove the native path ran by pointing fallbacks at `/nonexistent`)." This bead builds the shared runner that enforces exactly that contract, so CI stays green without weights yet a broken native path fails LOUDLY when weights are present.

## WHAT TO DO
Build `tests/common/model_gate.rs`:
1. **Gate check**: `native_model_available()` does a cheap header sniff (magic bytes / `.focrq` `FOCRQ\0` magic or the safetensors header) at the resolved model path (via `resolve_model(spec)` over `$FOCR_MODEL_DIR`, `~/.cache/franken_ocr/models`, …). No tensor load.
2. **Skip-with-SUCCESS when absent**: if no model, the test returns Ok and logs an NDJSON line `{event:"skip", result:"skip_no_model", searched_dirs:[...]}` — CI is green, but the skip is VISIBLE in logs and never silently passes a missing assertion.
3. **PROVE the native path ran when present** (the critical guard): before running, point EVERY fallback/alternate code path at `/nonexistent` (e.g. `FOCR_QUANT` selection, any reference-cmd fallback) so that if the test accidentally exercised a fallback instead of the real native engine, it errors. Then assert the structured log carries `native_path_ran=true` and a native-engine sentinel (e.g. the dispatched `simd_tier` was set, the `.focrq` header was actually parsed, the real decode loop emitted per-stage lines). A test that 'passes' without ever entering `native_engine/` is a FAILURE.
4. **`run_e2e(image, args) -> E2eRun`** helper that invokes the real `focr` binary (or the library `OcrEngine::recognize`), captures stdout NDJSON/JSON + the structured test log, and returns parsed output + the proof flags.
5. **Determinism hook**: under `temperature=0` greedy, run twice and assert byte-identical (delegates to TEST-determinism-gate).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **`/nonexistent` fallback trick** (from AGENTS.md): the only robust way to prove the NATIVE path ran is to make every non-native path explode. This catches the insidious case where weights exist but the test silently degrades to a stub/fallback and reports a false green.
- **Header sniff, not tensor load**, for the gate (cheap, no 6.67 GB read just to decide to skip).
- **Visible skip** (logged with searched dirs) so a developer who EXPECTED the model to be found sees why it wasn't (actionable error listing every searched dir, per §7.5).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- The gate must distinguish "model absent" (skip-green) from "model present but corrupt/wrong-version" (FAIL with exit-code 3/7 mapping, §7.4) — a corrupt model is a real failure, not a skip.
- Don't let `FOCR_FORCE_ARCH` or `FOCR_QUANT` overrides from the dev's shell leak into the proof (the runner sets a clean, explicit env).
- The native-path sentinel must be something only the real engine sets (a stub could fake a flag) — prefer asserting real side-effects (parsed `.focrq` header values matching the manifest census, real per-decoder-layer stage logs, the OQ-18 token count of 273 at base 1024).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Without weights: every model-gated test returns Ok and logs `skip_no_model` with searched dirs; CI green.
- With weights present: tests run, assert `native_path_ran=true`, and FAIL if a fallback was exercised (proven by an injected fault that breaks the native path → test goes red, does not silently skip).
- A corrupt/wrong-version model FAILS with the §7.4 exit-code mapping, never skips.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Self-test: with weights absent → skip_no_model, green.
- Self-test (fault injection): with weights present but native engine forced to error → test goes RED (proves it did not silently skip).
- Self-test: a corrupt `.focrq` (bad magic / format_version too high) → exit-code 7, FAIL.
- See **TEST-e2e-cli-script** for the full end-to-end golden comparison built on this runner.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
- depends_on **E-P0**: needs `resolve_model`, `native_model_available()`, `.focrq` header sniff, and exit-code mapping from the scaffold.
- depends_on **TEST-log-emitter**: emits the `native_path_ran` / `skip_no_model` proof lines through it.

Packaging delta: inlined per test file vs a shared tests/common module — the repo convention.

title: Harden decoder helpers against malformed Mat backing lengths
description:
## Background / why
Fresh-eyes audit after `bd-14ve` found the same public-field invariant gap in decoder helpers. `Mat` fields are public, so callers can construct a shape whose `data.len()` does not equal `rows * cols`. `decoder::apply_rope`, `decoder::add_residual`, and `decoder::prefill_attention` validate logical shapes but then borrow rows or rebuild a `Mat`, which can panic on malformed backing data.

## Scope
- Add a local checked `rows * cols` / backing-length validator in `src/native_engine/decoder.rs`.
- Apply it before row access or elementwise zip in public decoder helpers that consume `Mat`, especially RoPE, residual add, QKV/attention helper paths.
- Add focused regressions proving malformed `Mat` inputs return clean `FocrError`s instead of panicking.

## Acceptance
- Malformed decoder `Mat` inputs produce actionable `FocrError::Other` messages.
- Existing valid-shape decoder tests remain green.
- Focused decoder tests, full cargo gates, and UBS pass.
close_reason: Fixed: decoder helpers now validate Mat backing lengths before RoPE row mutation, linear projection, residual add, prefill attention transposes, and top-level forward. Added malformed-input regressions for apply_rope, linear_no_bias, add_residual, and prefill_attention. Verified cargo +nightly fmt --check; focused cargo +nightly test native_engine::decoder --lib; cargo +nightly check --all-targets; cargo +nightly clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo +nightly test; ubs --only=rust src/native_engine/decoder.rs (exit 0, no critical findings).

title: GOT decode perf campaign: int8+topK-refine lm_head (SDOT/VNNI) + parallel per-head attention + seed last-row = got-forward 35.9s to 16.6s, byte-identical, oracle-validated
description:
User: "squeeze out absolutely each and every optimization! and don't forget specialized optimizations to supercharge perf on apple silicon and intel/amd processors specifically!"

Follow-on to bd-3bom (lm_head pretranspose 487->41s). The remaining 35.9s got-forward for page_0107 broke down (FOCR_TIMING) as: vision 5.8s, seed 1.16s, decoder layers 30s [attn 4.9s, gemv 7.6s], lm_head 16.2s. Attacked the three biggest doctrine-compliant levers; a kernel-map subagent confirmed the decode int8 GEMV (franken_ocr src/simd) already dispatches the FULL per-arch ISA ladder (SDOT on Apple Silicon; AVX-512-VNNI / AVX-VNNI / AVX2 on Intel-AMD), register-blocked + N-parallel + bandwidth-bound at m=1 — so the wins come from moving work ONTO it, not writing new kernels. (bf16/BFMMLA does NOT exist in the stack, so a bf16 vision lever was correctly ruled out.)

LEVERS (each env-gated so ONE build measured every config; the gate on the numerics lever IS its doctrine-#2 kill-switch):
1. int8 lm_head + top-K f32 refine (FOCR_GOT_INT8_LMHEAD, DEFAULT ON). The lm_head reads the ~0.6 GB f32 tied head per token (memory-bound). Quantize it to per-output-channel int8 (SDOT/VNNI GEMV, ~0.15 GB) then recompute the top-256 candidates in exact f32 (normed·embed_row) so the greedy argmax matches the f32 head. NEAR-LOSSLESS: byte-identical output on page_0107 (688/688 tokens), and the env-gated oracle certs RAN and PASSED on this default (kvcache_greedy_matches_oracle_l4 == oracle L4 [9707,38,1793,12,93495,17,13,15], decoder_matches_torch_oracle, recognize_reads_the_sample_image_e2e golden). lm_head 16.9s -> 1.94s (8.7x). Kill-switch: FOCR_GOT_INT8_LMHEAD=0 -> provably-bit-identical f32 head.
2. Parallel per-head decode attention (FOCR_GOT_SEQ_ATTN to disable, DEFAULT parallel). Each of the 16 heads is a self-contained softmax over disjoint output lanes -> rayon fan-out is BIT-IDENTICAL. attn 5.02s -> 2.43s (2.1x); OUTPUT byte-identical.
3. Seed last-row-only lm_head. forward_prefill_seed projected the full [N,vocab] head then sliced the last row; now projects only the last row through the shared got_lm_head. seed 1.16s -> 0.27s; bit-identical.

RESULT (page_0107, Apple M4, got-ocr2.int8.focrq): got-forward 35.93s -> 16.6s (2.16x THIS turn), decode 30.07s -> 10.6s, 23 -> 64.7 tok/s. Byte-identical + oracle-validated. Cumulative from the 8-min start: got-forward 482.85s -> 16.6s (29x); decode 1.4 -> 64.7 tok/s (46x).

Gates: fmt/clippy clean, 745 lib tests + all 4 env-gated GOT oracle certs pass on the int8+refine default; ubs 0-critical on the diff. Evidence: artifacts/perf/<this-bead>/.

FOLLOW-UP (separate beads, from the kernel map): (a) GOT prefill + qkv GEMM still route through nn::linear_int8_dynamic (ft-kernel-cpu) which is SCALAR int8 on x86 below AVX-512-VNNI (e.g. AVX2 Threadripper) and has no SMMLA — routing them through franken_ocr's own simd ISA ladder would fix x86 prefill; (b) per-step Mat/Vec allocations in the decode loop (~gemv+misc 6.9s) could be buffer-reused.
close_reason: Shipped in the perf(decode) commit: int8+topK-refine lm_head (default, SDOT/VNNI, 8.3x), parallel per-head attn (2.1x), last-row seed. got-forward 35.9→16.6s (2.16x), byte-identical + all 4 GOT oracle certs pass on the int8 default; 745 tests green.

title: int4 GEMM/GEMV kernels: in-register int4→int8 unpack → same SMMLA/VNNI/SDOT MAC
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
This is the heart of Phase 4 and the biggest decode lever (§6.3, §9.4 lever #3). There is **NO CPU int4 matmul instruction**, so int4 weights are **unpacked to int8 in-register and fed to the SAME SMMLA / VNNI / SDOT MAC** built in Phase 3 (§6.6). The win is **bandwidth + footprint** — half the weight bytes streamed per decode token vs int8 — NOT extra compute. Applied to the expert FFN bulk (the dominant decode cost) this is up to ~2x decode throughput.

## WHAT TO DO
Add an int4-weight path to the `int8_gemm` / `int8_gemv` entrypoint (plan §6.6) so a `QInt4PerGroup` weight tensor runs through the existing Phase-3 micro-kernels after an in-register unpack:
- **Unpack:** load the packed int4 nibbles (two per byte) for the current K-panel tile, sign-extend each nibble to int8 in-register, apply the per-group scale at dequant time (scales applied **post-accumulation**, like int8: `dequant = i32_acc · scale_w_group · scale_a_row`). The unpack must NOT spill to memory — unpack a register tile, MAC it, discard.
- **Reuse the Phase-3 MAC verbatim** per arch (§6.6 catalog): ARM A1 SMMLA `vmmlaq_s32` (prefill, register-blocked, compute:load ≥ 2:1) + A2/decode SDOT `vdotq_s32`; x86 X1 VPDPBUSD `_mm512_dpbusd_epi32` (U8S8, +128 fold), X2 AVX-VNNI, X3 AMX `_tile_dpbssd` (prefill), X4 AVX2 `_mm256_maddubs_epi16`→`_mm256_madd_epi16` (carries its own i16-saturation overflow proof, §5.4), S scalar floor.
- **Per-group scale application:** because int4 is per-GROUP (g=16-32) not per-output-channel, the accumulator must be partitioned by group along K, or the scale folded per-group-block. Design the K-tiling so a group boundary aligns with a tile boundary (g divides the tile K-block of 64-256, §6.6) — then accumulate each group's i32 partial, scale it, and sum the scaled partials. Document the exact accumulation order (it is bit-identical across SIMD vs scalar because integer add is exact within a group; the per-group f32 scale sum order must be fixed and identical scalar-vs-SIMD).
- **Expert decode pre-packing:** experts pre-packed cache-contiguous per `(layer, expert)` so the 8 active experts (6 routed + 2 shared) load as contiguous int4 blocks; software-prefetch the next expert's weights while computing the current (§6.7 decode regime).
- **Tier mixing:** a decoder layer has int4 (gate/up) + int8 (down/v_proj) tensors side by side — the kernel dispatches per-tensor on its `.focrq` dtype/tier, not per-layer.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Unpack-to-int8-in-register, not a separate dequant pass.** A memory round-trip to materialize int8 would erase the bandwidth win (the whole point). The unpack lives inside the micro-kernel's load.
- **Reuse Phase-3 MAC, don't write a new one.** NE-INH-5: never trade a good kernel for a naive one. The int8 MAC is already bit-exact and at-peak; int4 only changes the load/unpack front-end.
- **Register/cache blocking is MANDATORY (NE-INH-3).** An un-blocked SMMLA was SLOWER than SDOT (load-bound, 2 loads:1 SMMLA). int4 halves the weight load, which *helps* the compute:load ratio — but the kernel must already be register-blocked with offline-pre-packed weights, or the win evaporates.
- **Per-group scale partition** keeps int4 group-quant exact relative to its own dequant reference; the scalar fallback computes the identical grouped sum so SIMD==scalar bit-identical on the i32 part.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- **i32 overflow proof obligation (§5.4) STILL applies, recomputed for int4-unpacked-to-int8.** Worst-case |acc| per group is `g · 127²` (S8S8) or `g · 255·127` (U8S8) — tiny for g≤32, but the cross-group SUM and any fused/accumulating path must be proven not to overflow. The dense layer-0 down_proj (K=6848) stays int8, so int4 never hits the K=6848 worst case — but assert this in a test, do not assume.
- **Packing/unpack must agree byte-for-byte with P4-convert-int4 per arch.** A nibble-order mismatch (hi/lo nibble) is silent garbage. Pin the convention and test it.
- **AVX2 path saturates at i16** before the i32 widen (§6.6 ⚠) — not automatically bit-identical for adversarial operands; carry the split-accumulate-every-2-K-steps proof or a DISCREPANCIES entry.
- **Apple AMX is NOT directly programmable** (NE-INH-4): the Mac int4-unpack path feeds NEON SMMLA/SDOT, no FFI. AMX is x86 (Accelerate is opt-in FFI only).
- **`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` islands:** the unpack intrinsics live in the named SIMD module behind `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` with a `// SAFETY:` per load and a bit-identical scalar fallback that cross-compiles to every target.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- int4-weight GEMM/GEMV produces results **bit-identical** to the scalar reference (which unpacks int4→int8 then does the exact grouped i32 MAC) on every arch — integer accumulation is exact; only the f32 group-scale sum needs a fixed order, also identical scalar-vs-SIMD.
- int4 vs int8 forward divergence (the genuine quant drift) is **measured for this model** and ledgered, NOT inherited.
- decode-per-token streams ≤ ~half the int8 weight bytes on the int4-tensor portion (verified by a bytes-streamed counter / roofline check, §9.1).
- i32 overflow proof: a unit test at the worst-case group operands on every arch asserts the i32 result equals an i64 reference and no path silently saturates.
- runtime feature dispatch selects the right tier; `focr robot backends` reflects it; `FOCR_FORCE_ARCH` overrides for testing.

## TESTS REQUIRED
Unit: per-arch int4-unpack correctness (nibble order, sign extension); grouped i32 MAC bit-identical to scalar; per-group scale application order; worst-case overflow at g=32. Bench: decode GEMV int4 vs int8 (bytes streamed + ms) on the expert-MLP shape (1280↔896). See `P4-int4-gemm-tests` (parity+bit-identical) and `P4-int4-gemm-bench`.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
- `E-P3`: reuses the Phase-3 SMMLA/AMX/VNNI/SDOT micro-kernels and per-arch packing — int4 is a load/unpack front-end on them.
- `P4-convert-int4`: needs the int4 `.focrq` records + packing convention to read.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## REVIEW-2 ADDENDUM — prefill MoE grouped-GEMM at int4, loader handoff, manual tier override
- **int4 in the prefill MoE grouped-GEMM (§6.7).** Phase-3 token-grouping turns 64 scattered expert GEMVs into ≤64 dense SMMLA/AMX GEMMs over per-expert token-blocks. When those expert weights are int4, the SAME in-register unpack-to-int8 front-end applies INSIDE the grouped GEMM (prefill is compute-bound, but the experts are still int4 on disk, so the weight stream is still halved). Assert the grouped-GEMM path dispatches per-tensor on the `.focrq` tier exactly like the decode GEMV, and that an int4 expert in a grouped GEMM is bit-identical to the same expert run as int4 GEMVs (grouping must not change the integer arithmetic).
- **Loader handoff (P4-r2-int4-loader).** This kernel reads borrowed slices (packed nibble payload, per-group scales, group_size, tier) from `native_engine/weights.rs`; it must NOT assume any int4 record was materialized to int8 on load — the unpack lives in the micro-kernel load, never a separate pass. The packing convention is the triangle convert(write)↔loader(read)↔kernel(unpack); all three must agree byte-for-byte (nibble hi/lo order) and a parity test exercises the round trip.
- **Manual per-tensor tier override (debug kill-switch).** Add `FOCR_FORCE_TIER=<tensor_glob>:<tier>` (or equivalent) so the AF-2 tier-up fallback (bump an offending tensor to int8) can be exercised/verified at runtime without re-converting, and so a regression can be bisected to one tensor's tier. Default unset = use the `.focrq` tiers verbatim. Document in DISCREPANCIES if it changes output.

title: Tests for the golden-fixture harness (hash-verify, canonicalization, provenance completeness) with structured logging
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The fixture harness is the trust root for the entire conformance ladder; if its hash-verify or canonicalization is subtly wrong, every downstream parity gate is unsound. This bead is the comprehensive test suite proving the harness behaves, emitting the structured NDJSON test-log lines the project mandates.

## WHAT TO DO
Write `tests/fixture_harness.rs` covering:
1. **Hash verification**: a fixture loaded clean passes; a fixture with one mutated byte is REJECTED with a clear error naming the file + expected/actual SHA-256.
2. **Canonicalization correctness**: feed JSON with `timing`, `run_id`, `duration_ms` fields + CRLF line endings + absolute paths → assert all scrubbed/normalized; assert idempotence (canonicalize(canonicalize(x)) == canonicalize(x)).
3. **Provenance completeness**: a `PROVENANCE.md` missing any required field (transformers/torch/Pillow versions, HF+GitHub commit, gen script git ref, exact command, per-fixture SHA-256) fails `provenance_complete()`.
4. **Loader against real golden corpus** (model-gated): if the golden corpus is present, load each `<doc>_reference.json` and each `<stage>.npy` and assert shapes match the OQ-18 census (e.g. logits last-dim == 129280; post-connector token count == 273 at 1024 base mode). Skip-with-SUCCESS if corpus absent.
5. **Structured logging**: every test emits NDJSON lines via the `TestLog` emitter (bead TEST-log-emitter): `{test, case, fixture, sha256, shapes, canonicalized_fields, result, elapsed_us}`.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Mutation tests (flip a byte) are the only way to prove hash-verify actually guards.
- Idempotence is the canonicalization correctness invariant.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Don't hardcode the golden corpus presence — gate it; CI without weights must still run the non-gated cases.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- All five test groups pass; mutation test proves rejection; idempotence holds; provenance-completeness rejects an incomplete file.
- Every test emits a valid NDJSON test-log line (validated by the log-schema validator from TEST-log-conventions).

## TESTS REQUIRED
- This bead IS the tests; it must itself emit structured logs and pass the log-schema validator.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
- depends_on **TEST-fixture-harness** (the thing under test).
- depends_on **TEST-log-emitter** (uses the structured-logging emitter).

title: macOS 26: close public-installer provenance sandbox execution failure
description:
The v0.7.2 public installer downloaded and checksum-verified the Apple Silicon release asset, but macOS 26.5 killed the newly staged Mach-O before main. Kernel logs reported "AppleSystemPolicy ASP: Unable to apply provenance sandbox: 268451845". The public asset SHA256 2fa4827c866d159d247ea61532e9e40b1e3d14f8aca14a8b7a8c23fd0e61fa8c matches the DSR manifest and the exact original DSR build output. Newly copied /bin/echo reproduced the same failure, so the current evidence points to a host provenance-policy defect or interaction rather than defective focr bytes; that classification is not yet conclusive.

Determine the root cause without weakening Gatekeeper or stripping security metadata. Reproduce on a clean macOS 26 host and a control macOS host; capture codesign, spctl, xattr, provenance, and kernel-log evidence. If release signing or notarization is required, sign/notarize before checksum generation and bind the signing identity and receipts into the release evidence.
