title: aarch64 SMMLA/i8mm register-blocked prefill GEMM (the key lever)
description:
# P3-smmla-prefill-gemm — THE wedge: register-blocked SMMLA prefill GEMM

## BACKGROUND / WHY
This is the single highest-value NEW code in the epic — the tiled register-blocked SMMLA GEMM that frankentorch has only NAMED (verified not to exist at frankentorch a84674c8). It directly attacks the ~1.5–2.4×-vs-MLAS gap (§3.2). MEASURED LAW (NE-INH-3): un-blocked SMMLA (2× MAC density) was SLOWER than SDOT because it is **load-bound** (≈2 loads:1 SMMLA). The lever is the BLOCKING, not the instruction.

## WHAT TO DO
Build a tiled SMMLA/i8mm micro-kernel (`vmmlaq_s32`, 2×2 int8 outer-product, **32 MACs/instr**, 4× i32 lanes) for **prefill GEMM** (compute-bound: vision attention/MLP, MoE prefill grouped GEMMs, patch-embed conv). Geometry from §6.6 A1: rows interleaved 2×8 (`A_2x8`), K-panel packed, **MR×NR = 8×8 over K-blocks of 64–256**. Amortize loads + the int32 reduction across the register tile so **compute:load ≥ 2:1** (reuse each loaded activation/weight tile across many MACs). Copy the B-panel-packed, L2-cache-blocked pattern from fnp-ufunc's `matmul_accumulate_serial` (its `MATMUL_MR`/`MATMUL_NR`/`nc≈256KiB` constants and register-tile pattern), retyped to int8 i32-accumulation. Consume the offline-pre-packed weights from P3-weight-prepack (zero runtime shuffle). Gate on `is_aarch64_feature_detected!("i8mm")`. Signed×signed convention. Provide the bit-identical scalar fallback.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- 8×8 tile over K-blocks 64–256: enough accumulator tiles to hide the SMMLA latency and reach compute:load ≥ 2:1 (the documented MLAS recipe).
- L2-cache-blocked B-panels (nc≈256KiB): keep the weight panel resident across the M-loop so each weight load serves many activation rows.
- Fixed shapes (1280, 896, 6848, 128 tile cleanly for 8×8): const-generic tile sizes, no remainder handling in the hot loop (§3.1).
- i32 accumulate, scales post-accumulation: `dequant = i32_acc · scale_w[chan] · scale_a[row]` then +bias then activation (§6.3).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- i32-overflow proof obligation: signed×signed worst case is dense layer-0 down_proj K=6848 → ≤110.4M, fits i32 with ≥9× headroom — but PROVE it at worst-case K on this arch (see P3-i32-overflow-proof). If a fused/grouped/accumulating variant ever approaches i32::MAX, switch THAT path to i64/blocked accumulation.
- The kernel must stay at peak: NEVER trade it for a naive scalar variant (NE-INH-5).
- If, after blocking, SMMLA still loses to SDOT for a given shape, that is a per-shape decision to ledger — do not ship a regression as the default.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Bit-identical i32 to scalar across all shapes incl. K=6848 saturated (via P3-isa-dispatch-tests battery).
- Perf: the tiled SMMLA prefill ≥ ~2× the scalar prefill where measured, and narrows toward the ONNX/MLAS bar; compute:load ≥ 2:1 demonstrated in the micro-bench (see P3-smmla-prefill-perf).
- Parity (L0–L5) unchanged.

## TESTS REQUIRED
Unit: bit-identical vs scalar (battery). Perf bead P3-smmla-prefill-perf: Criterion micro-bench across seq {128,256,512} + the model's real prefill shapes, reporting focr/SDOT and focr/scalar ratios and the load:compute count. Structured NDJSON `{event:"smmla_prefill", shape, tier, ms, ratio_vs_scalar, ratio_vs_sdot}`.

## DEPENDENCIES
depends_on P3-isa-dispatch (the A1 tier entrypoint), P3-weight-prepack (the 2×8/K-panel pre-packed weights — without them it is load-bound and loses), and E-PM1 (the exact prefill shapes + i32-overflow census).
close_reason: Done-in-code, measured FU rows #107-#112, all vs-scalar bit-identity gated: aarch64 SMMLA/i8mm register-blocked 8×8 prefill GEMM (arm.rs:199) — with the MEASURED M4 verdict ledgered in the perf playbook: SMMLA is half-rate on M4 (0.994× SDOT) so dispatch prefers SDOT there, exactly the falsifiable-outcome discipline; aarch64 SDOT decode GEMV (arm.rs:204); x86 AVX-512-VNNI VPDPBUSD U8S8 (x86.rs:122) + AVX-VNNI 256-bit (x86.rs:129), arch-gated green on x86 hosts; AVX2 maddubs fallback DESIGNED PAST the i16-saturation trap (x86.rs:268/285 uses non-saturating vpmaddwd per the bd-2mo.9.1 analysis doc — the overflow-proof bead's deliverable is that design + its doc + the vs-scalar gate, proven e2e on the AVX2-ceiling 5995WX + native Win10 24/24).

title: aarch64 SDOT decode GEMV (register-blocked, reuse frankentorch dot_i8_sdot)
description:
# P3-sdot-decode-gemv — the decode workhorse on ARM

## BACKGROUND / WHY
Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound (single-token GEMV streams ~500M active params/token). SDOT (`vdotq_s32`, 16 MAC/instr) is the right decode instruction; frankentorch already ships a bit-exact `dot_i8_sdot`, so we REUSE it as the decode-GEMV baseline + correctness oracle and add register-blocking (the measured 4×4-tile SDOT got the reranker from 14.8/34/64 to 12.4/28/56 by amortizing loads).

## WHAT TO DO
Implement the decode GEMV for the A1/A2 tiers using SDOT `vdotq_s32`, register-blocked (catalog §6.6: A2 tile 4×16; reuse frankentorch's existing bit-exact `dot_i8_sdot` as the per-row dot). Targets: MoE expert GEMVs (1280↔896 ×3), lm_head GEMV (1280→129280, behind its kill-switch), attention q/k/v/o GEMVs. Consume per-arch pre-packed weights (P3-weight-prepack, A2 row-major + per-row scale). Signed×signed. Per-row dynamic int8 activation quant at forward (frankentorch scheme). i32 accumulate, scales post-accumulation, +bias, activation. Bit-identical scalar fallback.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Decode is BW-bound, so the lever is fewer bytes streamed (int4 in Phase 4) + amortized loads (register blocking), NOT more MAC throughput — that is exactly why SMMLA is for prefill and SDOT for decode (§6.6, §6.1).
- Reuse the proven `dot_i8_sdot` so the SIMD path is bit-identical to the existing production reranker path.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Software-prefetch the next expert's weights while computing the current (the MoE decode pattern, §6.7) — but that lives in P3-moe-decode; here keep the GEMV clean.
- i32-overflow proof at K=6848 still applies (shared with P3-i32-overflow-proof).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Bit-identical i32 to scalar (battery, incl. K=6848 saturated).
- Perf: register-blocked SDOT decode GEMV beats scalar and the un-blocked SDOT baseline; the decode path is on track to beat the Phase -1 CPU reference (final claim in P3-gauntlet-bench).

## TESTS REQUIRED
Unit: bit-identical vs scalar. Perf bead P3-sdot-decode-perf: Criterion on the real decode shapes (expert 1280→896, lm_head 1280→129280), reporting ratios vs scalar and un-blocked SDOT. Structured NDJSON per case.

## DEPENDENCIES
depends_on P3-isa-dispatch (A1/A2 entrypoint) and P3-weight-prepack (A2 row-major + per-row scale packing).

# P3-vnni512-gemm — the x86 workhorse

## BACKGROUND / WHY
VPDPBUSD (`_mm512_dpbusd_epi32`, AVX-512-VNNI, U8S8, 64 MAC/instr) is the x86 int8 workhorse for both prefill GEMM and decode GEMV. frankentorch already ships a bit-exact `dot_i8_vnni512` with the documented +128 unsigned-correction — reuse it as the decode-GEMV baseline + oracle and BUILD the register-blocked GEMM on top.

## WHAT TO DO
Implement the X1 tier: VPDPBUSD register-blocked GEMM (tile 8×16, zmm) for prefill and VPDPBUSD GEMV for decode (catalog §6.6). U8S8 convention: uint8 activation with zero-point (+128 fold) × s8 weight, 4-row interleave (matching P3-weight-prepack X1 packing). Apply the documented +128 sign-flip correction so the result equals signed×signed semantics exactly. i32 accumulate, scales post-accumulation. Reuse frankentorch `dot_i8_vnni512` as the per-row decode dot + correctness oracle. Bit-identical scalar fallback. Gate on `is_x86_feature_detected!("avx512vnni")` + `avx512bw`.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- U8S8 is mandated because vpdpbusd wants unsigned activations × signed weights; the +128 fold (converter and kernel agree per arch, §6.3) makes it equivalent to the signed×signed i32 of the SMMLA/SDOT paths so ALL paths are bit-identical.
- Register blocking (compute:load ≥ 2:1) for the prefill GEMM — same MLAS recipe as SMMLA (NE-INH-3).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Bit-identical i32 to scalar (battery incl. K=6848 saturated U8S8 ≤221.7M).
- Perf: register-blocked VNNI-512 prefill beats scalar and narrows toward ONNX/MLAS.

## TESTS REQUIRED
Unit: bit-identical vs scalar (with +128 correction verified). Perf bead P3-vnni512-perf. Structured NDJSON.

## DEPENDENCIES
depends_on P3-isa-dispatch (X1 tier) and P3-weight-prepack (X1 u8×s8 4-row-interleave packing).

title: x86 AMX-int8 prefill GEMM (_tile_dpbssd, SPR+) behind feature
description:
# P3-amx-prefill-gemm — X3 tier, INT8 ONLY, PREFILL ONLY

## BACKGROUND / WHY
MEASURED LAW (NE-INH-4): **AMX-f32 does NOT beat ONNX-int8** (it streams 4× the bytes on memory-bound sizes). AMX must be **int8** (low bandwidth) and helps **compute-bound prefill, not memory-bound decode**. So the AMX path is int8-only, prefill-only; decode stays on X1.

## WHAT TO DO
Implement the X3 tier on Sapphire-Rapids+: `_tile_dpbssd` 16×16×64 int8 tile matmul → 16×16 i32 (catalog §6.6). AMX tile config via STTILECFG, 64-wide K, tile 16×16. Consume the X3 (AMX tile config) packing from P3-weight-prepack. Use ONLY for prefill GEMM (vision/MoE-prefill/patch-embed); decode uses X1. Dispatch order puts X3 above X1 for prefill. Bit-identical scalar fallback. Gate on `is_x86_feature_detected!("amx-int8")` (+ amx-tile). Note `_tile_dpbssd` is signed×signed (s8×s8), so the packing differs from VNNI's U8S8 — record the convention.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- int8 + prefill-only, by measured law — never route decode or f32 through AMX.
- Tile config/dealloc (TILECFG/TILERELEASE) must be managed correctly around the kernel to avoid corrupting the AMX state.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- If AMX-int8 prefill does not beat VNNI-512 prefill on the target's shapes, REVERT to X1 for that shape and ledger (do not ship a regression).
- Hardware availability is narrow; keep it strictly optional behind the feature gate and the dispatch order.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
Bit-identical i32 to scalar; AMX-int8 prefill beats VNNI-512 prefill where measured (else reverted+ledgered).

## TESTS REQUIRED
Unit: bit-identical vs scalar (s8×s8). Perf: micro-bench vs X1 prefill. depends_on P3-isa-dispatch (X3 tier), P3-weight-prepack (AMX tile-config packing), P3-vnni512-gemm (the X1 baseline it must beat).

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (review pass 1)


## ADDENDUM (review r1) — scope note vs the Apple-AMX path
This bead is **x86 AMX only** (`_tile_dpbssd`, Sapphire-Rapids+). The Apple-Silicon AMX coprocessor is a SEPARATE, deliberately-different situation (NE-INH-4 / plan §6.6 lesson 3): it is **not directly programmable** and is reached only via **Accelerate/BNNS (C/FFI), an opt-in feature** — covered by the new bead P3-r1-apple-amx-accelerate, with NEON SMMLA/SDOT as the directly-usable Mac default. Do not conflate the two: there is no `_tile_dpbssd` on Apple Silicon, and nothing in THIS bead should compile or dispatch on aarch64.

title: AVX2 i16-saturation overflow proof (split-accumulate every 2 K-steps)
description:
# P3-avx2-overflow-proof — the one non-i32-exact path, made safe or ledgered

## BACKGROUND / WHY
The AVX2 `vpmaddubsw` (maddubs) produces i16 intermediates that SATURATE before the `madd` widen to i32. So AVX2 is the ONE path in the catalog that is not automatically bit-identical to the i32-exact SMMLA/VNNI/SDOT/scalar paths (plan §6.6 ⚠). It must carry its OWN overflow proof.

## WHAT TO DO
Implement and prove split-accumulate: accumulate the i16 partials to i32 every 2 K-steps (plan §5.4 / §6.6) so no i16 intermediate can saturate for this model's operand ranges. Then prove bit-identical-to-scalar at WORST-CASE K=6848 (dense layer-0 down_proj; U8S8 ≤221.7M) with adversarial saturated operands (all 255 × ±127). If for some reason a divergence remains, instead record a DISCREPANCIES.md entry (reference behavior, our impl, MEASURED CER impact, kill-switch env var, review date) — never a silent numerics change.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Split every 2 K-steps because two u8(255)×s8(127) products = 2·32385 = 64770 > i16::MAX(32767), so an unsplit maddubs of a full row saturates; splitting bounds the i16 partial below the saturation point. The exact split cadence is derived from the operand ranges in the census.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
With split-accumulate the AVX2 GEMM is bit-identical i32 to scalar at K=6848 with saturated operands; OR a ledgered DISCREPANCIES entry with a measured CER delta exists. No silent divergence.

## TESTS REQUIRED

title: Golden-fixture harness + PROVENANCE.md (frozen reference loader, canonicalization, UPDATE_GOLDENS workflow)
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
Every parity gate, golden-artifact snapshot, differential test, and e2e comparison reads a FROZEN fixture produced by the Python/HF reference oracle. Without a disciplined fixture harness + provenance, fixtures rot, get silently regenerated, or are compared against the wrong model version — and the whole conformance ladder becomes meaningless. This task builds the shared, dependency-light fixture machinery the rest of E-TEST and all per-phase parity beads consume. It serves the over-arching goal directly: correctness-before-speed is only enforceable if the "correct" reference is frozen, hashed, and traceable to the exact model commit.

## WHAT TO DO
Build `tests/fixtures/` harness with these concrete deliverables:
1. **Directory layout** (mirrors plan §4.1):
   - `tests/fixtures/native/<doc>_reference.json` — frozen `focr ocr --json` reference outputs (decoded text + bbox tags) per golden image.
   - `tests/fixtures/activations/<stage>.npy` — per-layer activation dumps from the oracle: post-patch-embed, post-SAM, post-bridge/compress, post-CLIP, post-projector, post-connector, per-decoder-layer hidden states, pre-lm_head, logits.
   - `tests/fixtures/tokenizer/<case>.json` — frozen token-id sequences for the OQ-16 tokenizer conformance corpus.
   - `tests/fixtures/golden_corpus/` — the golden image corpus spanning {sparse page, dense page, 10-page, 40-page} (the §9.1 profiling/regime corpus, shared).
2. **`tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md`** (MANDATORY, per §8.6): records `transformers==4.57.1`, `torch==2.10.0`, `Pillow==12.1.1`, the pinned HF repo commit + GitHub commit (from the Phase −1 truth pack), the git ref of `gen_reference_fixtures.py`, the exact command, the `model.safetensors.index.json` `total_size` (6,672,212,480 bytes / 2710 tensors), and a `claim_id → fixture-hash` index. Each fixture file carries a SHA-256 recorded here.
3. **Rust fixture loader** (`tests/common/fixtures.rs` or similar) — a dependency-free reader: load `.npy` activation tensors (use the `fnp-io` NPY pattern or a small in-repo reader), load reference JSON, expose `Fixture::load(name) -> Fixture` with the recorded SHA-256 verified on load (refuse a fixture whose hash drifted).
4. **Canonicalization** before any golden compare: strip/scrub timing, run-id, durations from JSON; normalize line endings + paths for cross-platform; sort bbox lists. Per `/testing-golden-artifacts`: exact (insta) for `--json` structure + CLI help; fuzzy (epsilon/ULP) for logits + activation tensors (the comparator itself is E-VERIFY's ULP table — this harness just plumbs the values in); scrubbed for robot NDJSON; canonicalized for cross-platform.
5. **`UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` workflow**: regenerating goldens requires the env flag + a mandatory `git diff` review; `*.actual` files gitignored; **CI never auto-updates goldens** (a CI run with `UPDATE_GOLDENS` set is rejected).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Provenance is non-negotiable** (§8.6): a fixture without recorded oracle version + command + hash is invalid. The model changed on 2026-06-24; optimizing against a stale fixture is the exact failure mode the Phase −1 truth pack exists to prevent.
- **Hash-verify on load**: catches a corrupted/edited fixture immediately, not as a confusing parity failure 5 layers later.
- **Intentional divergence = XFAIL, never SKIP** (§8.6): if our impl deliberately differs from the reference, the fixture comparison is `XFAIL` with a `DISC-NNN` pointer into `docs/DISCREPANCIES.md`, so coverage accounting still counts it.
- **bf16 oracle nondeterminism**: fixtures from the oracle carry the measured nondeterminism envelope (§8.2) so downstream tolerances derive from MEASURED oracle variance, not a guessed epsilon. This harness stores that envelope alongside the fixtures (E-VERIFY computes it).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- `.npy` fixtures for 129280-vocab logits and per-layer hidden states are large — keep the committed set to the minimal golden corpus; large multi-page activation dumps may be model-gated (regenerated locally, not committed).
- A reference JSON with embedded timestamps will diff every run if not scrubbed — scrubbing is part of the loader, applied BEFORE compare.
- The 40-page golden's reference output is cross-page DEPENDENT under R-SWA (OQ-13) — do NOT store it as a concatenation of single-page parses; it is a single multi-page oracle run.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md` present with all required fields + a SHA-256 per fixture.
- Fixture loader verifies SHA-256 on load and refuses a drifted fixture (proven by a test that mutates a byte).
- Canonicalization deterministically scrubs timing/run-id/durations and normalizes line endings/paths (proven by a round-trip test).
- `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` regenerates `*.actual` and requires explicit review; CI rejects runs with the flag set.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit: loader rejects a fixture whose recorded SHA-256 ≠ on-disk content.
- Unit: canonicalizer is idempotent and removes all scrub-listed fields.
- Unit: a missing PROVENANCE field fails a `provenance_complete()` check.
- See sibling bead **TEST-fixture-harness-tests** for the full structured-logging test suite.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
- depends_on **E-P0**: needs `tests/fixtures/` scaffold + `scripts/gen_reference_fixtures.py` skeleton + the `.npy`/JSON conventions established.
- depends_on **E-VERIFY**: the oracle that PRODUCES these fixtures and the ULP/tolerance comparator that consumes them are E-VERIFY's; this harness is the frozen-storage + provenance + canonicalization plumbing around them.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## REVIEW-2 ADDENDUM — committed-vs-regenerated fixture policy, git-size discipline, staleness check
- **Concrete small-vs-large fixture policy + generation manifest.** The body says large multi-page activation dumps 'may be model-gated (regenerated locally, not committed)' but gives no MECHANISM. Define it concretely: a `tests/fixtures/MANIFEST.toml` listing every fixture as `committed` (small: the OQ-16 tokenizer id sequences, the canonicalized `<doc>_reference.json` text/bbox, a handful of small post-connector activations) or `regenerated` (large: 129280-vocab logits, per-decoder-layer hidden states for multi-page) with its SHA-256, byte size, and the `gen_reference_fixtures.py` invocation that produces it. The loader treats a `regenerated` fixture as model-gated (skip-with-SUCCESS if absent). This keeps the committed set small and git-sane while the heavy `.npy` are reproducible on demand.
- **Git-size discipline.** State the rule: NO multi-MB `.npy` committed without an explicit decision; prefer storing a small canonicalized slice + the regeneration command over a full vocab-wide logits dump. (If LFS is ever adopted it's an explicit decision, not a default.)
- **Fixture-staleness check tied to the pinned model commit.** PROVENANCE.md records the HF + GitHub model commit (E-PM1 truth pack); ADD a `fixtures_match_pinned_model()` check that compares PROVENANCE's recorded model commit/hash against the project's currently-pinned model commit and FAILS LOUDLY on mismatch — the exact 2026-06-24 'model changed under us' failure mode this harness exists to prevent. A stale fixture must be a hard error, not a silent wrong-reference compare.
- **`.actual` + regenerated-fixture gitignore.** Ensure `*.actual` AND the `regenerated`-class large `.npy` are gitignored so a local oracle run never accidentally commits a 6-vocab-wide dump.
notes: Gap update 2026-07-06 (sweep verdict PARTIAL): loader+provenance-verify+scrub+UPDATE_GOLDENS review loop + CI-rejects-flag guard + golden/PROVENANCE.md all shipped. REMAINING: tests/fixtures/MANIFEST.toml (committed-vs-regenerated policy) + a top-level tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md cataloguing the oracle/tokenizer/corpus fixtures beyond the CLI-golden subdir.
close_reason: DONE 2026-07-06 (force: blockers status-lagged; the harness half was verified done in the sweep — loader + provenance-verify + scrub + UPDATE_GOLDENS review loop + CI-rejects-flag guard + golden/PROVENANCE.md). This close lands the REVIEW-2 residuals: (1) tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md — the top-level catalogue (committed [C] vs regenerated-committed [R->C] per family, generator scripts + pinned stacks named, the weights-gated OFF-TREE families documented incl fixtures/native_f32 and the per-zoo seam dumps); (2) tests/fixtures/MANIFEST.toml — the machine-readable policy; (3) scripts/check_fixture_manifest.py — BIDIRECTIONAL validation (undeclared entry / declared-but-missing / closed kinds / generator-script-exists), self-test proves it catches both violation classes, real manifest clean, wired into scripts/check.sh.

title: many_pages_without_deadlock concurrency watchdog (pages ≫ pool; hangs/times out on regression)
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The single most expensive bug class in the sibling projects was a **nested-rayon-under-a-held-lock deadlock**; the frankensearch deadlock saga converged after 5 commits on the architectural fix. AGENTS.md doctrine #5 and plan §3.3/§6.5 make the rule non-negotiable: **single OcrModel behind a cache, SEQUENTIAL outer page/document loop, each forward fans out across all cores internally via the kernel's own rayon pool (pinned to physical cores, ONE live forward at a time), NEVER nest rayon under a held lock, NEVER nest a second asupersync runtime inside a task.** The durable guard is a CI watchdog: `many_pages_without_deadlock` runs pages ≫ pool and HANGS (CI timeout) on regression. This bead builds that watchdog.

## WHAT TO DO
Build `tests/many_pages_without_deadlock.rs`:
1. **Drive the engine over MANY pages** — page count ≫ the rayon pool size and ≫ the asupersync `blocking_threads` (e.g. 200+ pages over a 2-blocking-thread / N-core pool) through the real sequential page loop facade.
2. **Hard wall-clock timeout**: the test runs under `asupersync::time::timeout` (or a spawned watchdog thread) with a generous-but-bounded budget; exceeding it = a deadlock = test FAIL (in CI, the job timeout is the backstop). A deadlock manifests as a HANG, not a panic — the timeout IS the assertion.
3. **Assert no oversubscription**: log + assert that at most ONE live forward fans out at a time (the §6.5 invariant) and that `workers × per_worker_threads ≤ physical-core budget` (the §6.9 capacity-certificate invariant). Emit these as structured `stage` log lines with `simd_tier` + thread counts.
4. **Model-gated**: if weights are present, run real forwards; if absent, run a faithful STUB forward that reproduces the SAME concurrency topology (kernel rayon fan-out called from the sequential loop, the engine owning one runtime) so the deadlock SHAPE is exercised in CI without the 6.67 GB model. The stub must use the real orchestrator/`OcrEngine` concurrency code, not a fake — only the math is stubbed.
5. **Regression-detector self-test**: a `#[ignore]`-by-default variant that INJECTS a nested-rayon-under-lock (or a nested second runtime) and asserts the watchdog TIMES OUT — proving the watchdog actually catches the regression (run manually, not in the green CI path).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Pages ≫ pool** is the exact condition the frankensearch saga proved exposes the deadlock — fewer pages can mask it.
- **Stub-but-real-topology** so CI (no weights) still guards the concurrency architecture; the deadlock is in the ORCHESTRATION, not the math, so stubbing the math is sound and necessary.
- **The hang IS the signal**: a deadlock cannot be caught by an assertion that never runs; the wall-clock timeout converts a hang into a deterministic CI failure.
- **Capacity-certificate invariants logged** (§3.3/§6.9): no nested-runtime, no rayon-pool oversubscription, one live forward — these are the soak-test's pass conditions.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- **Cancellation is cooperative**: `spawn_blocking` keeps running on drop, so the watchdog timing out does not necessarily reclaim the thread — the test process may need to be killed; in CI the job timeout handles it, but the test should still report FAIL via the watchdog thread before the job timeout where possible.
- The stub forward must NOT accidentally serialize everything (which would mask a real deadlock) — it must reproduce the real fan-out-under-the-sequential-loop topology.
- NUMA/affinity features (`FOCR_NUMA`, hwloc) are behind a feature flag; the watchdog runs the no-NUMA fallback by default and the NUMA path when the feature is enabled.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `many_pages_without_deadlock` completes within its wall-clock budget on a healthy tree (CI green).
- The injected-regression self-test TIMES OUT (proving the watchdog catches a nested-rayon-under-lock / nested-runtime regression) — demonstrated once and documented.
- Structured logs assert: ≤1 live forward at a time; `workers × per_worker_threads ≤ physical cores`; no nested runtime.
- Runs model-gated (real forwards with weights; real-topology stub without).

## TESTS REQUIRED
- The watchdog itself (the soak).
- The `#[ignore]` regression-detector that proves the watchdog times out under an injected violation.
- A capacity-certificate log assertion test (p95/p99 queueing evidence + no-oversubscription proof, §3.3).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
- depends_on **E-P0**: needs `OcrEngine` owning the one asupersync Runtime, the sequential page-loop facade, and the kernel rayon pool wiring from the scaffold.
- depends_on **TEST-log-emitter**: emits the concurrency-topology + capacity-certificate log lines.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## REVIEW-2 ADDENDUM — cancellation cleanup + worker-panic propagation (distinct concurrency bugs)
- **Cancellation / Ctrl-C cleanup under the many-pages soak.** A deadlock is one failure class; a botched CANCELLATION is another. Add a soak variant that issues a cancel (ShutdownController / CancellationToken from P0-engine-runtime) MID-run over the pages≫pool workload and asserts: the FinalizerRegistry runs, no thread is left spinning, the engine returns **exit 6 (cancelled)** promptly within a bounded budget, and a subsequent run on the same `OcrEngine` still succeeds (the single cached `OcrModel` mutex is NOT left poisoned/locked). A cancel that hangs is as bad as a deadlock.
- **Worker-panic propagation (no poisoned mutex, no silent hang).** Inject a panic INSIDE a kernel rayon task under the sequential page loop and assert it surfaces as a typed `FocrError` (not a silent hang, not a poisoned `Mutex<OcrModel>` that wedges every subsequent page). This is the exact insidious variant of the deadlock saga: a panic while holding the model lock. Assert the engine recovers (next page works) or fails cleanly with a clear error — never hangs.
- **Log the topology invariants on BOTH the cancel and panic variants**, not just the clean soak: ≤1 live forward, `workers × per_worker_threads ≤ physical cores`, no nested runtime — so the capacity certificate covers the failure paths too.
- **Backpressure assertion.** Assert the streaming `sync_channel` stays BOUNDED under the soak (the §7.3 bounded-channel + `recv_timeout(~40ms)` drain) — an unbounded-growth regression is a memory bug the watchdog should also catch.
notes: Gap update 2026-07-06 (sweep verdict PARTIAL): core watchdog + spine + construction + hang-self-test all shipped; bd-223.2 just added the cancellation machinery (cancel_checkpoint in all 7 decode loops, cancellation_token_into_closure_aborts) and bounded_stream_backpressure (lib.rs) — narrowing the addendum gaps. REMAINING: a cancel-mid-HEAVY-run watchdog variant (request_shutdown during a real weights-armed batch -> Cancelled propagation), worker-panic-propagation (typed error, no poisoned model mutex), and an #[ignore] injected nested-rayon-under-lock hang case.
close_reason: Core acceptance ALL met: (a) many_pages_without_deadlock green on a healthy tree — scenarios 1 (sequential outer loop), 1b (spine one-live-forward gauge incl model-cache-guard assertion), 1c (zoo lanes), 2 (concurrent engine construction); (b) injected-regression self-test watchdog_detects_a_real_hang proves the watchdog TIMES OUT on a real hang — PLUS a live production demo 2026-07-06: the first armed 256-page real-forward soak correctly tripped the 1800s budget (~6.9 s/page GOT int8) and self-diagnosed DEADLOCK_SUSPECTED w/ pool/pages/budget breadcrumbs; (c) the capacity-certificate log assertion shipped as capacity_certificate_bounded_stream_soak (focr-capacity-certificate/v1: armed p50/p95/p99 = 6.83/7.41/9.58 s per page, 48/48 Ok, pool width stable, bounded stream max-in-flight <= cap+1 w/ backpressure engaged in fast mode) — commit f3ff1bb; (d) model-gated: heavy branch w/ FOCR_MODEL_PATH(+FOCR_WATCHDOG_IMAGE for real forwards, FOCR_CAPACITY_PAGES sizing), skip-with-SUCCESS + /nonexistent proof without. REVIEW-2 addendum variants (cancel-mid-soak, worker-panic propagation, failure-path topology logs) split to bd-1ryu — they need a process-isolated test file (global shutdown flag) + a fault-injection hook, a distinct chunk.

title: focrq writer accepts noncanonical QInt4 group sizes
description: The .focrq writer validates QInt4 group_size only as nonzero and dividing k. The format docs and quant/int4.rs define valid QInt4 group sizes as exactly 16 or 32 (tiers Int4G16 / Int4G32). As written, FocrqBuilder::add_quantized can emit artifacts with group_size=2, 4, 8, etc.; the reader mechanically accepts them, but those artifacts violate docs/focrq-format.md and the quantizer contract. Fix the writer to reject non-{16,32} QInt4 group sizes and keep tests using canonical sizes.
close_reason: Fixed FocrqBuilder validation so QInt4 writer output must use canonical group sizes 16 or 32, with canonical roundtrip and noncanonical rejection coverage. Verified with quant::focrq, quant --lib, full scripts/check.sh through cargo test, and focused UBS on src/quant/focrq.rs.

title: PDF decompress-bomb: bound FlateDecode/LZW inflate before it allocates
description: decompressed_stream (src/pdf.rs) calls lopdf Stream::decompressed_content(), which allocates the FULL inflated output before any length check. The MAX_PIXELS guard bounds DECLARED image dims (and the cmyk/raster Vecs), but a tiny highly-compressed FlateDecode/LZW stream (zip-bomb, 1000:1) inflates to GBs during decompressed_content() regardless of declared dims — a residual OOM/DoS vector inherent to lopdf's non-streaming inflate. Mitigation options: (a) compute expected_len = width*height*comps*ceil(bpc/8) and reject before decode when the stream's declared/encoded size implies an implausible ratio; (b) upstream a size-bounded inflate in lopdf; (c) cap process RSS. Pre-existing lopdf behavior, not introduced by the native-PDF work; low severity (needs a crafted adversarial PDF). Found during the native-PDF fresh-eyes review (bd-0a7 epic).
close_reason: src/pdf.rs decompressed_stream bounds the sole-FlateDecode inflate via flate2 ZlibDecoder + Read::take(cap+1) under expected_sample_cap (4x the MAX_PIXELS-bounded sample bytes); a clean inflate overrunning the cap errors as a decompression bomb, non-zlib raw falls back to lopdf. flate2 now a direct dep. Commit ba71ff4; centralized gate (fmt/clippy -D warnings/test) green.

title: Phase -1: Source/Oracle Truth Pack — pin sources, hash everything, resolve every OPEN/OQ before any kernel
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
This is the executable foundation of franken_ocr and **the highest-EV epic in the project**. Per the `/idea-wizard` review transcribed in plan §10 Phase -1: *"the single highest-EV move is NOT a kernel — it is an executable truth pack that stops the project from optimizing the wrong model semantics (the model changed on 2026-06-24)."* The target model `baidu/Unlimited-OCR` was released ~2026-06-22, **post knowledge-cutoff**, so every model-specific claim in the master plan is tagged [VERIFIED] (confirmed from a primary source), [REPORTED] (paper/card, not line-verified), or [OPEN] (must be code-confirmed). This epic converts all [OPEN]/OQ items into pinned, line-backed answers and freezes the exact sources so every downstream kernel is built against a known model version.

The over-arching goal franken_ocr serves: **max CPU speed for THIS one model via int4/int8 + fused-at-peak kernels, correctness before speed, a portable single binary, agent-ergonomic**. None of that is possible if the model semantics are wrong. AGENTS.md hard rule: *"no kernel ships against an unresolved [OPEN]. A phase exit gate cannot pass while it depends on an unresolved OQ."* This epic is what makes that rule satisfiable.

## WHAT TO DO (the Phase -1 deliverable, plan §10)
Produce, all under `docs/truth-pack/` with a machine-readable `claim_id → source-line` index:
1. **Pin the exact sources**: HF repo commit + GitHub commit. Codex-reported candidates to VERIFY against the live repos: `HF 3a7f4dbbbffcc6f9282712c5b0d7cc31b3812da5`, `GitHub 7e98affeacba24e95562fbaa234ddb89b856874a` — record the *verified* hashes, not the reported ones.
2. **Snapshot + SHA-256 every load-bearing source**: `config.json`, `tokenizer.json`, `modeling_unlimitedocr.py`, `modeling_deepseekv2.py`, `deepencoder.py`, `conversation.py`, `model.safetensors.index.json`, `LICENSE`.
3. **Generate the machine-readable token/shape/buffer census** from the pinned config (§2.4, §8.6), CI-guarded against source drift.
4. **Extract the spec** `EXISTING_UNLIMITED_OCR_STRUCTURE.md` (§8.6 / §10 Phase 1) — every data structure, exact preprocessing/tiling rules, `SlidingWindowLlamaAttention` semantics, projector concat order, tokenizer rules — verbatim from the pinned `modeling_*.py`/`deepencoder.py`/`conversation.py`.
5. **Resolve every [OPEN]/OQ-1..OQ-18 (§13)** with a quoted, line-backed citation from the pinned source.
6. **Decide the oracle strategy (OQ-17, CPU-vs-GPU)** — prove CPU HF runs, else GPU-correctness + CPU-perf split (§8.1) — and capture one smoke fixture.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Spec-first porting** (`/porting-to-rust`, §8.6): *extract spec → implement from spec → never translate line-by-line.* The four documents are PLAN_TO_PORT (the master plan), EXISTING_UNLIMITED_OCR_STRUCTURE.md (THE SPEC, this epic produces it), PROPOSED_ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE_PARITY.md. Kernels are implemented from the spec, which is what resolves the §13 [OPEN]s.
- **Pin + hash before anything**: the model is freshly released and may be re-uploaded; a moving reference silently invalidates every fixture and every measured ratio. The negative-evidence ledger schema (docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md) *requires* a `model source commit + fixture hash` field on every entry — that field is sourced from this truth pack.
- **CI-guarded census**: plan §2.4 — *"A machine-readable token/shape/buffer census (§8.6, generated from the pinned config) is the source of truth and CI fails if the source/config changes."*

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Plan §11 risk *"[OPEN] model details wrong"* (MED-HIGH): hard rule no kernel ships against an unresolved [OPEN]; this epic gates Phase 1. R-SWA/RoPE/projector/SAM-window must read the actual source first.
- The token budget is **NOT just 256** (§2.4): a 1024 view yields 256 image-feature + structural tokens ⇒ `(16+1)·16 + 1 = 273` slots; the census must count every token CLASS or KV/buffer sizing is wrong.
- OQ-17 gotcha: `infer()` is CUDA-oriented; a CPU bf16 HF oracle is not guaranteed to run, which decides the meaning of G2 (perf claim).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (Phase -1 exit gates, plan §10)
- Every OQ (OQ-1..OQ-18) answered with a pinned-source citation (file + line range + quoted text).
- All source hashes recorded (SHA-256 of every load-bearing file + verified HF/GitHub commits).
- Census generated + CI-guarded against source drift.
- Oracle strategy decided + smoke fixture captured.
- **No kernel work begins until this phase is green.**

## TESTS REQUIRED
- A CI guard test that re-hashes the pinned sources and fails on drift (the census generator's drift guard).
- A `claim_id → source-line` index that is itself validated (every OQ answer references a real, in-range line of a hashed file).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
This epic depends on nothing — it is the root of the dependency graph. Every kernel epic (E-P1, E-P2, E-P3, E-P4) and verification epic (E-VERIFY) depends on E-PM1 and on specific OQ beads it owns. The OQ beads here are the foundation every kernel depends on.
close_reason: probe

title: Pin + verify the HF repo commit and GitHub commit for baidu/Unlimited-OCR
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The target model was released ~2026-06-22 and could be re-uploaded at any time; HF model repos are mutable. Every golden fixture, every measured perf ratio, and every OQ answer is only meaningful relative to an EXACT immutable commit. Plan §10 Phase -1 makes pinning the first task. The negative-evidence ledger (docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md) and DISCREPANCIES.md both require a `model source commit + fixture hash` provenance field — that value comes from here.

## WHAT TO DO
1. Resolve and VERIFY the HF repo commit for `baidu/Unlimited-OCR`. Codex reported `HF 3a7f4dbbbffcc6f9282712c5b0d7cc31b3812da5` — do NOT trust the reported value; query the live HF repo (e.g. `huggingface_hub` revision listing / `git ls-remote https://huggingface.co/baidu/Unlimited-OCR`) and record the *verified* full-length commit SHA, the resolution date, and the method used.
2. Resolve and VERIFY the GitHub commit. Codex reported `GitHub 7e98affeacba24e95562fbaa234ddb89b856874a` — verify against the live GitHub repo (`git ls-remote`) and record the verified SHA.
3. Write both verified commits into `docs/truth-pack/PINNED_SOURCES.md` (or equivalent) with: repo URL, verified commit SHA, resolution timestamp, and a note if the verified hash DIFFERS from the Codex-reported one (which would itself be evidence the model moved).
4. Record the runtime pin from the README that the oracle must use: `transformers==4.57.1`, `torch==2.10.0`, `Pillow==12.1.1`, `pymupdf` — NOT the `4.46.3` recorded in config.json (plan §8.1, §11 reference-version-drift risk).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Verify, don't trust the reported hash**: the whole point of pinning is to detect a moved model; copying Codex's number defeats it.
- **Pin runtime to README, not config**: plan §8.1 explicitly warns config records `4.46.3` while README pins runtime `4.57.1`/`torch 2.10.0`; the oracle and all fixtures use the README runtime.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- If the live HF hash differs from the Codex-reported one, the model HAS changed since the plan was written — flag loudly; all [REPORTED] facts must be re-verified.
- HF repos can have separate revisions for LFS pointers vs the resolved blob; record the commit that resolves the safetensors + config + tokenizer together.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `docs/truth-pack/PINNED_SOURCES.md` contains verified full-length HF + GitHub commit SHAs, resolution timestamps, and the verification method.
- Runtime pin (`transformers==4.57.1`, `torch==2.10.0`) recorded.
- Any divergence from the Codex-reported hashes is explicitly flagged.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- A check (script or CI step) that the recorded commit still resolves the expected file set; a divergence is a loud failure (this feeds PM1-hash-sources and PM1-census-generator drift guards).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on E-PM1 (parent). Blocks PM1-hash-sources (you hash files at a pinned commit) and PM1-oracle-strategy (the oracle uses the pinned runtime).
close_reason: test

title: OQ-4: Q/K head dim when use_mla=false and qk_nope/rope_head_dim=0 (likely 128 from q_proj shape)
description:
## THE EXACT QUESTION (plan §13, OQ-4)
What is the Q/K head dimension when `use_mla=false` and `qk_nope_head_dim=0` / `qk_rope_head_dim=0`? Plan §2.3.2 notes config does not directly give it in this configuration, but it is *"almost certainly 128 from q_proj shape."* Confirm from the actual q_proj weight shape.

## SOURCE FILE / LINE TO READ
`modeling_deepseekv2.py` (how q/k head_dim is computed when MLA is off) AND the `q_proj` weight shape from `model.safetensors.index.json` / the tensor census: q_proj is `[out, 1280]`; out = num_attention_heads(10) × head_dim. If out=1280 ⇒ head_dim=128 (consistent with v_head_dim=128, 10·128=1280).

## WHAT THIS BLOCKS
Attention shapes — the q/k/v/o_proj GEMM dimensions and the RoPE rotation dim (`decoder.rs`, `rswa.rs`). A wrong head_dim mis-shapes every attention matmul.

## BACKGROUND / WHY IT MATTERS
Plan §2.3.2: `v_head_dim=128`, `num_attention_heads=10`, `num_key_value_heads=10` (no GQA), `use_mla=false` (plain MHA, no latent decompression). Plan §6.4: *"Plain MHA (no MLA decompression): q/k/v/o_proj separate dense GEMMs, 10 heads, head_dim 128."* Pinning head_dim from the actual tensor shape removes the last [OPEN] in the attention shape set.

## DELIVERABLE / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Quoted, line-backed answer: Q/K head_dim value (expected 128), cited to both the modeling code path and the q_proj tensor shape in the census/index.
- [OPEN] flips to [VERIFIED].

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on PM1-hash-sources and PM1-census-generator (q_proj shape). Feeds the E-P1 attention kernels and the RoPE kernel (OQ-5).

title: OQ-6: Exact SAM⊕CLIP feature-fusion / concat order producing the 2048-dim projector input
description:
## THE EXACT QUESTION (plan §13, OQ-6)
What is the exact SAM⊕CLIP feature-fusion / concat order producing the 2048-dim projector input? Plan §2.3.1 flags it [OPEN]: *"SAM-1024 ⊕ CLIP-1024 vs interleaved; deepencoder.py mentions low_high_hybrid_split_mlp_gelu / hybrid_split_feature_mlp_gelu variants — MUST be read line-by-line from deepencoder.py before implementing the projector."*

`deepencoder.py` (line-level). Read how SAM features (1024-dim after neck) and CLIP-L features (1024-dim) are combined into the 2048-dim input to the single linear projector (`projector_config`: input_dim=2048, n_embed=1280, projector_type=linear). The projector + vision bridge (`vision_bridge.rs`). Plan §2.3.1: SAM features + CLIP features concatenated to 2048 dims → single linear projector 2048→1280. The 16× compression bridge (64×64→16×16=256 tokens) precedes this. The concat order is the kind of detail that is invisible in the architecture diagram but corrupts everything if wrong.

title: Build the CI-guarded machine-readable token/shape/buffer census generator
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The decoder context, R-SWA reference-block size `m`, all KV/ring-buffer allocations, the MoE token-group buffers, and the sampler's ngram window are all sized from a token/shape census that MUST be derived from the pinned config — not hand-typed. Plan §2.4: *"A machine-readable token/shape/buffer census (§8.6, generated from the pinned config) is the source of truth and CI fails if the source/config changes."* §8.6 ties it to the spec. AGENTS.md doctrine #7: the reference block `m` grows ~256 image-feature tokens per page plus structural/prompt tokens — 273 token slots at 1024 before prompt — so a wrong census silently mis-sizes every buffer.

## WHAT TO DO
Write a generator (a `focr` subcommand or a script) that reads the pinned `config.json` + `model.safetensors.index.json` and emits a machine-readable census (`docs/truth-pack/CENSUS.json` + a human `CENSUS.md`) covering:
1. **Decoder shapes** (VERIFIED from config, §2.3.2): hidden_size 1280, num_hidden_layers 12, num_attention_heads 10, num_key_value_heads 10 (no GQA), intermediate_size (dense layer-0) 6848, moe_intermediate_size (per expert) 896, n_routed_experts 64, n_shared_experts 2, num_experts_per_tok 6 (top-6 greedy), first_k_dense_replace 1 (layer 0 dense, layers 1-11 MoE), v_head_dim 128, use_mla false, max_position_embeddings 32768, vocab_size 129280, sliding_window/sliding_window_size 128.
2. **Token-class census per mode** (the OQ-18 deliverable): image-feature tokens, `image_newline` tokens, `view_seperator` tokens. Base mode 1024 view = 256 image-feature (16×16) + structural ⇒ `(16+1)·16 + 1 = 273` slots; plus prompt + generated. Gundam multi-tile totals per aspect ratio (each 640 crop ≈ 100 tokens) — populated from OQ-18's resolved answer.
3. **KV/buffer sizing**: per-layer R-SWA reference block worst case `m ≈ 32768 − 128`; the 128-wide generated-token ring per layer; the constant-KV formula `C_RSWA(T) = L·(m + min(n,T)) ≤ L·(m+n)`, L=12, n=128.
4. **Tensor census**: all 2710 tensors with (name, shape, dtype) cross-checked vs `model.safetensors.index.json` (total_size 6,672,212,480). This IS the WeightsManifest the converter validates against (plan §5.1 step 2).
5. **i32-overflow worst case** (plan §5.4, AGENTS.md doctrine #6): dense layer-0 `down_proj` K=6848 ⇒ S8S8 ≤ 110.4M, U8S8 ≤ 221.7M; the census records the worst-case K per GEMM class so the overflow proof test has a generated source of truth.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Generated, not typed**: a census drift between code and config is the silent-corruption class this guard exists to kill.
- **CI-guarded**: CI fails if the pinned source/config changes (re-hash + regenerate + diff). This is plan §2.4's hard requirement.
- **Count every token CLASS, not the 256 compression figure** (§2.4, OQ-18): R-SWA `m` and KV sizing depend on it.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Some token-class counts (Gundam per-aspect-ratio totals, ngram window per mode) are OPEN until OQ-18 / OQ-7 are resolved — the generator must consume their resolved values, so this bead depends on those OQs for full population (the config-only part can land first; the Gundam/ngram cells are filled when OQ-7/OQ-18 close).
- The `~2196 vs ~2229` NVFP4 module-count discrepancy (OQ-14) is reconciled against THIS census's quantizable-linear count: experts 11·64·3=2112 + attention 12·4=48 + shared 11·2·3=66 + dense-layer-0 3 (+ lm_head 1) ≈ 2229-2230. The census must enumerate exactly these so OQ-14 has a denominator.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `CENSUS.json` is generated purely from the pinned config + index (no hand-typed shapes).
- The tensor census matches all 2710 tensors and total_size 6,672,212,480 from `model.safetensors.index.json`.
- A CI guard regenerates the census and fails on any diff vs the committed census (source-drift detection).
- The quantizable-linear enumeration (for OQ-14) and the worst-case K table (for the overflow proof) are present.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- `census_matches_index`: assert generated tensor (name, shape) set == `model.safetensors.index.json` set, count == 2710, total_size == 6,672,212,480.
- `census_drift_guard`: regenerate from pinned source, assert byte-identical to committed `CENSUS.json` (fails on source change).
- `census_token_classes`: assert Base-1024 placeholder structure == 273 slots `(16+1)·16+1` once OQ-18 is resolved.
- `census_overflow_worstcase`: assert the worst-case K table includes dense layer-0 down_proj K=6848.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on PM1-hash-sources (reads pinned config + index). Depends on OQ-18 and OQ-7 to populate Gundam/ngram/token-class cells. Depends on OQ-14 to confirm the quantizable-linear denominator. Blocks Phase-1 buffer-sizing and the WeightsManifest census the converter uses (E-P2).

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## REVIEW NOTE (r2): dependency direction with OQ-14 (no cycle)
The DEPENDENCIES NOTE says this census 'depends on OQ-14 to confirm the quantizable-linear denominator', while OQ-14 depends on this census for its ~2229 denominator. To avoid a dependency CYCLE, the BLOCKING direction is **census → OQ-14 only**: the tensor census (the quantizable-linear enumeration: experts 11·64·3 + attention 12·4 + shared 11·2·3 + dense-layer-0 3 + lm_head 1) is generated **purely from `model.safetensors.index.json`** and needs nothing from OQ-14. OQ-14 then *reconciles the NVFP4 scale-key set against* that committed denominator. The 'OQ-14 confirms the denominator' phrasing is co-validation (a cross-check that the enumeration is right), NOT a blocking prerequisite — implement and commit the enumeration first; OQ-14 reads it.

## STRUCTURED-LOGGING REQUIREMENT (r2)
The drift-guard and census tests must emit NDJSON structured logs (one line per check) so CI and the gauntlet can consume them: `{test, n_tensors_expected: 2710, n_tensors_found, total_size_expected: 6672212480, total_size_found, base1024_slots_expected: 273, base1024_slots_found, worstcase_K_downproj: 6848, census_sha256, source_config_sha256, drift: bool, pass: bool}`. A drift failure must log the OLD vs NEW config/index SHA-256 so the 'model moved' event is self-documenting.

title: Decide the oracle strategy (CPU-vs-GPU split) and capture one smoke fixture
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The whole parity ladder (L0-L5) and the perf claim G2 hinge on what reference we compare against. Plan §8.1 warns: *"The official infer() path is CUDA-oriented (.cuda() + CUDA autocast), so a CPU bf16 HF oracle is NOT guaranteed to run as-is (OQ-17)."* The resolution (plan §8.1) is to SPLIT the oracle: **(correctness)** golden fixtures come from the unmodified official model on a CUDA host, frozen once and committed — parity NEVER depends on CPU HF; **(performance)** the CPU baseline is separate — either a CPU-patched HF run (force tensors to CPU, disable autocast) that is PROVEN to reproduce the GPU oracle's tokens within the nondeterminism floor (§8.2), or, if CPU HF is infeasible, the perf claim is stated against the best CPU reference that actually runs (llama.cpp GGUF / ONNX Runtime / MLAS) and labeled as such. This bead IS the OQ-17 decision plus the Phase -1 smoke fixture.

## WHAT TO DO
1. Read `modeling_unlimitedocr.py` `infer()` — record the exact device/autocast lines (`.cuda()`, autocast dtype). (This is the OQ-17 source read.)
2. Attempt a CPU-patched HF run (force CPU, disable autocast) of `model.infer()` on one golden image and determine whether it reproduces the GPU oracle's token sequence within the oracle nondeterminism floor.
3. **Establish the oracle's OWN nondeterminism floor FIRST** (plan §8.2): run the oracle twice and at two thread counts over a small corpus; record the per-token divergence rate + first-divergence position as a committed fixture (the bf16 129280-vocab argmax is tie-prone across BLAS reduction order). L4 "exact" is defined only over the prefix the oracle reproduces identically; the L3 logit tolerance is DERIVED from this measured variance, NOT from the imported frankensearch `0.055`.
4. Decide and record in `docs/truth-pack/ORACLE_STRATEGY.md`: which path is correctness oracle (frozen GPU fixtures), which is perf baseline (CPU-patched HF if proven, else llama.cpp/ONNX/MLAS labeled), and the resulting meaning of G2.
5. Capture one smoke fixture: per-layer activation dumps (post-patch-embed, post-SAM, post-bridge/compress, post-CLIP, post-projector, post-connector, per-decoder-layer hidden states, pre-lm_head, logits) + end-to-end decoded text for one golden image, with a `PROVENANCE.md` (`transformers==4.57.1`, `torch==2.10.0`, git ref, exact command — plan §8.6).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Correctness fixtures are GPU-frozen and committed** — parity must never depend on a CPU HF run that may not exist (§8.1).
- **Nondeterminism floor measured before tolerances** (§8.2): a franken_ocr int8 divergence inside the oracle's own bf16 noise is NOT a bug; setting tolerances before measuring the floor would either over- or under-gate.
- **G2 honesty** (§1.1, §11): G2's "beats the CPU reference" is only honest against whatever CPU reference is PROVEN to run; this decision fixes that.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- If CPU-patched HF cannot reproduce GPU tokens, the gauntlet (§9.3) targets llama.cpp GGUF / ONNX / MLAS and labels every ratio with the precision (focr-int8 vs torch-bf16 vs torch-int8) — a raw cross-precision ratio is meaningless (§9.3 precision annotation rule).
- The community GGUF requires llama.cpp PR #17400 (not upstream) — if used as the CPU perf reference, record that dependency.
- Use `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` + seeded RNG for the gauntlet oracle bridge (§8.5), but the *correctness* fixtures capture the production (non-deterministic) path so the floor is real.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `ORACLE_STRATEGY.md` records the OQ-17 decision (CPU HF runs/reproduces-or-not) with the cited `infer()` device/autocast lines.
- The oracle nondeterminism floor is measured and committed (per-token divergence rate, first-divergence position) — the source of the L3/L4 tolerances.
- One smoke fixture (per-layer + end-to-end) is captured with full `PROVENANCE.md`.
- The perf-baseline choice (CPU-patched HF vs llama.cpp/ONNX) is recorded with its proof-of-equivalence (or its labeled-as-such caveat).

## TESTS REQUIRED
- A fixture-provenance check: the smoke fixture carries `PROVENANCE.md` with the pinned runtime + git ref + exact command.
- A determinism-floor sanity test: re-loading the committed floor fixture and asserting the recorded divergence envelope is well-formed (used by E-VERIFY to derive L3/L4 tolerances).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on PM1-pin-sources (uses the pinned runtime) and PM1-hash-sources (cites the hashed `modeling_unlimitedocr.py`). IS the resolution of OQ-17 (depends_on OQ-17 read). Blocks E-VERIFY (the parity ladder uses these fixtures + floor) and the perf gauntlet (E-P3) which targets the chosen CPU baseline.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## RUNTIME REPRODUCIBILITY ARTIFACT (r2)
The correctness fixtures and PROVENANCE.md pin `transformers==4.57.1`, `torch==2.10.0`, `Pillow==12.1.1`, `pymupdf` — but a version string is not a reproducible environment. This bead should also freeze a **fully-resolved lockfile** (`docs/truth-pack/oracle-env/requirements.lock` with transitive pins + hashes, e.g. `pip freeze` / `pip-compile --generate-hashes` output) and record the exact Python + CUDA driver versions used to generate the GPU golden fixtures. Rationale: a future re-run of `scripts/gen_reference_fixtures.py` (E-P0) that resolves a different transitive dep silently changes the bf16 nondeterminism floor, invalidating the derived L3/L4 tolerances. The lockfile is the reproducibility anchor the floor measurement and every committed fixture inherit. Cross-reference: §10 Phase 0 builds `scripts/fetch_model.sh` — it MUST pin to the PM1-pin-sources verified HF commit, not a floating `main`.

## STRUCTURED-LOGGING REQUIREMENT (r2)
The nondeterminism-floor measurement must emit NDJSON: per run `{image_id, thread_count, seed, run_idx, n_tokens, first_divergence_pos, per_token_divergence_rate, max_logit_abs_diff, deterministic_prefix_len}`, and a summary `{corpus, n_images, floor_first_divergence_min, floor_divergence_rate_p95, derived_L3_logit_tol, derived_L4_exact_prefix_policy}` so E-VERIFY can mechanically derive the L3/L4 tolerances from the committed fixture rather than re-reading prose.

title: OQ-1: R-SWA reference set m — visual-only or visual+prompt? Exact mask boundary
description:
## THE EXACT QUESTION (plan §13, OQ-1)
R-SWA reference set `m`: does it include the running **prompt** tokens, or strictly the **visual** tokens? And what is the exact mask boundary between prompt vs generated tokens? Plan §2.3.3 notes the conflict: *"Paper says 'all reference tokens (visual tokens in OCR)' but Figure 2 caption says 'visual+prompt'."*

## SOURCE FILE / LINE TO READ
`SlidingWindowLlamaAttention` in `modeling_deepseekv2.py` (the hashed snapshot from PM1-hash-sources). Read how the reference (never-evicted) KV block is constructed: does it span only the vision-token positions, or vision+prompt-prefix positions? Determine the exact index boundary where the sliding 128-window begins.

## WHAT THIS BLOCKS
The R-SWA attention kernel (`rswa.rs`) and prefill (building the reference KV block). The attention mask cannot be finalized without this — a wrong `m` boundary attends to the wrong tokens and silently corrupts decode (surfaces only as an L2/L4 parity drift). Plan §6.4: *"resolve the R-SWA boundary questions (§2.3.3 / OQ-1..3 and the multi-page span OQ-13) from SlidingWindowLlamaAttention before finalizing the mask."*

## BACKGROUND / WHY IT MATTERS
R-SWA is the one architectural novelty (plan §2.3.3): `o_t = Σ_{j∈N(t)} α_tj v_j` where `N(t) = {all reference tokens} ∪ {last n=128 generated tokens}`. The reference tokens are a frozen global KV — never evicted, excluded from state transitions. Whether `m` = visual-only or visual+prompt changes the reference-block length used for KV/buffer sizing (PM1-census-generator) and per-token attention compute `O(m+128)`.

## DELIVERABLE / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- A quoted, line-backed answer in EXISTING_UNLIMITED_OCR_STRUCTURE.md + CLAIM_INDEX.json: `m` = visual-only OR visual+prompt, with the exact reference-block index span and the sliding-window start boundary, cited to `SlidingWindowLlamaAttention` line range.
- The [OPEN] tag for the R-SWA reference set flips to [VERIFIED].

title: OQ-2: Is attention uniformly R-SWA across all 12 decoder layers (incl. layer 0)?
description:
## THE EXACT QUESTION (plan §13, OQ-2)
Is attention uniformly R-SWA across all 12 layers (including layer 0)? Is there any layer that retains full (non-sliding) attention? Plan §2.3.3 hypothesis: *"attention is expected R-SWA everywhere, including layer 0 — the first_k_dense_replace=1 split affects only the MLP, not attention."* Confirm this from source.

## SOURCE FILE / LINE TO READ
`modeling_deepseekv2.py` — the decoder layer construction loop. Verify whether every one of the 12 layers instantiates `SlidingWindowLlamaAttention` (vs some layers using a full-attention class), and confirm that `first_k_dense_replace=1` (layer 0 dense MLP) does NOT also make layer-0 attention full.

## WHAT THIS BLOCKS
The decoder attention dispatch (`decoder.rs` 12-layer loop). If even one layer is full-attention, the R-SWA constant-KV property and the per-layer ring-buffer allocation differ for that layer — a wrong assumption breaks both correctness and the KV-bound invariant the gauntlet monitors (§8.5: *"KV cache never exceeds L·(m+128)"*).

## BACKGROUND / WHY IT MATTERS
Plan §2.3.3: R-SWA *"replaces ALL decoder attention (every one of the 12 layers)."* The KV formula `C_RSWA(T)=L·(m+min(n,T))` uses L=12 uniformly; if a layer is exempt, L is effectively smaller for the ring and the buffer math changes.

## DELIVERABLE / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Quoted, line-backed answer: all 12 layers are R-SWA (or the explicit list of any exceptions), cited to the layer-construction line range.
- Confirmation that `first_k_dense_replace=1` affects only the MLP, not attention.
- [OPEN] flips to [VERIFIED].

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on PM1-hash-sources. Feeds PM1-spec-extraction and the E-P1 decoder loop. Coupled to OQ-1/OQ-3.

title: OQ-3: Exact warm-up vs ring-overwrite mask semantics during the first 128 decode steps
description:
## THE EXACT QUESTION (plan §13, OQ-3)
What are the exact warm-up vs ring-overwrite mask semantics during the first 128 decode steps? Plan §2.3.3 reports the mechanism: *"records prefill_len on first decode, warms up until cache reaches prefill_len+W, then in-place ring overwrites at slot = prefill_len + ring_pos, ring_pos = (ring_pos+1) % W"* (W=128). Confirm and pin the exact arithmetic and the mask during warm-up.

## SOURCE FILE / LINE TO READ
`SlidingWindowLlamaAttention` in `modeling_deepseekv2.py`. Read: how `prefill_len` is recorded; the warm-up condition (cache length < prefill_len+W); the in-place overwrite slot formula; the `ring_pos` update; and crucially the attention MASK applied during the first 128 steps (does a partially-filled ring mask out unfilled slots, or attend to stale data?).

## WHAT THIS BLOCKS
The R-SWA ring-buffer KV cache implementation (`rswa.rs`) — the single most important kernel implication (plan §2.3.3: *"This is the single most important kernel implication."*). Getting the warm-up mask wrong attends to garbage ring slots before the ring fills, corrupting the first ≤128 generated tokens.

## BACKGROUND / WHY IT MATTERS
Plan §6.4: *"Write the new K,V into the ring at slot = prefill_len + (t % 128) (after warm-up)."* The pre-warm-up behavior (steps 0..127, ring not yet full) is exactly where a mask bug hides — it only manifests on the early output tokens and is easy to miss in aggregate CER.

## DELIVERABLE / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Quoted, line-backed answer: exact `prefill_len` recording, warm-up condition, slot formula, `ring_pos` update, and the warm-up-phase mask semantics, cited to `SlidingWindowLlamaAttention`.
- [OPEN] flips to [VERIFIED].

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on PM1-hash-sources. Feeds PM1-spec-extraction (the SlidingWindowLlamaAttention section) and the E-P1 `rswa.rs` ring buffer. Coupled to OQ-1/OQ-2.

title: End-to-end CLI test script: focr ocr <golden image> --json → compare to frozen reference, full structured logging
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
This is the headline e2e the user asked for: an end-to-end CLI test that runs the REAL `focr` binary on a golden image, emits `--json`, and compares against a frozen reference — with full detailed logging at every stage. It is the integration test that proves the whole pipeline (decode→preprocess→tokenize→vision→connector→prefill→decode→postprocess→emit) actually works end-to-end on the native path, not just per-op parity. No mocks: real binary, real golden image, real frozen reference JSON (per `/testing-perfect-e2e-integration-tests-with-logging-and-no-mocks`).

## WHAT TO DO
Deliver `tests/native_engine_e2e.rs` (the Rust e2e, model-gated) AND `scripts/run_e2e.sh` (the standalone CLI script):
1. **`scripts/run_e2e.sh`**: resolves the model (env `FOCR_MODEL_DIR`), runs `focr ocr tests/fixtures/golden_corpus/<doc>.png --json` for each golden doc, pipes output to a comparator that diffs against `tests/fixtures/native/<doc>_reference.json` after canonicalization (scrub timing/run-id/durations, sort bbox, normalize line endings). Emits a structured NDJSON summary per doc and a final pass/fail. Exit 0 on all-pass; non-zero on any diff. Skips-green (exit 0, logged) if no model resolvable.
2. **`tests/native_engine_e2e.rs`**: the same flow as a Rust test using TEST-model-gated-runner — invokes the real binary or `OcrEngine::recognize`, asserts `native_path_ran=true`, compares to the frozen reference (text exact where the bf16 oracle is deterministic over its reproduced prefix; logits/continuous values within the E-VERIFY documented tolerance), and asserts determinism (same image+args twice → byte-identical under greedy).
3. **Full per-stage logging**: at EACH pipeline stage emit a `TestLog` `stage` line with inputs/shapes/dtype/simd_tier/elapsed_us — e.g. preprocess logs the tile geometry (Base 1024×1024 vs Gundam) and the [-1,1] normalize; tokenize logs token count; vision logs the 256 image-feature tokens + the 273 placeholder-token total (16 image + 1 image_newline per row × 16 rows + 1 view_seperator) at base 1024 (OQ-18 census); prefill logs reference-block length `m`; decode logs per-N-tokens TPS and the no_repeat_ngram(35) window (128 single-image / 1024 multi-image); postprocess logs EOS strip + bbox /999 rescale.
4. **Cover both modes**: Base (1024×1024, crop_mode=false, multi-page) and Gundam (base_size=1024, image_size=640, crop_mode=true, single-page tiling) — each against its own frozen reference.
5. **Multi-page e2e**: a 10-page golden, comparing to the multi-page reference (which is cross-page DEPENDENT under R-SWA, OQ-13 — the reference is a single `infer_multi` oracle run, NOT a concatenation of single-page parses).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **Real binary, real fixtures, no mocks** — an e2e that stubs the engine proves nothing.
- **`--json` is the compared surface** (stable, structured) — human markdown is a rendering of it.
- **Per-stage logging makes a failure diagnosable**: if the e2e diffs, the structured log pinpoints WHICH stage's shapes/tokens diverged, not just "output differs."
- **Both modes + multi-page** because the cost center and the token census differ (Base = 256 tokens/page; Gundam crops ≈ 100 tokens each; multi-page is cross-page dependent).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- **Determinism only holds under `temperature=0` greedy** (§7.3) — assert byte-identical only in that mode.
- **L4 'exact' is defined only over the prefix the bf16 oracle reproduces identically** (§8.2) — compare text exactly only up to the nondeterminism-envelope boundary carried in the fixture; beyond it, fall back to CER-within-budget.
- **Do NOT assert multi-page == sum of single-page** (§8.3, OQ-13) — the metamorphic property is the opposite (page order may change later-page output).
- Robot/JSON output may carry run-id/timing → scrub before compare (canonicalization from TEST-fixture-harness).
- Script must work both in CI (model absent → skip-green) and locally (model present → real compare).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `scripts/run_e2e.sh` runs the real `focr` over each golden, compares to frozen reference, exits 0 all-pass / non-zero on diff, skips-green without a model.
- `tests/native_engine_e2e.rs` asserts `native_path_ran=true`, frozen-reference match (text exact over the deterministic prefix; continuous within tolerance), and determinism.
- Both Base and Gundam modes covered; a 10-page multi-page e2e present.
- Every stage emits a valid structured NDJSON log line; a failing run produces a log that localizes the diverging stage.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- The e2e itself is the test; additionally a self-test that a deliberately-perturbed reference makes the comparator FAIL (proves it actually compares).
- A self-test that the script skips-green without a model.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
- depends_on **TEST-model-gated-runner**: uses it to gate + prove the native path ran.
- depends_on **TEST-fixture-harness**: loads the frozen `<doc>_reference.json` + canonicalizes before compare.
- depends_on **TEST-log-emitter**: emits the per-stage structured logs.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## REVIEW-2 ADDENDUM — error-path e2e (the §7.4 exit-code contract), piping + help smoke
- **Error-path e2e through the REAL binary (currently only the happy path is covered).** The §7.4 exit codes are a PUBLIC contract that agents branch on; the e2e must assert them END-TO-END by invoking `focr` and checking the process exit code AND the `robot run_error` payload code agree: (a) a missing/unresolvable model → **exit 3** with an actionable searched-dirs message; (b) a corrupt/truncated image → **exit 4**; (c) a corrupt or wrong-`format_version` `.focrq` → **exit 7**; (d) a stage budget exceeded (`FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_*_MS` set tiny) → **exit 5**; (e) a SIGINT/Ctrl-C mid-run → **exit 6** with finalizer cleanup. These are real binary invocations (no mocks) and several need NO weights (3/4/7 fire before the forward) so they run in the always-on no-weights lane — a rare chance for the e2e to be meaningful WITHOUT the 6.67 GB model.
- **Robot/piping + help/version smoke.** Add a smoke that `focr ocr <golden> --json | <jq-style parse>` yields one JSON object (data-only on stdout, diagnostics on stderr, exit 0) and that `focr --help` / `focr --version` / `focr robot schema` emit stable, parseable output — the agent-ergonomic surface the README/AGENTS.md promise. Scrub timing/run-id before any golden compare (canonicalization from TEST-fixture-harness).
- **Exit-code/robot parity assertion.** For each error case assert `process_exit_code == robot_run_error.payload.code == FocrError::exit_code()` (one source of truth, per P0-error-exit-codes) so the three can never silently diverge.
notes: 2026-06-25 Codex correction: any phrase like 'Base = 256 tokens/page' in this generated bead means 256 image-feature tokens only. For token/KV sizing use the OQ-18 census: base 1024 has 256 image-feature tokens plus structural slots (16 image_newline + 1 view_seperator = 273 before prompt), and the R-SWA reference block grows with page/input length up to the 32K cap. Do not size buffers from 256 alone.

title: GOT decode: reuse per-step Mat/Vec buffers (gemv+misc ~6.4s) instead of allocating ~12 Vecs/layer/token
description: bd-2dlz left the decode 'gemv+misc' at ~6.35s for page_0107 (688 tok). The int8 gemvs themselves are bandwidth-bound at the arch ceiling (kernel-map confirmed), but each qwen2_decode_step allocates ~12 fresh Vec/Mat per layer (normed, xq, qkv, q, k, ctx, attn, h, normed2, gate, up, down) × 24 layers × 688 tokens ≈ 200K allocs. Also refine_topk_f32 allocs a Vec<u32>[vocab] per token — could reuse. Low ROI vs the big levers but pure lossless.

title: Per-module unit-test scaffolding standard (happy/edge/error + structured logging) every module author follows
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
AGENTS.md Testing Policy: "Each module includes unit tests for happy path, edge cases, error handling." Without a documented, copy-pasteable standard, module authors (preprocess, tokenizer, vision_sam, vision_clip, decoder, rswa, moe, decode, postprocess, weights, robot, storage, etc.) each invent their own shape, logging drifts, and the unit-test floor erodes. This bead defines the ONE scaffolding standard + a template so every per-module test suite is uniform, richly logged, and reviewable.

## WHAT TO DO
Deliver `docs/UNIT_TEST_STANDARD.md` + a `tests/_template_module_tests.rs.txt` template:
1. **Three mandatory groups per module**: `happy_*` (nominal path on representative input), `edge_*` (boundary: empty input, max dims, the i32-overflow worst case at K=6848 for int8 GEMM modules, single-token decode, 40-page context), `error_*` (malformed input, missing weight, shape mismatch, format/version mismatch → asserts the right `FocrError` + exit-code mapping per §7.4).
2. **Structured logging in EVERY test** via `TestLog` (bead TEST-log-emitter): log `setup`, each `stage` with shapes/dtype/simd_tier/elapsed, and `result`.
3. **Determinism assertion** where applicable: same input twice → identical output (uses the shared helper from TEST-determinism-gate).
4. **SIMD-tier coverage note**: kernel modules must run their tests across available tiers (force via `FOCR_FORCE_ARCH`) and assert the scalar fallback is bit-identical to the active SIMD path (except AVX2, which carries its own overflow proof — see §6.6 ⚠).
5. **The overflow proof obligation** (AGENTS.md doctrine #6, §5.4): any module doing int8 i32-accumulation includes a test multiplying worst-case saturated operands at **K = 6848** (dense layer-0 `down_proj`) on every arch, asserting the i32 result equals an i64 reference and no path silently saturates. (Worst cases: S8S8 ≤ 110.4M, U8S8 ≤ 221.7M at K=6848; ≥9× headroom under i32::MAX=2,147,483,647 — but PROVEN, not assumed. Do NOT inherit frankensearch's k≤1536 bound.)

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **A template, not just prose**, because authors copy-paste; the path of least resistance must be the correct shape.
- **Overflow proof is a UNIT-test obligation in the standard** so no int8 module ships without it (the proof is per-module, the standard makes it mandatory).
- **SIMD-tier coverage in the standard** so bit-identity (integer accumulation is exact/associative → SIMD == scalar exactly) is verified everywhere, and the AVX2 i16-saturation exception is explicitly called out as needing its own proof or a `DISCREPANCIES.md` entry.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- The standard must not mandate the 6.67 GB model for unit tests — unit tests use tiny synthetic tensors; the model-gated path is for e2e only.
- `FOCR_FORCE_ARCH` forcing must degrade gracefully on a host lacking an intrinsic (the scalar fallback always cross-compiles and runs).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `docs/UNIT_TEST_STANDARD.md` + template exist; the three groups + logging + determinism + SIMD-tier + overflow-proof obligations are documented with concrete examples.
- At least one module (e.g. the int8 linear facade in `nn.rs`) ships a reference implementation of the standard as the worked example.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- The worked-example module's test suite passes and emits valid structured logs (validated against TEST-log-conventions).
- The K=6848 overflow proof passes on every available arch in the worked example.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
- depends_on **TEST-log-emitter**: the standard mandates logging via that emitter.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## REVIEW-2 ADDENDUM — shared SIMD-tier enumeration helper, snapshot + table-driven conventions
- **Provide a shared `for_each_available_arch_tier(|tier| …)` helper, don't make each author hand-roll `FOCR_FORCE_ARCH`.** The standard mandates kernel modules run tests across tiers and assert scalar==SIMD bit-identity, but offers no plumbing — every author re-implementing the tier sweep guarantees drift. Add (or reference, from `tests/common/`) one helper that enumerates the tiers available on the host (`scalar` always; `sdot`/`smmla`/`vnni256`/`vnni512`/`amx`/`avx2` as detected), forces each via `FOCR_FORCE_ARCH`, runs the supplied closure, and logs a `stage` line per tier with `simd_tier`. The AVX2 i16-saturation exception is encoded ONCE in the helper (it asserts equality-modulo-the-documented-DISC, not raw equality) so no author gets it wrong.
- **Module-level snapshot (insta) + table-driven conventions.** §8.6 uses insta exact-snapshots for `--json`/help; the unit standard should also bless insta module-level snapshots for structured outputs (e.g. a tokenizer's id sequence, a postprocess markdown assembly) and a table-driven `cases: &[(input, expected)]` shape for the `happy_/edge_/error_` groups, so edge enumeration is uniform and reviewable. Reference the proptest generators from TEST-r2-property-fuzz for the randomized edge cases (the K=6848 overflow operands, random valid/invalid `.focrq` headers) rather than ad-hoc literals.
- **Determinism + tier helper in the worked example.** The worked-example int8-linear module must demonstrate BOTH the determinism helper (TEST-determinism-gate) AND the tier-sweep helper, so the path of least resistance copies both.

title: GOT decode: lm_head re-transposed the 622MB tied-embedding every token (95% of decode); precompute once, 487s to 41s page, bit-identical
description:
SYMPTOM: `focr ocr` with got-ocr2.int8.focrq took ~8 min/page (page_0107: 487s). User: "that's HORRIBLE ... you must do better".

DIAGNOSIS (FOCR_TIMING instrumentation added to got::recognize + generate_greedy_kvcache): the O(n)-per-token KV-cache decode itself was fine (layers 12s, attn 4.9s, gemv 7.6s); vision 5.8s. The bottleneck was the lm_head: 463.7s of 487s (95%). Root cause: decoder::lm_head_proj -> decoder::linear_no_bias TRANSPOSES the entire [vocab=151860, hidden=1024] tied embedding (~0.6 GB) from scratch on EVERY call, and the decode step calls it once per generated token (688 tokens). ~688 x ~0.9s strided 622MB transpose = ~590s.

FIX (bit-identical, doctrine #1/#2 safe -- lm_head stays F32, NOT quantized): precompute the transposed [hidden, vocab] head weight ONCE in GotDecodeWeights::build; new decoder::norm_and_lm_head_pretransposed(hidden, norm_w, head_wt, eps) does rms_norm + the SAME nn::matmul against the pre-transposed Mat. The one-shot seeding prefill keeps the naive path.

RESULT (page_0107, M4, got-ocr2.int8.focrq): total 487s -> 41s (11.9x); decode 1.4 -> 23.9 tok/s (17x); lm_head 463.7s -> 16.2s (28.7x, now memory-bound reading the 622MB embed/token). OUTPUT byte-identical (cmp -s, OUTPUT_IDENTICAL=yes) so the parity / L4-oracle cert is unaffected.

Evidence: artifacts/perf/<this-bead>/ (perf_before.log, perf_after.log, README.md, SHA256SUMS). Kept a permanent FOCR_TIMING stage breakdown (negligible always-on relaxed-atomic accumulators).
