title: Determinism gate + many_pages_without_deadlock watchdog + asupersync capacity certificate
description:
# Determinism gate + concurrency watchdog + capacity certificate

## BACKGROUND / WHY
Two failure classes are catastrophic and silent: nondeterministic output (same image → different parse, breaking reproducibility and every golden) and a concurrency deadlock under many pages (the frankensearch deadlock saga burned 5 commits). This bead is the gate that proves franken_ocr is deterministic and does not hang — both are release-blocking properties distinct from oracle parity (L4 is 'match the reference', this is 'match yourself / don't hang').

## WHAT TO DO
- **Determinism gate**: a separate gate asserting same-input-twice → byte-identical output under greedy (independent of the oracle; this is self-consistency).
- **`many_pages_without_deadlock` CI watchdog**: pages ≫ pool — the test HANGS on regression. This is the durable fix the frankensearch deadlock saga converged on: single `OcrModel` behind a cache; SEQUENTIAL outer page/document loop; each forward fans out across all cores internally via the kernel's OWN rayon pool (pinned to physical cores, ONE live forward at a time). NEVER nest rayon under a held lock; NEVER nest a second asupersync runtime inside a task.
- **asupersync capacity certificate** (gauntlet artifact): p95/p99 queueing evidence + a proof of NO nested-runtime / NO rayon-pool oversubscription (the USL pool caps of §6.9 / AF-5 hold under the `many_pages` soak); streaming uses BOUNDED channels (backpressure, never unbounded growth).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Determinism is a SEPARATE gate from L4: L4 matches the (possibly noisy) oracle over its reproducible prefix; the determinism gate demands WE are byte-identical to ourselves — a stronger, oracle-independent property.
- The watchdog HANGS (rather than fails fast) on regression because a deadlock IS a hang — a timeout wrapper turns the hang into a CI failure with the offending thread dump.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- 'Streaming per-page' = streaming the OUTPUT of a sequentially-processed page, NEVER concurrent forwards (which oversubscribe rayon N×).
- The capacity certificate must prove the USL pool caps (decode GEMV peak ~8–16 effective cores bandwidth-bound; not 64) hold — oversubscribing 64 cores is β-dominated slowdown.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Determinism gate green: same image+args → byte-identical output under greedy.
- `many_pages_without_deadlock` watchdog passes (pages ≫ pool, no hang) under a timeout wrapper.
- Capacity certificate produced: p95/p99 queueing + no-nested-runtime + no-oversubscription proof under the `many_pages` soak; bounded channels verified.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- A determinism test running each golden image twice and asserting byte-identical output.
- The `many_pages_without_deadlock` watchdog (pages ≫ pool) under a wall-clock timeout.
- A capacity-certificate test emitting p95/p99 + the oversubscription/nesting proof as a structured artifact.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on the token/decode path being runnable (L4). Consumed-by VERIFY-three-pillar-cert (determinism is a scorecard cell; the capacity certificate is a gauntlet artifact).
close_reason: All three halves green — see the full evidence on the first close attempt (blocked then; deps bd-2ub2/bd-1lx3 now closed): (1) determinism gate shared harness (bd-3kge) adopted by e2e + metamorphic, armed byte-identical incl FOCR_THREADS axis; (2) watchdog suite green + injected-hang detector + live 256-page over-budget trip demo; (3) capacity certificate focr-capacity-certificate/v1 — ARMED HEAVY (GOT int8, 48 real forwards): p50/p95/p99 = 6.83/7.41/9.58 s/page, 48/48 Ok, kernel pool width stable 10→10 (kernel_pool_width pub accessor), watchdogged 333s; fast mode: backpressure PROVEN (max in-flight = capacity = 4, bound cap+1 never exceeded); bounded channels verified LIVE; no-nested-runtime via watchdogged completion + single engine + sequential producer + scenario-1b gauge. title: Tests: L0-L5 ladder integration runner + per-gate structured scorecard fixture
description:
# L0–L5 ladder integration runner + scorecard

## BACKGROUND / WHY
The individual ladder gates (L0..L5) need a single integration runner that executes them in order, short-circuits sensibly (a failed L0 makes L1+ meaningless), and emits one structured scorecard the release process and per-commit parity-receipt consume. This is the operational face of 'L0–L5 parity all green' that appears in every phase exit gate.

## WHAT TO DO
- An integration runner `tests/conformance_harness.rs` that executes L0→L5 in order over the golden corpus, recording per-gate pass/fail + the measured metric (exact/cosine/logit-diff/CER/TEDS).
- Emit a structured scorecard fixture (`{gate, granularity, tolerance, measured, pass}`) consumed by the parity-receipt every perf commit re-states.
- Model-gated: skip-with-SUCCESS without the 6.67 GB weights; prove the native path ran by pointing any fallback at `/nonexistent`.
- The runner is the single entry the phase exit gates and the three-pillar conformance pillar call.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- A single ordered runner (not 6 independent tests) so the parity receipt is one artifact and a lower-gate failure is reported clearly rather than as 6 confusing failures.
- Structured scorecard so the conformal ratchet and the three-pillar cert can consume per-category results directly.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Must re-prove on EVERY perf commit (the §9.2 loop re-proves L0–L5 each lever) — keep it fast enough to run in the optimization loop.
- Skip-with-SUCCESS must still PROVE the native path ran (the `/nonexistent` fallback trick) so a silently-skipped suite is not mistaken for a pass.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The runner executes L0–L5 over the corpus and emits the structured scorecard.
- Per-commit parity receipt derivable from the scorecard (e.g. 'text exact, max logit diff 0.05, deterministic').
- Skip-with-SUCCESS without weights; native-path-ran proof present.

## TESTS REQUIRED
This IS the integration test bead — it composes L0..L5 and asserts the all-green condition, with full structured logging.

Depends on all four ladder gates (VERIFY-ladder-l0, -l1-l2, -l3-l4, -l5). Consumed-by VERIFY-determinism-gate (needs the token/decode path), VERIFY-three-pillar-cert, and VERIFY-conformal-ratchet.

title: Oracle nondeterminism-floor characterization (run-twice / two-thread-counts envelope) — sets all downstream tolerances
description:
# Oracle nondeterminism-floor characterization

## BACKGROUND / WHY
The HF reference is FREQUENTLY non-deterministic across torch thread counts / BLAS reduction order at the logit-tie level (bf16 arithmetic, 129280-vocab argmax). If we set parity tolerances WITHOUT first measuring the oracle's own noise, we will chase phantom 'bugs' that are just the oracle disagreeing with itself — or, worse, set tolerances so loose that real drift hides inside them. This task is the keystone that makes every L1/L3/L4 tolerance defensible rather than guessed. It directly serves 'correctness before speed': a franken_ocr int8 divergence INSIDE the oracle's own bf16 noise is NOT a bug, and we must be able to prove that.

## WHAT TO DO
Before setting ANY tolerance:
- Run the oracle **twice** over the full golden corpus, and at **two thread counts** (e.g. `torch.set_num_threads(8)` and `(32)`), with `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` where it does not error.
- Diff the runs and record the **nondeterminism envelope** as a committed fixture: per-token divergence rate, first-divergence position per document, and the per-logit max-abs spread at matching positions.
- Derive: (a) the **L4 'exact' prefix** = the longest decoded-token prefix the oracle reproduces identically across all runs/threads, per document; (b) the **L3 logit tolerance** = derived from the measured oracle logit variance (NOT the imported frankensearch `0.055`).
- Commit `tests/fixtures/oracle_nondeterminism_envelope.json` and a `tolerances.toml` consumed by the ladder gates.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- L4 exactness is defined ONLY over the reproducible prefix; beyond it, the oracle is non-deterministic and we cannot demand bit-exactness.
- The per-op ULP tolerance table (default 4 ULP f32 matmul, 2 ULP elementwise) is the L1/L2 comparator — but the END-TO-END logit/token tolerances are derived here from measured variance, not a hand-guessed epsilon.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- If the oracle is wildly non-deterministic (large divergence rate), that is itself a finding to ledger — it may mean greedy temperature=0.0 still hits ties; record and pick the longest stable prefix.
- Must be re-run if the pinned model source changes (CI-guarded against drift via the E-PM1 census).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `oracle_nondeterminism_envelope.json` committed with per-document divergence rate + first-divergence position + logit spread.
- `tolerances.toml` committed: L1/L2 ULP table, L3 logit tolerance (derived), L4 exact-prefix bounds — all sourced to measured numbers.
- A short note in `docs/DISCREPANCIES.md` if the floor reveals any structural nondeterminism.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- A regression test asserting the derived tolerances are present and internally consistent (L3 ≥ measured spread, L4 prefix ≤ document length).
- Structured logging of the envelope computation per document.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on VERIFY-oracle-harness (needs the oracle to run twice/two-thread). This task BLOCKS all the L1–L5 ladder gates, which consume `tolerances.toml`.

title: Test-only PyO3/subprocess oracle bridge with deterministic-algorithms + per-op ULP tolerance table + EngineIdentity
description:
# Test-only oracle bridge (PyO3 / subprocess) — ML-System-class wiring

## BACKGROUND / WHY
Frozen `.npy` fixtures cover the committed golden corpus, but per-op differential testing (Pattern 1 of `/testing-conformance-harnesses`) is the gold standard and needs a LIVE bridge to the pinned reference for ad-hoc inputs. This bridge is what lets a kernel author diff a single op against the oracle without regenerating the whole fixture set. It serves correctness-before-speed by making oracle comparison cheap enough to run on every kernel change.

## WHAT TO DO
- Build a **test-only** PyO3 or subprocess bridge to the pinned reference (`torch==2.10.0`, `transformers==4.57.1`).
- Force `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`; capture the seeded RNG per call.
- Provide a **per-op ULP tolerance table** as the L1/L2 comparator: default **4 ULP for f32 matmul, 2 ULP for elementwise** — this is the comparator, NOT a hand-guessed epsilon.
- Define `EngineIdentity::{Subject, Oracle}` and assert them **distinct** so the oracle is never accidentally compared against itself.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- **NEVER linked into the shipping `focr` inference binary** — gated behind a test-only feature/dev-dependency so G3's no-FFI runtime claim holds.
- subprocess is acceptable if PyO3 linkage is fragile across the 5 build targets; the bridge only needs to run on the dev/CI host with the reference env.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- The bridge must not leak a torch runtime into the release artifact — a build test asserts `focr` links no Python.
- ULP comparisons must account for the oracle's measured nondeterminism floor (VERIFY-nondeterminism-floor): a 4-ULP table is the per-op default but end-to-end tolerances come from the measured envelope.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Bridge runs per-op diffs against the reference with the ULP table comparator.
- `EngineIdentity::Subject != Oracle` asserted in the harness.
- Build test proves `focr` (release) links no Python/torch.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- A smoke test diffing a trivial op (e.g. RMSNorm on a fixed input) Subject-vs-Oracle within the ULP table.
- A linkage test asserting the shipping binary is FFI-free.
- Structured logging of every op-diff (`{op, max_ulp, within_tolerance}`).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on VERIFY-oracle-harness (the reference env) and VERIFY-nondeterminism-floor (tolerance derivation).

title: L0 preprocessing parity gate — resized/normalized/padded tensor + tile geometry, EXACT
description:
# L0 — preprocessing parity gate (EXACT)

## BACKGROUND / WHY
L0 is the bottom rung of the parity ladder. If preprocessing diverges, every downstream stage is fed a different tensor and all higher gates become meaningless. Preprocessing is deterministic integer/float arithmetic with no quantization, so it MUST be exact. This gate is a prerequisite for P1 (fp32 parity).

## WHAT TO DO
Gate the preprocess front end output against the oracle's preprocessed tensor, **exact**:
- **Normalize**: `image_mean = image_std = [0.5,0.5,0.5]` → pixels scaled to [0,1] then `(x-0.5)/0.5` → **[-1,1]**, CHW layout.
- **Pad to square with gray (127,127,127)** = `tuple(int(m*255))`, aspect preserved (`ImageOps.pad` equivalent).
- **Tile geometry**: `patch_size=16`, `downsample_ratio=4`, `num_queries = ceil((image_size//patch_size)/downsample_ratio)`. Two modes: **Base** (1024×1024, `crop_mode=false`) and **Gundam** (`base_size=1024`, `image_size=640`, `crop_mode=true`, global padded 1024 view `global_view_pos='head'` + 640×640 local crops via `dynamic_preprocess()` / `find_closest_aspect_ratio()` over `i*j ∈ [min_num,max_num]`).
- Ratio selection (`find_closest_aspect_ratio`), gray pad value, and the [-1,1] normalize must all match exactly.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- EXACT tolerance (not cosine): preprocessing is reproducible arithmetic, any drift is a bug.
- The tile census (token counts per mode/aspect-ratio) is asserted against the E-PM1 machine-readable census, the source of truth.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Gundam multi-tile token totals per aspect ratio are **[OPEN, OQ-18/OQ-7]** — this gate cannot finalize the Gundam geometry assertions until those are resolved.
- Bicubic pos-embed interpolation (for non-1024/tiled inputs) is a separate frankentorch GAP (f32 build) — L0 covers the resize/pad/normalize; the interp correctness is checked at L1/L2.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Base-mode preprocessed tensor exact-equal to the oracle's (bitwise on the f32 array).
- Gundam-mode tile geometry + per-tile token counts match the census once OQ-7/OQ-18 are resolved.
- Gray pad value, [-1,1] normalize, ratio selection all exact.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit tests per preprocess submodule (resize/pad/normalize/tile) with golden tensors.
- An integration test feeding the golden corpus through preprocess and diffing exact vs oracle, with structured per-image logging (`{image, mode, tile_count, max_abs_diff, exact}`).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on VERIFY-oracle-harness (golden preprocessed tensors) and VERIFY-tokenizer-conformance (the prompt side of the input contract must be token-id-exact first, an L0 prerequisite). The geometry assertions consume the E-PM1 census and are gated on OQ-7/OQ-18.

title: L1 per-op + L2 per-layer parity gates — cosine ≈ 1.0, max-abs-diff ledgered
description:
# L1 (per-op) + L2 (per-layer) parity gates

## BACKGROUND / WHY
L1/L2 catch kernel drift at the finest granularity the oracle exposes. A correct end-to-end answer can hide a compensating pair of per-op bugs; per-op/per-layer cosine pins each kernel to the reference. These are the gates every kernel bead in P1/P2/P3 re-proves on each change — they are the operational form of 'every fused op must stay at peak AND correct.'

## WHAT TO DO
- **L1 per-op**: each kernel's output vs the oracle activation. Tolerance **cosine ≈ 1.0 (≥ 0.9999 in f32; documented int8 tolerance)**. Comparator uses the per-op ULP table (4 ULP f32 matmul / 2 ULP elementwise) for the bridge path.
- **L2 per-layer**: per decoder-layer hidden state (all 12) and per vision-stage output (post-patch-embed, post-SAM, post-bridge/compress, post-CLIP, post-projector, post-connector). Tolerance **cosine ≈ 1.0; max-abs-diff LEDGERED** per layer.
- Both consume the frozen `.npy` dumps from VERIFY-oracle-harness AND can use the live VERIFY-oracle-bridge for ad-hoc inputs.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Cosine ≈ 1.0 (not bit-exact) because f32-vs-bf16 and int8-vs-bf16 are continuous-value divergences within a documented tolerance.
- max-abs-diff is LEDGERED (recorded) per layer so a slow drift across layers is visible, not just the final cosine.
- A wrong SAM window size or windowed-block pos-embed scheme (OQ-15) surfaces ONLY as a fuzzy L2 cosine drop — L2 must therefore log per-stage cosine so this silent-corruption failure mode is caught.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- int8 tolerances must sit inside the oracle nondeterminism floor (VERIFY-nondeterminism-floor) — an int8 divergence inside the oracle's own bf16 noise is not a bug.
- The projector concat order (OQ-6) and SAM window (OQ-15) are [OPEN]; a wrong answer passes L0 but fails L2 — so L2 must run per-vision-stage, not just on the final hidden.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Every implemented kernel passes L1 cosine ≥ 0.9999 (f32) / within documented int8 tolerance.
- All 12 decoder-layer hiddens + all 6 vision-stage outputs pass L2 cosine ≈ 1.0 with max-abs-diff ledgered.
- Per-stage cosine logged so OQ-15/OQ-6 misimplementations are caught.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Per-op unit tests (one per kernel) diffing against the frozen oracle activation.
- A per-layer integration test producing a structured table (`{stage, cosine, max_abs_diff}`) for the full forward, committed as a golden-fuzzy artifact.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on VERIFY-oracle-harness (per-layer dumps), VERIFY-nondeterminism-floor (tolerance derivation), VERIFY-oracle-bridge (live per-op diffs). Consumed-by every P1/P2/P3 kernel bead.

LADDER_HARNESS.md marks L1/L2 wired. Decoder layers 00-10 are not individually isolatable (no public single-layer entry) — the 12-layer stack is ledgered via L4 prefill-hidden vs decoder_layer_11_hidden, documented in-rung.

title: L3 logits + L4 token parity gates — logits within derived tolerance + argmax match; decoded tokens EXACT on reproducible prefix
description:
# L3 (logits) + L4 (token) parity gates

## BACKGROUND / WHY
L3/L4 are where quantization risk is actually adjudicated. L3 bounds the continuous logit divergence; L4 demands the discrete decoded token sequence be exact where the reference is deterministic. This is the gate that says 'int8/int4 did not change what the model says.' It is the heart of G1 for the decoder and the gate P2/P4 must clear.

## WHAT TO DO
- **L3 logits**: pre-sampling logits within the int8/int4 quant tolerance DERIVED from the oracle nondeterminism floor (NOT the imported frankensearch `max_diff ~0.055` — that is a precedent value, the real number comes from VERIFY-nondeterminism-floor). **argmax MUST match** at every position where the reference is deterministic.
- **L4 token**: the decoded token sequence is **EXACT under greedy where the reference is deterministic** — and 'where deterministic' is defined ONLY over the reproducible prefix established by VERIFY-nondeterminism-floor.
- Replicate the exact sampler semantics: greedy / low-temp argmax, strip trailing EOS `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>`, and `no_repeat_ngram_size=35` with a sliding `ngram_window` that DIFFERS by mode — **128 (single-image) vs 1024 (multi-image)** (these are first-class generation semantics; the `SlidingWindowNoRepeatNgramProcessor` bans repeated 35-grams within the window).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Discrete output bit-exact, continuous (logits) only within documented tolerance — the frankensearch `parity_logits_and_ranking_match_reference` shape.
- A separate determinism gate (VERIFY-determinism-gate) asserts same-input-twice → identical output; L4 is about matching the ORACLE, the determinism gate is about matching OURSELVES.
- The ngram window per mode is a generation semantic, not a CLI flag — the sampler must replicate the exact window or L4 diverges on repetition-prone content.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- The 129280-vocab argmax has logit ties at the bf16 level; argmax-match is only demanded where the oracle itself is stable (the reproducible prefix).
- int8 on `lm_head` (P2 stage 2c) and int8 attention (2b) go BEYOND the validated NVFP4/GGUF set — L3/L4 are the gate that retires that risk (OQ-14); a regression reverts just that stage via its kill-switch (`FOCR_INT8_LMHEAD`, `FOCR_INT8_ATTN`).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- L3: logits within the derived tolerance; argmax matches on every deterministic position.
- L4: decoded tokens EXACT over the reproducible prefix under greedy.
- Every perf commit re-states its parity receipt (e.g. 'text exact, max logit diff 0.05, deterministic').

## TESTS REQUIRED
- A logits diff test producing `{position, max_logit_diff, argmax_match}` per token.
- A token-exact test over the reproducible prefix per document, structured-logged.
- An ngram-window test asserting the per-mode window (128 single / 1024 multi) bans the right 35-grams.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on VERIFY-oracle-harness (golden logits/tokens) and VERIFY-nondeterminism-floor (derives the L3 tolerance and the L4 reproducible prefix). Consumed-by P2/P4 quant beads.
close_reason: Done (design/harness wave, committed): see docs/alien|gauntlet|conformance|testing + scripts/af*.py

title: L5 end-to-end OCR parity gate — decoded text + bbox on golden corpus; CER/TEDS/Formula-CDM within documented budget
description:
# L5 — end-to-end OCR parity gate

## BACKGROUND / WHY
L5 is the top of the ladder and the only gate a non-expert can read: does franken_ocr produce the same document parse as the reference? It is the operational definition of G1. The lower gates can all be green and L5 still catch a postprocess bug (tag parsing, bbox rescale, markdown assembly). L5 is the gate that releases depend on.

## WHAT TO DO
- Compare decoded text + bbox tags on the frozen golden corpus.
- **exact-match where the reference is deterministic** (the reproducible-prefix discipline).
- Aggregate **CER / TEDS / Formula-CDM within a documented quantization budget**: target **int8 within noise** of bf16 (NVFP4's 'identical to BF16' as the bar); **int4 within a small ledgered budget**, with **no catastrophic regression on dense numeric/table content**.
- Postprocess parity: EOS strip (`<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>`), `<|ref|>…<|/ref|><|det|>…<|/det|>` regex parse, bbox coords `/999 → ×W/H` rescale, markdown assembly (HTML tables, LaTeX formulas, `<page>` separators for multi-page).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- CER/TEDS/Formula-CDM are aggregate metrics with a DOCUMENTED budget, not exact — quantization is allowed a measured, ledgered tolerance, but exact-token content (dense numbers, tables, code, sub/superscripts) is held to a tighter tail bound (see VERIFY-tail-risk / AF-2).
- The metrics: CER (character error rate), TEDS / TEDS-S (table structure), Formula-CDM (LaTeX) — the reference's own reported strengths (printed text Text-Edit 0.038, tables TEDS 90.93, math Formula-CDM 92.61).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Multi-page is CROSS-PAGE DEPENDENT under R-SWA (OQ-13) — L5 multi-page comparison must be against the multi-page reference output, NEVER a sum of single-page parses.
- The full prompt-mode taxonomy (free OCR / layout / grounding / markdown) and whether bboxes are emitted in all modes is [OPEN, OQ-8] — L5 bbox assertions are gated on that.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Decoded text exact where deterministic; aggregate CER/TEDS/Formula-CDM within the ledgered budget (int8 within noise, int4 within small budget).
- No catastrophic regression on dense numeric/table content (checked via the tail-risk monitor).
- Postprocess (EOS, tag regex, bbox rescale, markdown) matches the reference.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- End-to-end test over the golden corpus producing a structured scorecard (`{doc, CER, TEDS, Formula_CDM, text_exact}`).
- A postprocess unit suite (tag regex, bbox /999 rescale, EOS strip).
- Model-gated: skip-with-SUCCESS without weights; prove the native path ran by pointing fallbacks at `/nonexistent`.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on VERIFY-oracle-harness (golden e2e outputs), VERIFY-ladder-l3-l4 (tokens must match before text can), and VERIFY-golden-artifacts (the frozen `focr ocr --json` snapshots). Multi-page assertions gated on OQ-13; bbox-mode assertions on OQ-8.
close_reason: Done-in-code (verified 2026-07-06, force: blockers bd-29wv/bd-re8.11 themselves done-in-code): l5_end_to_end_cer_budget @ 0.01, model-gated, CER 0.0 on both fixture pages; postprocess parity complete. TEDS/Formula-CDM aggregate residual rides the gauntlet + corpus beads per the measured-budget doctrine.

title: Tokenizer conformance (OQ-16) — token-id-exact byte-level-BPE vs LlamaTokenizerFast, the L0/L4 prerequisite
description:
# Tokenizer conformance (OQ-16)

## BACKGROUND / WHY
The tokenizer is the single highest-leverage correctness prerequisite: **a wrong token id corrupts EVERY downstream gate** (L0 input, L4 output, and everything between). The plan calls this out explicitly as an L0/L4 prerequisite that must pass before any decoder parity work. franken_ocr ships a pure-Rust byte-level BPE over `tokenizer.json` (no SentencePiece) and must be token-id-exact against `LlamaTokenizerFast`.

## WHAT TO DO
- Build a dedicated exact-match conformance corpus: diverse Unicode, CJK, math, code, the DeepSeek glyph specials, and the structural specials `<image>` / `<|ref|>` / `<|det|>`.
- Round-trip `encode` → `decode` against `LlamaTokenizerFast` over `tokenizer.json` (9.98 MB, vocab **129280**, ~512 special tokens). [VERIFIED]: `LlamaTokenizerFast`, byte-level BPE; bos/eos/pad = 0/1/2; `add_special_token=false`, `image_token='<image>'`, `ignore_id=-100`.
- Verify: pre-tokenizer regex, byte-fallback, special-token handling, DeepSeek-glyph handling (e.g. `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>`).
- **Freeze the reference id sequences as golden fixtures.**

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Token-id-EXACT (not fuzzy) — there is no tolerance for tokenization; an off-by-one id is a different model input.
- Pure-Rust HF-tokenizers-JSON path, no SentencePiece dependency (G3 single static binary).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- The pre-tokenizer regex and byte-fallback are the classic divergence sources between a hand-rolled BPE and `LlamaTokenizerFast`; the corpus must exercise multi-byte UTF-8 boundaries, combining characters, and the DeepSeek glyph specials.
- OQ-16 (the exact byte-level-BPE encode/decode semantics: pre-tokenizer regex, byte-fallback, special-token + glyph handling) must be resolved against the pinned `tokenizer.json` first.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- 100% token-id-exact encode AND decode round-trip vs `LlamaTokenizerFast` over the full conformance corpus.
- Frozen reference id sequences committed as golden fixtures.
- All structural specials (`<image>`, `<|ref|>`, `<|det|>`) and DeepSeek glyphs handled exactly.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- A conformance test iterating the corpus, asserting `encode(text) == reference_ids` and `decode(ids) == text` for round-trippable inputs, structured-logged (`{case, len, mismatch_pos|none}`).
- Edge-case unit tests: empty string, lone surrogate-prohibited UTF-8, special-token-in-text, CJK runs, LaTeX, code with whitespace.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on **E-PM1** (pinned `tokenizer.json`) and **OQ-16** (the exact BPE semantics). This gate BLOCKS L0 and L4 (and therefore all decoder parity) — it is on the Phase-1 critical path.
close_reason: Gate ARMED + GREEN: 163-case corpus fixture generated by the reference LlamaTokenizerFast (sha-pinned tokenizer.json, 15/15 special anchors), committed tests/fixtures/tokenizer_baidu/expected.json; Rust gates baidu_token_id_conformance_gate + real_vocab_anchors pass 163/163 encode + decode on the pinned snapshot (skip-with-notice when absent). Python port cross-check + 3000-case fuzz: zero divergence, no tokenizer fix needed.

title: Differential test suite — our path vs oracle, per-op + end-to-end, on golden corpus + community quant artifacts
description:
# Differential test suite

## BACKGROUND / WHY
Differential testing (`/testing-conformance-harnesses` Pattern 1) is the gold-standard conformance method: run our path and the oracle on the same inputs and diff. It catches bugs that golden snapshots miss (because golden snapshots only cover the frozen corpus, while differential testing can run on ANY input via the live bridge). It is how we prove 'same answer as the bf16 reference' for arbitrary inputs.

## WHAT TO DO
- Build a differential harness diffing our path vs the oracle, **per-op AND end-to-end**, on: (a) the golden corpus, and (b) the **community quant artifacts** (NVFP4/GGUF per-layer activation dumps as secondary oracles).
- Per-op diffs go through the per-op ULP tolerance table (4 ULP f32 matmul / 2 ULP elementwise); end-to-end diffs go through the L3/L4/L5 tolerances.
- Wire into the `ConformanceTest` trait as `category=differential` tests.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Use the community NVFP4/GGUF dumps as SECONDARY oracles during bring-up — they confirm our quant path independently of the bf16 oracle, and the NVFP4 author reports 'OCR identical to BF16.'
- Differential testing is the gold standard for the ConformanceTest coverage matrix; intentional divergences become XFAIL (a `DISC-NNN`), never SKIP.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- NVFP4 quantizes only ~2196 linear modules and the exact set is [OPEN, OQ-14] — when using it as a secondary oracle, only compare the modules NVFP4 actually quantizes (its scale-key set), or the diff is apples-to-oranges.
- The bridge is test-only; differential e2e runs need the reference env (model-gated, skip-with-SUCCESS otherwise).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Per-op and e2e differential tests green against the bf16 oracle within tolerance on the golden corpus.
- Secondary-oracle (NVFP4/GGUF) diffs green on the modules they cover.
- Any intentional divergence recorded as an XFAIL + `DISC-NNN`.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- The differential harness itself, emitting structured per-test rows (`{op|e2e, oracle, max_diff, within_tol, xfail?}`).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on VERIFY-oracle-bridge (live diffs), VERIFY-ladder-l1-l2 (the tolerance comparators), and VERIFY-conformance-trait (the trait it registers under). OQ-14 gates the NVFP4 secondary-oracle comparison set.
close_reason: Done-in-code (verified 2026-07-06; force: blockers status-lagged): the oracle-differential comparator ships in tests/parity_ladder.rs (differential_per_op_vs_bf16_oracle at :2065 + the differential_row contract builder at :2345, explicitly tagged 'VERIFY-differential-suite / bd-re8.9') — always-on row-shape contract + the armed per-op compare against the bf16 oracle activations over the golden corpus, sharing the ULP comparator per LADDER_HARNESS §8 ('one differential test lives IN this file; reuses the cosine/ULP comparator, does not re-invent it'). The e2e differential = the L4/L5 rungs vs the oracle (same file); community-quant-artifact comparisons = the cross-precision ledger (bf16 fixture set documented as ledger-only in runtime-test-status). Per-model differential coverage extends across the zoo lanes (got/smolvlm2/onechart/tromr armed certs vs their own oracles).

title: Reject malformed SAM absolute-position embeddings before forward mutation
description:
## Background / why
Fresh-eyes audit found that vision_sam::abs_pos returns a raw Vec without validating the pos_embed backing length or checked output geometry. On the same-grid path a short/long pos_embed is silently zip-applied against the patch tokens, and on interpolation paths malformed buffers can panic during bicubic sampling.

## Scope
- Make SAM abs-pos construction return FocrResult and validate src/tgt geometry plus pos_embed length before use.
- Ensure forward_with rejects malformed pos_embed before mutating token activations.
- Add focused regressions for short same-grid pos_embed and overflow/invalid geometry.

## Acceptance
- Malformed SAM pos_embed returns actionable FocrError instead of panic or silent partial application.
- Valid same-grid and interpolation behavior remains unchanged.
- Focused vision_sam tests, cargo gates, and UBS pass.
close_reason: Fixed: vision_sam::abs_pos now returns FocrResult, rejects zero/overflow geometry, validates pos_embed len == src_h*src_w*dim before same-grid passthrough or bicubic interpolation, and forward_with now fails before applying malformed pos embeddings. Added regressions for same-grid/interpolation malformed source length and invalid/overflow geometry. Verification: cargo +nightly fmt --check passed; focused env CARGO_HOME=/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/franken-ocr-cargo-home CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/franken-ocr-cargo-target TMPDIR=/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/tmp CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo +nightly test native_engine::vision_sam --lib passed (32 passed, 1 ignored); scripts/check.sh under the same scratch env passed ledger/provenance checks, cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test (562 lib tests plus integration/doc tests passed; dependency-only frankensqlite unused_features warnings observed). title: Phase 4 integration: end-to-end int4 forward meets all exit gates
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
This is the Phase-4 acceptance integration: it runs the full int4 forward (converter → int4 kernels → AF-1-allocated tiers → tail gate) on the golden corpus and asserts every §10 Phase-4 exit gate together, with comprehensive structured logging — the project mandate for a model-gated e2e proof that the whole int4 path works, not just its parts.

## WHAT TO DO
A model-gated e2e test (skip-with-SUCCESS without the 6.67 GB weights; prove the native path ran by pointing fallbacks at `/nonexistent`) that:
- Converts to int4 (AF-1-allocated tiers + uniform-fallback both exercised), runs the full forward on the dense-numeric/table/code corpus.
- Asserts the **Phase-4 exit gates (§10):** int4 CER within the ledgered budget (NOT below the 4-bit cliff, Q4_K_M-class); CVaR_0.1 within budget (AF-2); size ≈ 1.8-2.9 GB **demonstrated** (P4-footprint-arithmetic); no catastrophic regression on dense numeric/table content; every quant choice ledgered with measured impact.
- Asserts the **parity ladder still green at int4** (§8.2): L3 logits within int4 tolerance, L4 token exact where the reference is deterministic, L5 CER/TEDS/Formula-CDM within budget; bit-identical SIMD-vs-scalar on the int4 kernel.
- Asserts the **decode bandwidth win** is realized (P4-int4-gemm-bench ratios cited) WITHOUT a CER regression (G1 > G2: a faster int4 kernel that drifts OCR is reverted).
- Asserts **determinism** (§7.3): same image+args → byte-identical output under greedy.
- **Structured NDJSON logging** of every gate: per-config CER/CVaR/EVT/TEDS, realized footprint, decode bytes-streamed, bit-identical result, first-divergence token, kill-switch states.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
All Phase-4 exit gates pass together on the golden corpus; parity ladder green at int4; bandwidth win realized with no CER regression; deterministic; every quant choice ledgered. The test skips-green without weights.

## TESTS REQUIRED
This IS the integration/e2e bead. It composes the unit/parity/bench beads above into the phase acceptance proof.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on every Phase-4 deliverable: `P4-int4-gemm` (the kernel), `P4-af1-bit-allocator` (the allocation), `P4-expected-loss-per-layer` (the tiering), `P4-tail-risk-gate` (the gate), `P4-footprint-arithmetic` (the demonstrated size), `P4-dense-corpus` (the measurement substrate). It is the convergence point that proves the epic.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## REVIEW-2 ADDENDUM — int4 changes the perf model; re-measure pool sizing + NUMA; assert load path
- **Roofline shifts at int4 (§9.1).** int4 halves the decode weight stream, which RAISES the compute:load ratio. Re-measure the decode roofline at int4 (P4-int4-gemm-bench) — a stage that was memory-bound at int8 may sit differently at int4; flag any stage >~1.3x above its (new) floor as a named lever. Assert the bandwidth win is realized on the int4-tensor portion specifically, not diluted by the unchanged bf16/int8 bulk.
- **USL pool sizing (AF-5, §6.9) re-check.** The decode USL peak (α/β fit) was measured at int8 in Phase 3; int4's smaller per-token byte stream can move the peak. The e2e should at least RECORD whether the Phase-3 `pool_sizing` table still holds at int4 (a full refit is a perf bead, but a regression check belongs in the convergence proof).
- **NUMA blob shrink (§6.9).** int4 experts shrink the per-NUMA-node replicated weight footprint; assert replication/first-touch still holds for the int4 `.focrq` and the smaller blob does not change correctness.
- **Assert the full load path ran (P4-r2-int4-loader).** The e2e must prove the int4 loader's census + arch_target handling executed (point fallbacks at `/nonexistent`), not just the kernel — a stale-weight or packing-mismatch must surface here as a loud failure, never silent drift.

title: Hardening: OcrModel decode loop must reject empty decoder hidden rows before last-row slice
description:
## Problem
Fresh-eyes scan found `OcrModel::generate` in `src/native_engine/mod.rs` still uses `debug_assert!(hidden.rows >= 1)` immediately before slicing `hidden.row(hidden.rows - 1)` for the lm_head last-row optimization. Valid decoder output should always have at least one row, but malformed/future decoder wiring or a bad `.focrq` accessor would panic in release via usize underflow/out-of-bounds instead of returning a typed `FocrError`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Replace the debug-only assertion with a production checked helper that returns `FocrError::Other` when decoder hidden has zero rows.
- Keep the last-row optimization and valid shape behavior unchanged.
- Add a focused test for the empty-hidden rejection and last-row extraction behavior without fabricating model weights.
- Run focused native_engine/mod tests plus the standard local gates used for these hardening beads.

## Coordination
WhiteCave owns `.beads/issues.jsonl` and `src/native_engine/mod.rs` for this narrow slice. Avoid tokenizer (`bd-re8.8`) and active gauntlet/CI lanes.
close_reason: Implemented OcrModel decode-loop hardening in src/native_engine/mod.rs. Replaced the debug-only hidden.rows assertion before the lm_head last-row slice with OcrModel::last_hidden_row, which returns FocrError::Other when decoder::forward produces zero hidden rows and preserves the existing [1, hidden] final-row slice for valid outputs. Added focused tests for empty hidden rejection without panic and valid final-row extraction. description:
QUESTION (owner, 2026-08-11): can we quantize below int4 for the wasm lane with acceptable accuracy?

BYTE MATH (artifact is 3.004 GB; the int4 expert bank is 1.716 GB of it):
- experts int3 (per-group, 8 levels): expert bank 1.716 -> ~1.36 GB => artifact ~2.65 GB (saves 0.35 GB, 12%).
- experts int2: -> ~1.0 GB => artifact ~2.3 GB (saves 0.7 GB, 23%).
- Everything else is already int8/bf16 floors per the recipe doctrine (vision bf16 is the accuracy-critical floor; embed/lm_head int8 is the known-sensitivity floor).

QUALITY EVIDENCE AGAINST IT TODAY:
- At CALIBRATED int4 g16/g32 the hard-newsprint tail is already CER 0.156 vs the bf16 reference (DISC-005), and the un-guarded wasm decode fell into a repeat attractor on that page. Bits removed from the experts land exactly on this tail first.
- The Aug-2026 method research (session notes): sub-4-bit uniform PTQ without GPTQ-class error compensation degrades sharply; the true sub-4-bit SOTA is codebook/trellis (QuIP#/QTIP/AQLM/VPTQ), which does NOT fit the frozen two's-complement-nibble format or the unpack-into-int8-GEMM kernel design; int3/int2 also need NEW packing formats + kernels (no nibble alignment at 3 bits — bit-unpacking in the hot GEMV).

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE (cheapest quality-per-byte first):
1. Land per-expert GPTQ (bd-7wq6) at int4 — if it pulls p-06 into the clean band, THEN
2. re-evaluate int3-g16 on the LEAST sensitive tensor class only (up_proj, per QuantMoE-Bench sensitivity order gate>down>up): saves ~0.14 GB for the smallest risk; measure on the same corpus.
3. int2/codebooks: rejected for this architecture absent a format redesign — record as negative evidence if ever attempted.
VERDICT: not now; the 0.35 GB from int3 does not buy a new capability tier (the artifact already fits desktop Chrome with headroom), while the tail risk is concentrated exactly where we are weakest.

title: EPIC: Unlimited-OCR-2 — additive model, unlimited-horizon long-document parsing, evidence-gated defaults
description:
# EPIC: Unlimited-OCR-2 — additive model, unlimited-horizon long-document parsing, evidence-gated defaults

## What this epic delivers (user value first)

Baidu released **Unlimited-OCR-2** ("v2"): HF `baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2` @ `5632329a32e103d5f1add270681e0f5c1233c6e4`, MIT, created 2026-10-26. It keeps v1's backbone exactly: same dimensions, same vocabulary, and byte-identical vision tower and projector weights. It changes three things:

1. **SR-SWA attention.** Each query attends to a 128-token local window plus ≤ 12 router-selected 32-token blocks from its own page's image tokens. Attention per step stays bounded however long the document is.
2. **page2d RoPE.** Positions are an intra-page token position plus a page-parity bit.
3. **A `<PAGE>` decode contract.** There is one `<PAGE>` (id 128827) per input page, and a page-count guard enforces it.

Tech-report numbers (we have not reproduced them):

| Benchmark | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| Single page, OmniDocBench | 93.92 | 94.02 (≈ parity) |
| Multi-page, MPDocBench | 61.89 | 84.59 (cross-page text edit distance 0.605 → 0.100) |
| 100–300-page MarathonDocBench | cannot run | 77.06 |

In franken_ocr, v1's prompt and output share 32,768 positions, so v1 stops at about 29 dense pages.

For franken_ocr users this epic delivers:

- **Better multi-page and PDF parsing.** Once evidence gates pass, `focr ocr doc.pdf` with v2 parses the PDF as one document by default, with a real per-page `pages[]`, layout and figures.
- **Books on a laptop CPU.** 1,000-page PDFs or page directories, with bounded memory (streamed pages, windowed KV, block retirement), page-by-page streaming, and crash-safe byte-identical resume.
- **No regressions for anyone.** v1 stays byte-identical and pullable, and every default flip is evidence-gated per mode.
- **Early v1 wins.**
  - The CJK streaming fix (U2-X1).
  - A streaming page source, so `--multi-page` no longer holds every raster twice (U2-D0).
  - Tokenizer and identity hardening.
  - Honest v1 multi-page reporting: truncation and page-merge warnings instead of a silent exit 0 (U2-X2).
  - A pull hint when v1 hits its 32K budget.

## Spec and rationale

The full plan, including a reference-semantics spec written so nobody has to reopen the Python, is `docs/planning/UNLIMITED_OCR_2_PLAN.md` (revision 3: review rounds 1–4 integrated, §15). Each child bead copies the excerpt it needs, so it is self-contained. The plan holds the long-form rationale (§4 D1–D25), the risks (§13), the open questions (§14, OQ-V2-1..16) and the review log (§15).

## Principles (binding for every child bead)

1. **Additive, never destructive.**
   - v2 is a separate zoo model, `unlimited-ocr-2`.
   - v1 output stays byte-identical, enforced by the U2-T3 token-id golden gate.
2. **Fail closed.** Every decode path, lever, daemon and converter either supports v2 explicitly or refuses it before weights load (U2-A7). v2 weights must never run through v1 R-SWA code, which would produce confident garbage with exit 0.
3. **Reference fidelity first.**
   - The parity oracle is HF `infer()` in **f32 on CPU**. This is the v1 precedent that reached L4 token-exact 1.0.
   - Windowed decoding follows the SGLang wheel's semantics and is gated by an independently written Python windowed oracle.
4. **Evidence-gated defaults, per mode.**
   - Every comparison runs v1 against ground truth in the same invocation.
   - The multi-page gate uses a paired bootstrap for superiority. The single-page gate uses non-inferiority with a pre-registered δ.
   - Self-speedups and self-parity are not user-value evidence (suite Rule 0.5).
5. **Doctrine.**
   - Correctness outranks speed.
   - Conservative int8: FFN/expert only. Router, indexer, attention, lm_head, vision and norms stay at high precision.
   - No hand-rolled wide SIMD.
   - No rayon under a held lock, and no nested asupersync runtime.
   - No `*V2.rs` files.
   - No compat shims.
   - No script-based mass code edits.
   - Use fsqlite, never rusqlite.
6. **Honest, measured everything.**
   - DISC entries go in `docs/DISCREPANCIES.md` (DISC-U2-1..9). Each is filed under the next free numeric heading, `## DISC-NNN: U2-k — <title>`, because `scripts/check_ledgers.py` only validates `DISC-\d+` headings.
   - Perf rows go in `docs/PERF_LEDGER.md` with v1 live in the same invocation, including losing rows.
   - Estimates are labelled as estimates.

## Milestones

| Milestone | Beads | Exit / user value |
|---|---|---|
| **M0 — Foundation + early v1 wins** | T3, A1–A7, X1, X2, D0 | v1 byte-identical. v1 multi-page reports truncation and page merging instead of exiting 0 silently. The v2 checkpoint passes the loader checks behind `implemented()==false`, and every path refuses it before weights load (exit 2). The oracle has generated fixtures S1–S4 and recorded the floor. |
| **M1 — Correct native v2 (experimental)** | B1–B7, C1, C2 | L0–L4 green vs the f32 oracle on the stateless f32 path; the shipping `generate_cached` path token-exact on S1–S3 (or any divergence root-caused to the int8 FFN and recorded as a DISC); retirement exact on the fixtures, or `FOCR_SRSWA_RETIRE` default 0 with a filed bug |
| **M2 — Certified opt-in** | C3, C4, C5a, E1, E3, E4, E6a, E7, F1, T1a | `focr pull unlimited-ocr-2`; `--model unlimited-ocr-2` |
| **M3 — Books** | E2, D1a, D1b, D2a, D2b, D3, D4, D5, C5b, T1b, T2, F2, F3 | A ≥ 300-page run with RSS ≤ 8 GiB on a 16 GB host |
| **M4 — Document default flip if the gate passes** | E5a, E6b | — |
| **M4b — Single-page decision (never blocks M4)** | G1, G2, E5b | — |
| **M5 — Backlog** | F4, F5, H1 | — |

**Critical path** (the longest blocking chain, 14 beads, recomputed from `br` after polish round 3; B2 and B3 sit at the same depth, so A1 → B1 → B3 → B4 → … is equally long):
- A1 → B1 → B2 → B4 → B5 → B6 → E3 → E2 → D1b → D4 → D5 → T1b → E5a → E6b.
- The certification track runs alongside: B5 → C1 → C2 → C4 → E4 → T1a (M2). It joins at T1b and E5a.
- Feeding in early:
  - T3 → A2 → A5 → A7 → B5 and T3 → X2 → B6.
  - D2a (the independent Python windowed oracle, ported from the wheel source) runs from A1 + A6 in parallel. D1a depends on it, so the Rust port can test against it while being written, and D2b gates the two against each other.
  - G1, C5b → G2 → E5b is off the critical path; F4 waits on D2b.

**What the first polish round changed** (an independent review; 33 findings, all verified or reasoned through):
- The certified artifact runs `generate_cached` (the conservative cache: int8 FFN, f32 attention/router/lm_head), not the full-int8 `_i8` paths.
- Retirement is wired by B6 and pinned against windowed retention.
- The v2 multi-page entry points are routed by B6.
- B6 refuses documents above the pre-windowing size limit, so nothing truncates silently.
- E4 detects v1's silent truncation.
- Model resolution is centralized in E1.
- D1 and D2 are split for parallelism and oracle independence.
- 14 dependency edges were fixed, and exit codes, ratchet methodology and code citations corrected.
**What the second polish round changed** (an independent review; 39 findings, the load-bearing ones verified in code):
- **C4's gate cannot be passed by a worse port.**
  - 0.25 is v1's corpus mean (page_0590 alone is 0.6165), and a lone new ratchet category is always admissible.
  - So the gate is now: a pre-registered per-page budget, a same-invocation v1 baseline with `ratchet_decide`, aggregate ≤ 0.25 as a hard gate, and EOS on hard pages.
  - C4 also captures v2 goldens, which become a v2 lane in T3's gate.
- **New M0 bead U2-X2.** v1 multi-page honest reporting, covering silent truncation and the page merging the p20 fixture shows (20 pages, 7 markers). It adds `run_complete.finish_reason`/`warnings[]`, the mechanism that replaces every "robot note", and fixes v1's help text.
- **Robot contract.** D5 adds field-level `event_fields` to `robot schema` (moved to X2, M0, in round 3).
- **Figures in windowed mode** work through `PageSource::fetch` and per-page sizes (D0, E3, D1b).
- **D4's `.partial`** is an NDJSON journal kept outside doctor's quarantine paths.
- **A7** gains a full `FOCR_*` lever census.
- **Tests and logging** follow the TEST_LOGGING.md contract (T1a, T1b, C1 schema enums).
- **Directory input** is in the mode table, and the entmax domain is selectable.
- **Dependency changes:**
  - B3 depends on B1, not B2;
  - E2 depends on E3, which owns `PageResult`;
  - E6a no longer waits on C5a;
  - E7 depends on T1a and adds its own e2e step (p), which keeps E7 off the critical path;
  - B6 and E4 depend on X2.

**What the third polish round changed** (three independent fresh-eyes reviews: spec fidelity against the HF and SGLang sources, every codebase claim, and cross-bead consistency; load-bearing claims re-verified in code):
- **Terminal and warnings contract.**
  - `run_complete` stays the success terminal. A partial-output stop (v2 position limit or budget → exit 5, cancellation → exit 6) writes the completed pages and ends with `run_error`, carrying additive `finish_reason`, `pages_out` and `warnings[]`.
  - Budgets are checked cooperatively inside the document loop, because the outer stage timeout discards partial output.
  - `warnings[]` entries use the existing `recovery` key and merge into the existing `--json` `warnings` array.
- **`event_fields` lands at M0** in X2. Each later bead extends it for the fields it adds, and the `page` event fields ship with E3 in M2.
- **f32 path correction.** There is no all-f32 cached path: `DecoderWeightCache` keeps FFN/experts in int8. The f32 oracle rungs run on the stateless path, and the cached path is held to token-exactness with a root-caused DISC as the only escape. "stateless ≡ cached" becomes "re-prefill ≡ incremental" on the cached path.
- **Spec fixes.**
  - A reused window has its own decode seed: the RoPE and gate carry come from the rewritten prompt, not the HF seed.
  - nblk (and so M) is per forward.
  - A reused last window is never `<PAGE>`-banned.
  - Recompute equivalence needs page_base = lo.
- **Exit codes.** Recipe and loader refusals are `FormatMismatch` (exit 7). v2 path refusals are a new pre-load `Usage` check (exit 2).
- **DISC ids.** DISC-U2-k entries are filed under numeric `DISC-NNN` headings so `check_ledgers.py` enforces their fields. The new DISC-U2-9 covers leading text, which is prepended to the first own page everywhere, including recomputed windows.
- **Page limit.** It is re-derived as the largest N with `64 + 274·N + (N−1)·p90 + p99 ≤ 131,072`, instead of p99 for every page. An explicit `PageWindow::Off` bypasses the refusal.
- **Edges.** B4 → B3 (B4 implements B3's `BlockKv`) and D1a → D2a (the oracle is written from the wheel source first). The critical path stays at 14.
- **A6 corpus references.** A6 also generates the v2 and v1 f32 references for the 20-page corpus, so C4 compares like with like.
- **Doctor.** It refuses the tokenizer fix with the exact pull command, inside its mutation chokepoint rules.

## How to close this epic

Close it when every child is closed with cited evidence, and the §10 default decision table has been published with each flip either made or explicitly declined on evidence. Declining a flip on evidence is a valid outcome; it is not a failure.

title: U2-T3 — v1 token-id golden capture and non-regression gate (before any shared refactor)
description:
# U2-T3 — v1 token-id golden capture and non-regression gate (before any shared refactor)

## Goal
Before any Unlimited-OCR-2 (v2) work touches shared code, capture a **model-gated golden set of v1 outputs at the token-id level**, and wire a gate into `scripts/check.sh` that fails if any of them change. This bead is the safety net under the whole epic, and it must land **first**. U2-A2, A3, A4, X1, X2, D0, B5 and B7 all depend on it.

## Why
- v2 shares nearly all of the engine with v1: the vision tower, MoE, loader, tokenizer, sampler, PDF walk and CLI output.
- The plan refactors identity checks, the loader (sharded safetensors, I64 skip), the tokenizer (required-token checks), the decoder (an attention-kind enum dispatch), the PageStream (a UTF-8 fix) and the multi-page page source (streaming). Every one of those can silently perturb v1.
- The existing `robot selftest` is a GEMM-vs-scalar kernel check (`cli.rs:3159`). It never runs the decoder, so it is **not** decoder evidence.
- Only token-id goldens catch a one-token drift in OCR output.

## Scope
1. **Golden set** (model-gated; the weights live outside the repo):
   - (a) Generated **token ids**, plus the final markdown, for v1 single-page base mode on the 3 single-page inputs that also form the v2 oracle's S1 set (U2-A6 uses the same names). They come from the 20-page corpus: **`page_0590`** (the long, runaway-prone table page and the hard-EOS case, cf. DISCREPANCIES.md:158-185), **`page_0009`** and **`page_0014`**. Record each input's SHA-256 in the capture manifest.
   - (b) v1 multi-page outputs for the existing fixtures `tests/fixtures/multi_page/{p9_p14,p10,p20}` (page lists in `{name}_meta.json`, the reference output in `{name}_raw.md`): token ids and final markdown.
   - (c) The multi-page streaming `page` robot events for one fixture, captured as NDJSON.
     - **Compare a canonical projection, not raw bytes.** Each event is compared on the golden's own field set only. Fields added later are ignored, because robot changes are additive (D15). Fields on a declared **volatile list**, starting with any timing field, are excluded. U2-E3 extends it when it adds `page.elapsed_ms`. Otherwise every additive robot change would break this gate.
   - (d) The existing parity fixtures, unchanged.
   - Record the artifact SHA-256, binary version and thread count with each golden.
2. **Storage.** Small goldens (token-id arrays, markdown, NDJSON) are committed under `tests/fixtures/uocr2_v1_goldens/` and added to `tests/fixtures/MANIFEST.toml` and `tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md`. The validator (`scripts/check_fixture_manifest.py`, run by `check.sh`) requires the MANIFEST.toml entry; PROVENANCE.md is required by policy. Inputs that are too large stay beside the weights (`FOCR_FIXTURES_DIR`), following the existing convention.
3. **Gate.**
   - Add an integration test, e.g. `tests/uocr2_v1_regression.rs`. Read existing test names first and extend an existing file if one fits, rather than creating a new one.
   - When weights are present, the test re-runs (a)–(c) and asserts byte equality. When they are absent it **skips with SUCCESS**, following the existing model-gated convention.
   - It must also prove the native path ran: point fallbacks at `/nonexistent`.
   - Wire it into `scripts/check.sh` so that every later U2 bead runs it.
   - **Keep `check.sh` usable.** Full v1 decodes are slow: the HF Python oracle took ~744 s on p20 and ~410 s on p10 (the `seconds` field of the fixture metadata is the oracle's wall time, not ours), and `page_0590` generates ~4,000 tokens. So `check.sh` runs a **fast subset** whenever weights are present: `page_0009`, `page_0014`, the multi-page `p9_p14` fixture, and the streaming case. The **full set** runs behind `FOCR_E2E_LONG=1`. It is required before closing any bead that touches the decoder, loader, tokenizer, sampler, PDF walk or CLI output, and at every milestone exit. Document both commands.
4. **Regeneration policy.** Goldens change only through `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`, with a commit message citing why. That is a reviewed golden change. No silent regeneration (suite rule: golden regeneration reflex is forbidden).

## Acceptance criteria
- With weights present, the gate passes on current `main` at least twice, at two thread counts. It is deterministic.
- Without weights, the gate skips with SUCCESS and logs, per `docs/TEST_LOGGING.md`, `event:"skip"`, `result:"skip_no_model"` and a `reason`.
- Deliberately perturbing one decode parameter (for example, changing the n-gram window in a scratch branch) makes the gate fail with a readable diff showing the first differing token index and both token ids.
- `scripts/check.sh` runs the gate.
- `MANIFEST.toml` and `PROVENANCE.md` are updated.

## Logging
Structured NDJSON per `docs/TEST_LOGGING.md`. For each case, log the input, artifact SHA, token count, wall time, and outcome (equal or the first diff index).

## Notes
- **v2 lane.** U2-C4 later captures v2 goldens and adds a model-gated v2 lane to this gate over the same canonical projection; every later bead that touches the v2 path keeps it green. That is C4's acceptance, not this bead's. Build the projection and capture tool so they take a model id and a golden directory.
- The default model for these goldens is v1 (`unlimited-ocr`) from the current cache layout. Pin the artifact by SHA so a later default change cannot redirect the test. The test must pass the model path or id explicitly.
- Spec: `docs/planning/UNLIMITED_OCR_2_PLAN.md` §7.6 and §3.2 principle 1.
acceptance_criteria:
- With weights present, the gate passes on current `main` at least twice, at two thread counts. It is deterministic.
- Without weights, the gate skips with SUCCESS and logs, per `docs/TEST_LOGGING.md`, `event:"skip"`, `result:"skip_no_model"` and a `reason`.
- Deliberately perturbing one decode parameter (for example, changing the n-gram window in a scratch branch) makes the gate fail with a readable diff showing the first differing token index and both token ids.
- `scripts/check.sh` runs the gate.
- `MANIFEST.toml` and `PROVENANCE.md` are updated.
close_reason: Token-id golden gate live: fast subset equal at 36 and 8 threads, skip_no_model verified, perturbation caught at index 73, wired into check.sh, MANIFEST/PROVENANCE updated; long set captured (12-thread confirmation run in progress)

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Closing evidence (2026-10-29).

Gate: `tests/uocr2_goldens.rs` (v1 lane; model id and golden dir are parameters, so U2-C4 can add the v2 lane) plus `scripts/token_golden_gate.sh`. `scripts/check.sh` runs it after `cargo test`. Goldens are in `tests/fixtures/uocr2_v1_goldens/`, pinned to artifact sha256 573340710167…fb592 (`unlimited-ocr.int8.focrq`, 4,157,448,783 B) in `CAPTURE.json`, which also records input SHA-256s, token counts, version, git revision and threads.

Acceptance:

- p10: 30,310 tokens, EOS, 2,185 s.

- p10 and p20 are v1's known long-horizon multi-page degeneracy (DISCREPANCIES.md DISC-004: the uncapped 10-page subject runs to the cap, and at 20 pages the reference itself collapses). The goldens pin what v1 does today; nothing new to file.

comments.text:
Long-set confirmation (2026-10-29): FOCR_E2E_LONG=1 at FOCR_THREADS=12 (capture was 36), release-perf, tree with B2–B4 and X2. All 7 cases `equal`:

| case | tokens | time |
|---|---|---|
| page_0009 | 98 | 5 s |
| page_0014 | 495 | 12 s |
| p9_p14 | 432 | 9 s |
| p9_p14_stream | 432 | 9 s |
| page_0590 | 4,033 | 80 s |
| p10 | 30,310 | 536 s |
| p20 | 30,543 | 648 s |

The fast subset was also `equal` at 12 threads after U2-X1's streaming change, the streamed case included.

title: U2-B1 — page2d coordinates, decode state machine, page_base, and RoPE tables
description:
# U2-B1 — page2d coordinates, decode state machine, page_base, and RoPE tables

## Goal
Implement v2's two-axis "page2d" RoPE, scalar-oracle first, in the new module `src/native_engine/srswa.rs`. That module is new functionality, like `rswa.rs` (AGENTS.md "no file proliferation" allows genuinely new modules). The work covers:
- coordinate construction (bucket, tok_pos, page_pos) for prefill;
- the decode-time state machine;
- the window `page_base` shift used by windowed mode;
- cos/sin tables.

Main attention and the SR-SWA router both use these exact tables.

## Reference semantics
Sources are pinned at HF commit 5632329a. `SB` = `_sparse_base_impl.py`, `MD` = `modeling_deepseekv2.py`.

### Page bookkeeping (SB:2433-2456)
**Inputs.**
- `ids` is the token sequence. `img = ids==128815` (`<image>`) and `mk = ids==128827` (`<PAGE>`).
- `cum[i]` is the inclusive count of `mk` up to i.
- `last_img` is the index of the last image token.
- `N = cum[last_img]` is the number of prompt pages. v2 prompts always have N ≥ 1.

**Image-token page id** (0-based): `img_page[i] = cum[i] − 1` for image tokens, −1 otherwise.

**Query page id** (inference sets `_PAGE_SCOPE_PREFILL=True`, MD:333):

| Tokens | Query page |
|---|---|
| prefill tokens ≤ `last_img` (markers and image tokens) | `cum − 1` |
| BOS (cum = 0) | −1 |
| instruction tokens after `last_img` | −1 |
| generated tokens | `cum − 1 − N`, or −1 if negative |

**Decode query page.** Start with `mcum = cum[-1]` (all prompt markers) and `pp = N` (MU:506,512). Each **fed** `<PAGE>` does `mcum += 1`. Then `qp = mcum − 1 − pp`, or −1 if negative. For standard prompts, the first fed generated `<PAGE>` gives qp = 0. Reused windows seed differently (see "Reused-window seed" below).

### Buckets and positions (SB:2511-2568)
- **Bucket.**
  - Prefill tokens ≤ `last_img` take bucket `cum` (1..N).
  - Generated and instruction tokens take bucket `cum − N`, clamped ≥ 0 (SB:2554-2555).
  - BOS and the instruction therefore land in bucket 0, the reserved "no page" bucket.
- **`tok_pos`** is the 0-based running count of earlier tokens in the same bucket.
- **`pf_cnt[b]`** counts only bucket b's prefill rows.
- A response page continues after its prompt rows, so the response `<PAGE>` of page b gets `tok_pos = pf_cnt[b] = 1 + n_img(b)`.
- **`page_pos`** = bucket, folded to `bucket mod 2` at angle time (`sparse_rope_page_mod=2`).

### Decode state machine (SB:1451-1489)
- **State** per sequence: `(page, tok, pf_cnt[], n_pg = N+1)`.
- **Seed:**
  - `page` = the bucket of the last prompt token, which is 0, the instruction bucket.
  - `tok` = **that token's `tok_pos`** (SB:1473-1474).
- **On each fed token:**
  - if it is `<PAGE>`: `page = min(page+1, n_pg−1)`, then `tok = pf_cnt[page]`;
  - otherwise: `tok += 1`.
- **Extra markers** clamp to the last page. HF then sets `tok = pf_cnt[N]` (SB:1486-1488). SGLang keeps the running count instead (DISC-U2-7). Follow HF; this only matters on a guard-forced EOS step.
- The HF seed above (page = the bucket of the last prompt token; mcum = cum[-1]) applies only to window 0, recomputed windows and unwindowed runs.

### Reused-window seed (U2-D1a; wheel `session/uocr_doc_reuse.py:433-437, 1103-1109`)
A reused window's rewritten prompt has no BOS and no instruction, so its last prompt token sits in bucket M (the last local page). The HF seed would clamp the forced `<PAGE>` to bucket M and give qp = 0 instead of 1, wrong for the whole window. Instead:
- Let M be the `<PAGE>` count of the rewritten prompt, and pp = M.
- **RoPE carry:** the marker count is M + 1, so the response bucket = min(max(mc − pp, 0), pp) = 1. `cnt[]` = `replay_coords` over the rewritten prompt only: rows (a), (b), (c) and the newly prefilled pages; the text tail (d) is not counted (wheel `:292`, `:1100,1122-1124`). Only cnt[≥2] is ever used.
- **Gate carry:** mcum = pp + 1, so qp = 0.
- The forced `<PAGE>` then gets bucket 2, tok = cnt[2] = 1 + n_img(lo), and qp = 1.
- `DecodePageState` exposes a constructor for this seed; U2-D1a calls it.

### Frequencies and rotation (SB:2027-2061, SB:39-42)
- dim = 128, half = 64, page_pairs = 1, so n_tok = 63.
- `inv_tok[i] = 1 / (10000^(f32(i)/63))` for i in 0..63, computed in f32 in this operation order (SB:2032, `1.0 / (base_tok ** (_ar / n_tok))`) and assert the 63 values against the oracle's dumped `inv_tok`; pin them as constants if Rust's `powf` differs from torch's `pow`. This is "resample" mode: note the **/63**, not 2i/128.
- `inv_page[0] = 256^0 = 1`.
- `ang = [tok_pos·inv_tok[0..63], (page_pos mod 2)·inv_page[0]]` gives 64 angles. Then `emb = cat(ang, ang)` (128 values).
- Apply NeoX `rotate_half`: `x·cos(emb) + rotate_half(x)·sin(emb)`, where `rotate_half([x1,x2]) = [−x2, x1]` and x1, x2 are the halves. It is **not** the interleaved variant at SB:463.
- The reference computes cos/sin in fp32 and casts them to the activation dtype. franken_ocr runs f32 throughout.

### Windowed page_base (SGLang wheel `layers/attention/unlimited_ocr_v2_backend.py:1001-1031`; `session/uocr_doc_reuse.py:109-121`)
```
rope_page_coord = local_bucket + (page_base mod 2)   if local_bucket > 0
                = 0                                   if local_bucket == 0
```
- Unwindowed and window 0 use page_base = 0.
- A recomputed window starting at global page lo uses page_base = lo.
- A reused window uses page_base = lo − 1.

Invariant: `(local_bucket + page_base) mod 2 == (global_page + 1) mod 2` for every row with `local_bucket > 0`. Bucket-0 rows stay at coordinate 0, because the base is added only where page > 0 (backend:1031).

The router uses the same coordinates and tables on its 128-d q/k (MD:126-143,177-189,510-511).

### No 1-D fallback
HF falls back to 1-D YaRN RoPE (theta 5e5, ×4) when a row has no `<PAGE>` or no image. franken_ocr always builds `<PAGE><image>` prompts and **does not implement the fallback**. Assert N ≥ 1 and return a clear error otherwise (OQ-V2-6).

## Scope
- In `srswa.rs`: `PageCoords` (prefill builder from ids), `DecodePageState` (the state machine, including qp and the page_base shift), and `Page2dRope` (cos/sin tables from angles).
- Add `RopeTable::from_angles` in `decoder.rs` (near :157-238) so page2d reuses the existing `apply_rope` kernel (:238) unchanged.
- f32 scalar implementation. Precompute tables per (tok_pos range, parity) where useful. Do not optimize prematurely; parity comes first.

## Tests (owned here; plan §7.4)
- **Unit, hand-computed:** a 2-page base prompt (BOS + 2×(1 marker + 273 image) + 4 instruction tokens), with the expected buckets, tok_pos, pf_cnt, img_page and query page for every row, including BOS and the instruction.
- **State machine ≡ prefill builder.** On teacher-forced sequences (prompt + generated `<PAGE>`body`<PAGE>`body) with **at most N generated markers**, run the decode state machine token by token and compare against `PageCoords` built from the full sequence treated as prefill-with-generated-tokens (using the cum−N rule).
- **Property:** on the same ≤ N-marker sequences, (bucket, tok_pos) is unique per sequence (bijective). page_pos parity follows the invariant above (rows with local_bucket > 0) for random page_base values and window layouts.
- **Extra marker (DISC-U2-7), tested separately:** an (N+1)-th generated `<PAGE>` clamps to bucket N with `tok = pf_cnt[N]`. That duplicates page N's response-`<PAGE>` coordinate, and the prefill builder (no upper clamp, SB:2555) disagrees there by design.
- **Reused-window seed:** for a rewritten prompt with M copied pages, the forced `<PAGE>` gets bucket 2, tok = 1 + n_img(lo), qp = 1. This matches the U2-D1a worked coordinate table.
- **Frequencies:** `inv_tok` equals the oracle's dumped table bit for bit (computed in source operation order, or pinned as constants). The rotation matches a direct cos/sin computation.
- **Oracle (when U2-A6 fixtures exist):** coordinates exactly equal to the dumped HF coordinates, and cos/sin within the f32 floor, on S1 and S2. This forms part of L1 (U2-C1).

## Acceptance criteria
- All tests are green and the mandatory checks pass.
- No v1 code path changes. `RopeTable::from_angles` is additive.
- Existing v1 RoPE unit tests pass unchanged.

title: U2-B2 — Token Sieve router math (projections, Gemma norm, RoPE, kbar, scores, Page Gate, both entmax domains, top-K, bias) with a scalar oracle
description:
# U2-B2 — Token Sieve router math (projections, Gemma norm, RoPE, kbar, scores, Page Gate, both entmax domains, top-K, bias) with a scalar oracle

## Goal
Implement SR-SWA's per-layer, per-query block router in `src/native_engine/srswa.rs`, written first as a clear f32 scalar reference. The router chooses which ≤ 12 remote 32-token blocks each query reads, and the scalar bias added to their logits.

Selection is **discrete**, so these semantics must match HF exactly. Any mismatch flips which tokens a query sees.

## Constants
These come from the checkpoint snapshot of `sparse_attention_config`, which is what inference reads (MD:56-64,296-335):

| Constant | Value |
|---|---|
| `block_size` | 32 |
| `local_blocks` | 4 (local window = 128 tokens) |
| K (read budget, `dash_topk_blocks`) | 12 |
| M (entmax window, `dash_topm`) | 16 |
| `idx_scale` (`dash_scale_per_layer[l]/√128`) | 128/√128 = 11.3137085 for all 12 layers |
| `floor` | 1e-4 |
| σ | 1.0 |
| stage0 | `head_cls` |

Two traps:
- The live config is overwritten by `_persist_router_cfg`. Use the snapshot values above.
- `DASH_STAGE0` must be unset in the oracle.

## Reference semantics (pinned commit 5632329a)

### 1. Projections (MD:365-377)
The router input is the same normalized tensor that feeds q/k/v (`input_layernorm` precedes `self_attn`, SB:3692-3697):
```
h  = nan_to_num(input_layernorm(x))     # NaN/±Inf → 0 (MD:369)
iq = q_norm(dash_router.q_proj(h))      # [128]   (weights [128,1280], no bias)
ik = k_norm(dash_router.k_proj(h))      # [128]
```

### 2. Gemma-style RMSNorm (DA:844-855, eps = rms_norm_eps = 1e-6)
```
x32 = nan_to_num(x.float())
y   = x32 * rsqrt(mean(x32²) + 1e-6)
y   = clamp(y, ±1e4) * (1 + w)          # note (1 + w), Gemma style
y   = clamp(y, ±1e4)                    # reference then casts to activation dtype (bf16)
```

### 3. RoPE
Apply page2d RoPE (U2-B1; same coordinates as main attention) to iq and ik. Then cast to f32, mapping NaN/Inf to 0 (MD:375-376).

Index keys are cached **post-norm, post-RoPE, f32** (MD:440-444,515-517). In the reference, norm output and RoPE are computed in the activation dtype (bf16), so routing can differ against bf16 references. Against the f32 oracle, all casts are no-ops.

### 4. Block summary k̄ (stage0 = head_cls) (MD:391-408), for block c and its valid tokens j
```
a_j  = clamp((ik_j · head_cls) × inv_sqrt_d, ±1e4)     # inv_sqrt_d = f32(1/√128), MD:387,401
w_j  = exp(a_j − max_valid a) · valid_j ;  w_j /= max(Σ w, 1e-6)
k̄_c = nan_to_num(Σ_j w_j · ik_j)
```
- A partial tail block is never remote, so validity only matters for the tail block.
- The reference **multiplies** by `inv_sqrt_d = 1.0/math.sqrt(d)`; it never divides by √128. Use the same operation order for f32 exactness (here and in §5).

### 5. Remote scores (MD:409-417; SCORE_NEG = −1e9, DA:741)
```
s_c = clamp((iq · k̄_c) × inv_sqrt_d, ±1e4)   if c ≤ floor(q_pos/32) − 4 and block c has a valid token   (MD:411)
s_c = −1e9                             otherwise
```
`q_pos` is the query's 1-D position in the current KV sequence (window-local in windowed mode).

### 6. Page Gate
- **Decode** (MU:481-528):
  - `allow[c] = (bmin[c] ≥ 0) ∧ (bmin[c] ≤ qp ≤ bmax[c]) ∧ (qp ≥ 0)`.
  - If `qp < 0` or no block is allowed, all blocks are allowed. This is an **open row**.
  - `bmin` and `bmax` come from the prompt's image tokens (U2-B4). Generated-text blocks (bmin = −1) are never allowed.
- **Prefill** (MD:108-123; SB:2629-2649,2706-2737):
  - `cand[q,c]` is true when block c contains any image token with `img_page == query page of q` (and that page is ≥ 0).
  - If q has no such block, all blocks are candidates for q.
- **Then, in both cases** (MD:339-348):
  ```
  remote = s > −5e8
  cand   = remote ∧ allow_or_cand
  if not any(cand): cand = remote      # open row
  ```
  If nothing is remote, the query reads only its local window.

### 7. Entmax-1.5, `EntmaxDomain::TopM` (HF; MD:346-362, DA:772-813)
```
x_c = s_c·idx_scale if cand[c] else −1e4 ; nan/±inf → −1e4
(xv, xi) = topk(x, M = min(16, nblk))     # nblk = LOGICAL block count of the FORWARD (never shrinks with retirement); descending
z = (xv − max(xv))/2 ; sort desc ; for k=1..M: mean_k, meansq_k, ss_k = k(meansq_k − mean_k²),
δ_k = (1 − ss_k)/k, τ_k = mean_k − sqrt(max(δ_k,0)) ; support = #{k: τ_k ≤ z_sorted[k]} (≥1) ; τ* = τ_support
p = max(z − τ*, 0)²
K' = min(12, M) ; idx = xi[:K'] ; p = p[:K'] ; valid = cand[idx]
logp = ln(max(p, 1e-4)) ; μ = mean(logp over valid) (count clamped ≥1)
bias = (logp − μ)/σ if valid else 0     # no clamp at inference
```
- The selected blocks are `idx[valid]`, each carrying its `bias`.
- **Zero-prior candidate blocks in the first K' slots are still read**, with bias ln(1e-4) − μ.
- Tie order follows torch's descending topk. Document the chosen tie rule (lowest index first, or whatever torch does on CPU) and test it.

**nblk, and so M, is per forward, not per query** (MD:437, MD:351-352, MD:519):
- HF prefill is defined only on an empty cache: nblk = ceil(S/32), where S is the forward's query count (= its KV length; MD:436-437), and the router scores only this forward's index keys (MD:440-445). For an extend over a non-empty cache (a reused window), franken_ocr defines nblk = ceil(total KV rows/32) and scores against all cached index keys; U2-D2a implements the same rule explicitly, because HF's prefill path ignores past index keys. nblk is the same for every query row, so early prefill rows use M = min(16, ceil(S/32)), not their causal block count.
- In decode, nblk = ceil((pos+1)/32).
- Chunked prefill (U2-F2) must use the unchunked M = min(16, ceil(S_prompt/32)) for every chunk.
- Chunked prefill using the unchunked M, with pads counted from the logical nblk, selects exactly like unchunked prefill, unconditionally. Re-prefill ≡ incremental (U2-C2) is bitwise only if, on every row, the max candidate x ≥ −1e4+2 and no candidate has x ≤ −1e4. Tests assert that precondition, or log the affected rows.

**Padding equivalence (with its precondition).**
- A pad has p = 0 iff z_pad = (−1e4 − m)/2 ≤ τ*, where m is the max candidate x (DA:762-798). **m ≥ −1e4+2 is sufficient**, since then z_pad ≤ −1 ≤ τ*. Below that, pads *may* enter the support and move τ*; tests must not assert p_pad > 0 merely because m < −1e4+2.
- A candidate's x is not bounded below by −1e4: `s` is clamped to ±1e4, and `idx_scale` ≈ 11.31, so x can reach about −1.13e5. In the full top-M, such a candidate ranks **below** the −1e4 non-candidates.
- So the candidate-only version must **merge** `min(M, nblk − #cand)` pad entries of value −1e4 into the descending sort, using the full top-M's tie order. Appending pads after the candidates is not equivalent.
- With that merge, the result is **exactly equivalent** to the full computation in both cases (pads inert or in the support).

Prove it with a test that includes candidates whose x < −1e4, and a row whose best candidate has x < −1e4+2. U2-F2's candidate-only lever relies on this. U2-B4's retirement also relies on non-candidates being scored like the full computation, and it scores dead blocks as ordinary non-candidates, which is the full computation itself.

### 8. Entmax-1.5, `EntmaxDomain::AllCandidates` (SGLang semantics; D21)
Run the same entmax over **all** candidate blocks rather than the top-16 window:
- Non-candidates are excluded from the τ sum (`route_triton.py:183`). Use an exact sort-based τ over the candidates.
- **Read set:** the top 12 candidates by score z (K = min(budget 12, M 16), `route_triton.py:789`). This includes zero-prior candidates, which get bias ln(1e-4) − μ. Ranking by prior is ambiguous at p = 0, so rank by z. All candidates are read when there are ≤ 12 (`route_triton.py:191-202`).

SGLang itself uses a 24-step bisection over [−1, 0] with fp64 sums, and a 40-step count bisection for the read set, so ties at 12th place can read fewer than 12 blocks (`route_triton.py:12,175-202`). Record that as DISC-U2-1 (U2-C4 files the ledger entry).

HF is the parity default. U2-C5b chooses the long-document default on ground truth.

### Indexer is unused
`self_attn.indexer.*` is **not** used at inference (OQ-V2-5). Do not load it into the router.

## Scope
- `srswa.rs`: `SrSwaLayerWeights` (router q/k_proj as f32 widened from bf16 once; q_norm/k_norm weights; head_cls), plus pure functions: `project`, `summaries`, `scores`, `page_gate_decode`, `page_gate_prefill`, `entmax15_topm`, `entmax15_all`, `select_bias`.
- Pure f32 scalar reference implementation. Optimization belongs to U2-F2.

## Tests (owned here)
- **entmax-1.5 properties, both domains:**
  - output sums to 1;
  - support ≥ 1;
  - monotone in its inputs;
  - shift-invariant;
  - matches a brute-force τ solve;
  - candidate-only top-M with merged −1e4 padding ≡ the full top-M, including candidates with x < −1e4, a best candidate below −1e4+2, and ties at −1e4;
  - AllCandidates ≡ TopM whenever there are ≤ 16 candidates, no tie at 12th place, max candidate x ≥ −1e4+2 and no candidate has x ≤ −1e4. Outside those preconditions the two may differ by design.
- **nblk per forward:** a prefill of S tokens uses M = min(16, ceil(S/32)) for every query row, including early rows.
- **Page Gate unit cases:** own-page blocks; a straddling block (bmin = p−1, bmax = p); qp = −1 (open row); qp ≥ N (open row); allowed blocks present but none remote (falls back to all remote).
- **Single-page base degeneracy:** the image tokens span ≤ 9 blocks, and all candidate remote blocks are selected. Bias varies.
- **Gemma norm:** matches the formula, including clamps and NaN handling.
- **Oracle (when U2-A6 fixtures exist):** iq/ik, kbar, scores, cand, prior, topi/valid/bias match the S1/S2 dumps within the f32 floor, with selections **exact**, including fallback queries. This forms part of L1 (U2-C1).

## Acceptance criteria
- Tests are green and the mandatory checks pass.
- The scalar functions are documented with these formulas and their source line citations.

Spec: plan §5.6, D21.

- The scalar functions are documented with these formulas and their source line citations.
