title: U2-T1a — e2e script `scripts/uocr2_e2e.sh` with NDJSON logging, M2 scenarios
description:
# U2-T1a — e2e script `scripts/uocr2_e2e.sh` with NDJSON logging, M2 scenarios

## Goal
A single model-gated end-to-end script that exercises the real `focr` binary on real inputs for every M2 user-facing v2 scenario, with **detailed structured logging**, so a regression anywhere in the stack shows up as a named failing step with timings and context.

## Rules
- **No mocks:** real binary, real artifact, real inputs.
- Model gating is per step: a step that needs the v2 artifact skips with SUCCESS (exit 0, logged "skipped: weights absent") when it is absent. (j)'s refusal half and (p) use synthetic artifacts and always run.
- Prove the native path ran by pointing fallbacks at `/nonexistent`.
- Logging follows the `docs/TEST_LOGGING.md` contract: `schema_version`, `ts`, `test`, `case`, `run_seq`, `event`, `result`, and `diag{error_kind, focr_exit_code, message}` on failure. Write **one NDJSON line per step** with:
  - `test:"uocr2_e2e"`, `case:<step>`, `event:result|skip|error`, `result:pass|fail|skip_no_model`, `elapsed_us`;
  - the native-path proof fields `native_path_ran` and `fallback_target` (the TEST_LOGGING `native_path_proof` contract);
  - `cmd`, `env` (every `FOCR_*` plus `RAYON_NUM_THREADS`), `threads`, `git_sha`, `binary_sha256`, `model_id`, `artifact_sha256`, `input_sha256`, `outputs{path: sha256}`, `exit_code`;
  - `peak_rss_bytes`, from `/usr/bin/time -lp` on macOS and `-v` on Linux, as `scripts/gauntlet_focr.sh:857-860` does;
  - `stdout_path` and `stderr_path`, kept after the run;
  - on failure, `diag`, `stderr_tail` (last 40 lines) and `diff_head` (first 20 diff lines).
- The script finishes by running `scripts/check_test_logs.py` on its own log. U2-C1 extends the schema's enums.
- Wire it into `scripts/check.sh` as a model-gated step (skip-success without weights).

## Scenarios (plan §7.7, T1a set)
- **(a)** single page, base: output equals the v2 golden captured by U2-C4 (`tests/fixtures/uocr2_v2_goldens/`).
- **(b)** 3-page document: 3 bodies, page events in order, JSON `pages[]` length 3.
- **(c)** 20-page document via `focr ocr doc.pdf --multi-page --model unlimited-ocr-2`.
  - In M2, v2 documents are always unwindowed (the HF-parity mode), because windowing (U2-D1a/D1b) and its flags (U2-D5) arrive in M3. 20 pages is within U2-B6's pre-windowing limit.
  - Assert 20 bodies in order.
  - Record peak RSS, which exercises block retirement; the plan's bound is ≤ v1 multi-page + 1 GiB.
  - The windowed equivalent is T1b's (d).
- **(g)** v1 regression check: v1 outputs byte-identical to the U2-T3 goldens.
- **(h)** `--json --extract-figures` in document mode: per-page outputs and figure files named `page{N}_figure_{M}`. The same flags with v1 `--multi-page` still exit 2 (`cli.rs:1393-1408`).
- **(i)** `focr pull unlimited-ocr-2`, including tokenizer sidecar installation.
  - Part mirror URLs must be HTTPS (`validate_https_url`, `dist.rs:347-398`); only the manifest may be local (`read_local_manifest`). So this step runs against the **published** manifest, and only with `FOCR_E2E_NETWORK=1`; otherwise it skips with SUCCESS.
  - U2-E4 unit-tests the offline pieces: a local manifest via `FOCR_MANIFEST_URL=<path>`, parsing, the recipe check and the install layout.
- **(j)** lever matrix (U2-A7):
  - every refused lever env var with v2 exits 2 before weights load, with the expected message;
  - an ignored lever (e.g. `FOCR_QKV_FUSED=0`) runs and reports `warnings[{kind:"ignored_lever"}]`.
- **(k)** CJK streaming across a split multi-byte character: `page` events keep flowing (U2-X1).
- **(l)** v1 honest reporting (U2-X2) plus the v2 remediation (U2-E4), with the v1 artifact present.
  - `FOCR_TEST_MAX_POSITIONS` (U2-X2's hidden test override of `DecodeParams.max_positions`) places the clamp inside page 2 of a 3-page document. That reaches the real clamp branch, not a reduced user cap.
  - Assert:
    - the stderr warning;
    - `warnings[{kind:"v1_truncated"}]`;
    - `finish_reason:"length"`;
    - exit 0 (v1 exit codes are unchanged);
    - the `focr pull unlimited-ocr-2` remediation in the warning's `recovery`.
  - Assert the remediation on the prompt-too-long error as well.
- **(m′)** the U2-B6 pre-windowing limit: a (limit + 1)-page v2 document is refused with exit 2 and a message naming the limit. Add it only while U2-D1b is open; U2-D1b deletes it when it lifts the limit; U2-T1b's (m″) covers the windowed case.
- **(r)** `ocr-batch` with v2: `focr ocr-batch --model unlimited-ocr-2` over 3 images, and with `--multi-page` over one 3-page document. Each output equals the corresponding solo v2 run.

- **(p)** health, doctor and triage. **U2-E7 adds this step to the script.** E7 depends on this bead, which keeps it off the T1b/E5a critical path. The step runs in a temp cache holding a synthetic v2 artifact next to a v1 `tokenizer.json`:

# U2-T1b — e2e book scenarios: windowed, resume, robot, skip, directory, ≥300 pages with RSS

## Goal
Extend `scripts/uocr2_e2e.sh` (U2-T1a) with the **book** scenarios that make up M3's user promise: unlimited-horizon documents with bounded memory, streaming, resume and graceful handling of bad pages. These are the end-to-end proofs behind the M3 exit gate.

## Rules
Same as T1a: no mocks, model-gated skip-success, native-path proof, and T1a's per-step NDJSON fields. Book steps also log `windows`, `time_to_first_page_ms` and `resumed_from`. Every T1b step decodes long documents, so each runs only under `FOCR_E2E_LONG=1`; `check.sh` runs none by default.

## Scenarios (plan §7.7, T1b set)
- **(d)** A 35-page windowed document, W=10, built by concatenating corpus pages: 35 bodies in order, 4 windows, no lookahead transcribed, `window` events with `reused`/`fallback_reason`.
- **(e)** Resume (U2-D4):
  - send SIGINT right after reading the robot `window` event with index 1;
  - assert exit 6, that a checkpoint is present, that the completed pages were written, and that the stream ends with a `run_error` carrying `finish_reason:"cancelled"`, `pages_out` and `checkpoint`, with no `run_complete`;
  - rerun with `--resume`, then `cmp` the output bytes against an uninterrupted run.

  Then the mismatch path: change W and get a refusal that names W. `--resume=recompute` then completes, labelled non-identical.
- **(f)** Robot contract: every line from steps (d), (e) and (m) validates against the `event_fields` in `robot schema` (introduced by U2-X2, extended for `window` by U2-D5).
- **(m)** Page-failure skip: a PDF with a JBIG2/vector page in the middle produces a `page` `skipped` event with the correct `source_page`, and the rest of the run continues with source-page map continuity.
- **(m″)** Replaces T1a's (m′), which U2-D1b deletes: a v2 document of N pages, where N is (page limit + 1) rounded up to the next N with N mod 10 == 1, runs windowed at W=10 in ceil(N/10) windows, exit 0, with N bodies in order. The last window has one own page.
- **(n)** Directory input: a directory of page images (natural sort) with `--multi-page` (until U2-E5a) is parsed as one document.
- **(o)** A **≥ 300-page synthetic run**:
  - record the peak RSS (must be ≤ 8 GiB at W=10 on a 16 GB laptop-class host, the M3 exit criterion) and time-to-first-page (must arrive after one window);
  - publish both in PERF_LEDGER, in the row format `scripts/check_ledgers.py` enforces (an `evidence_id` under `artifacts/perf/` with a manifest).
  - Long-running: mark the step so `check.sh` runs it only with an opt-in env such as `FOCR_E2E_LONG=1`. Document the command.
- **(q)** A 35-page windowed `--json --extract-figures` run (U2-D1b): `pages[]` has length 35, figures are named by source page, and raster bytes in flight stay ≤ (W+2) rasters.

## Acceptance criteria
- All scenarios pass on a host with the artifact. (o) has been run once, with results published.
- Logs are complete.

Spec: plan §7.7, §11 M3 exit, D14, D15, D19, D24.

title: U2-T2 — Concurrency watchdog scenarios for windowed v2 documents
description:
# U2-T2 — Concurrency watchdog scenarios for windowed v2 documents

## Goal
Extend the `many_pages_without_deadlock` CI watchdog (`tests/many_pages_without_deadlock.rs`) with **multi-page and windowed v2 document** scenarios. Today it has no multi-page scenario at all (plan §6.4). The windowed pipeline adds new sequencing that could deadlock or nest runtimes:
- the page source rasterizing between forwards;
- the checkpoint I/O between windows;
- the streaming sink callbacks;
- the per-window rayon fan-out.

## Doctrine #5 (what the watchdog protects)
- One `OcrModel` behind a cache; a **sequential** outer page/window loop.
- Each forward fans out across all cores internally via the kernel's own rayon pool.
- **Never rayon under a held lock; never a nested asupersync runtime inside a task.**
- A watchdog with pages ≫ pool size hangs on regression. That deadlock saga is why the doctrine exists.

## Scenarios
- A v2 document with pages ≫ the rayon pool size (e.g. 4× threads), unwindowed and windowed (W small, e.g. 2, to force many windows and splices).
- With a streaming sink callback that does I/O, and with checkpointing on (U2-D4; this bead depends on it and on U2-D1b's pipeline).
- With an injected window fallback (recompute) mid-run.
- The v1 `--multi-page` page-source scenario is owned by U2-D0, so it lands in M0.
- Each scenario runs under a hard timeout; exceeding it fails with a thread dump if available.

## Model gating
The test may use a tiny synthetic or random-weight configuration if the real weights are absent, so the *orchestration* is exercised in CI. With weights, it runs the real artifact. Document which is which in the test output.

## Acceptance criteria
- The new scenarios are green in CI under timeout.
- A deliberately introduced lock-held rayon call (in a local experiment, not committed) is shown to hang the watchdog, which proves the test has teeth. Record that in the bead notes.
- Mandatory checks pass.

Spec: plan §6.4, doctrine #5, D19.
acceptance_criteria:
- The new scenarios are green in CI under timeout.
- A deliberately introduced lock-held rayon call (in a local experiment, not committed) is shown to hang the watchdog, which proves the test has teeth. Record that in the bead notes.
- Mandatory checks pass.

title: U2-D1b — Windowed document pipeline: streaming page source per window, raster dropping, once-per-page vision, recognize_document integration, W=10 default
description:
# U2-D1b — Windowed document pipeline: streaming page source per window, raster dropping, once-per-page vision, recognize_document integration, W=10 default

## Goal
Turn U2-D1a's windowed decoding core into the user-facing **book pipeline**. Pages stream from disk one window at a time, rasters are dropped as soon as they are encoded, unreadable pages are skipped without shifting numbering, and the whole thing runs through the one library document API (`recognize_document`, U2-E2) that the CLI already uses.

After this bead, `focr ocr book.pdf --multi-page --model unlimited-ocr-2` works on books of any length with bounded memory, using the `PageWindow` default of W=10 for documents with N > W.

## Pipeline (plan §6.6)
```
PageSource (lazy, U2-D0) ─▶ window planner (U2-D1a) ─▶ per window:
    rasterize + preprocess own+lookahead pages ─▶ vision per page ─▶ drop rasters
    ─▶ prefill (or splice + prefill) ─▶ decode with guard ─▶ per-page bodies (token-id split)
    ─▶ sink(PageResult{source_page, text, layout, figures}) ─▶ per-window callback (checkpoint: U2-D4)
```

## Scope
1. **Page source → window inputs.**
   - Feed U2-D1a's per-window input iterator from the U2-D0 lazy page source.
   - Only the own and lookahead pages of the **current** window are rasterized. Rasters are preprocessed, vision-encoded and **dropped** before decode starts, so the rasters in flight are bounded by W+1 (D19).
   - Rasterization runs on the orchestrating thread **between** forwards, never concurrently with one (doctrine #5, plan §6.4).
2. **Once-per-page vision.**
   - The lookahead page is encoded once, in window k. Its KV is copied into window k+1, never re-encoded.
   - Fallback recomputes re-encode by design. Count them separately.
3. **Skipped pages (D24).**
   - A page that fails to rasterize gets a `page` `skipped` event. It is excluded from the window's prompt and keeps its slot in the source-page map. The planner counts only decodable pages.
   - `PageResult.source_page` and `half` come from the map, so numbering never shifts.
4. **`recognize_document` integration (U2-E2).**
   - `PageWindow::N` and `PageWindow::Off` become live options.
   - The **default for v2 document mode becomes W=10**: unwindowed when N ≤ 10, windowed otherwise.
   - This lifts U2-B6's pre-windowing page limit. Documents above it are now windowed instead of refused.
   - An explicit `PageWindow::Off` requests unwindowed decoding whatever N is. It bypasses U2-B6's refusal and relies on the exit-5 position stop, so nothing truncates silently.
   - The 131,072-position limit applies per window.
5. **CLI document mode** (`--multi-page` with v2, directory input) runs through this path. Windowing flags are U2-D5, so until then the CLI uses the default.
6. **v1 is untouched.** v1 multi-page keeps its own semantics; U2-T3 stays green.
7. **Per-page layout and figures.**
   - As each page completes, run U2-E3's per-page layout function with that page's `(width, height)` from the U2-D0 map.
   - With `--extract-figures`, re-fetch the page via `PageSource::fetch`, crop its figures, write them, and drop the raster.
   - Raster bytes in flight stay ≤ (W+2) rasters: own pages, the lookahead, and one re-fetch.

## Tests
- **Model-gated:** a 25-page synthetic document (concatenated corpus pages) through `recognize_document` with the default W=10. It yields 25 `PageResult`s in order, with correct `source_page`, and no lookahead transcribed.
- **Skip mid-window:** a synthetic PDF with a JBIG2 or vector page in window 2. The page is skipped with the right `source_page`, later pages keep correct numbering, and the window plan adjusts.
- **Vision encode counter:** encodes = decodable pages + fallback recomputes, with no lookahead re-encodes.
- **Raster memory:** under a 40-page run, peak raster bytes in flight ≤ (W+1) × the largest page raster. Log the measured RSS.
- **Limit lifted:** a (limit + 1)-page v2 document is no longer refused; it runs windowed (model-gated, can share the 25-page fixture machinery at W=2).
- The `many_pages_without_deadlock` watchdog still passes. U2-T2 adds windowed scenarios.
- **Figures in windowed mode** (model-gated): a 25-page windowed `--json --extract-figures` run names figures by source page, and raster bytes in flight stay ≤ (W+2) rasters.

## Acceptance criteria
Tests are green, the U2-T3 gate (v1 lane, plus the v2 lane once U2-C4 adds it) is green, and the mandatory checks pass. bd-3gyt and bd-paom stay consistent with the shared PDF page source (`PdfPages::render`, U2-D0) (related beads).

If `scripts/uocr2_e2e.sh` (U2-T1a) exists when this lands, delete its step (m′) (the pre-windowing refusal), since it no longer applies to the default path. If it does not exist yet, U2-T1a must not add (m′). U2-T1b's (m″) owns the windowed replacement scenario.

## Logging
- `FOCR_TIMING` row `window`. The `pagesource` row is U2-D0's, and `vision.page` is U2-F1's.
- The run summary records windows, skipped pages, vision encodes and fallback recomputes.

Spec: plan §6.6, §6.4, D13, D17, D19, D24.

Tests are green, the U2-T3 gate (v1 lane, plus the v2 lane once U2-C4 adds it) is green, and the mandatory checks pass. bd-3gyt and bd-paom stay consistent with the shared PDF page source (`PdfPages::render`, U2-D0) (related beads).

If `scripts/uocr2_e2e.sh` (U2-T1a) exists when this lands, delete its step (m′) (the pre-windowing refusal), since it no longer applies to the default path. If it does not exist yet, U2-T1a must not add (m′). U2-T1b's (m″) owns the windowed replacement scenario.

description:
# U2-A4 — Tokenizer v2: added tokens 128827–128830, v2 tokenizer pin, conformance vs HF

## Goal
Make franken_ocr's tokenizer **token-id-exact** against HF for v2's `tokenizer.json`, including the four new added tokens, and pin that file. v1 already has tokenizer conformance (OQ-16), and this bead extends it to v2. It is a prerequisite for every downstream parity gate (AGENTS testing policy).

## Facts (verified 2026-10-28)
- The v2 `tokenizer.json` is 9,980,278 B, sha256 `c55c165e32c5a67830362a53e1f548c8930dcc8469efa30ff3252a982799c589`.
- Same BPE model, pre-tokenizer, normalizer and decoder as v1. The normalizer is empty.
- **4 new added tokens, all non-special** (`special: false`):

  | Token | Id |
  |---|---|
  | `<PAGE>` | 128827 |
  | `<BLOCK>` | 128828 |
  | `<FORK>` | 128829 |
  | `<CHILD>` | 128830 |

  Only `<PAGE>` is used by inference code.
- The v1 truth pack's `tokenizer.md` says the max producible id is 128826. For v2 it is 128830. Update the truth pack.
- franken_ocr's tokenizer already splits on **all** added tokens, longest-first, regardless of the `special` flag (`src/tokenizer/mod.rs`: the longest-first sort at `:362`, `split_on_added` at `:617`, called from `encode` at `:544`; the special-id table is at `:86-119`). It decodes non-special added tokens literally even with `skip_special`, so `<PAGE>` should already work.
- This bead **proves** that, rather than assuming it.

## Scope
1. **Fixtures.** Generate HF reference tokenizations with the pinned stack (tokenizers 0.21.4 `tokenizers.Tokenizer` over this exact tokenizer.json, the object `LlamaTokenizerFast` wraps, as the v1 generator does) for a corpus that includes:
   - the v2 prompt `"<PAGE><image>"*n + "Multi page parsing."` for n = 1, 3 and 20, encoded with `add_special_tokens=False`;
   - text with `<PAGE>` adjacent to letters, digits, CJK, whitespace and newlines;
   - each of the 4 new tokens;
   - grounding-grammar strings (`<|ref|>…<|/ref|><|det|>[[…]]<|/det|>`);
   - typical OCR output (markdown, tables, LaTeX) in English and Chinese.

   Store the fixtures beside the v1 ones (`tests/fixtures/tokenizer_baidu/expected.json`), as a v2 file, e.g. `expected_uocr2.json`. Extend the existing generator, `scripts/gen_token_id_fixtures.py` (its `FOCR_BAIDU_*` env inputs already parameterize the tokenizer, corpus and output); do not fork it.
2. **Conformance test.** Encode and decode are id-exact and string-exact against the fixtures.
3. **Property and fuzz tests.**
   - Splitting added tokens is idempotent.
   - `<PAGE>` round-trips.
   - A fuzz test over random interleavings of added tokens and text: decode(encode(s)) == s, and encode never splits an added token.
4. **Pin (publish only).** Publish the v2 tokenizer SHA-256 and the required id set as named constants or data next to the v1 tokenizer pins: {128827 `<PAGE>`, 128815 `<image>`, 0 BOS, 1 EOS}. **U2-A5 depends on this bead and wires them** into the arch registry's `tokenizer_sha256()` and `required_token_ids()`, whose methods U2-A2 created. This bead does not edit the registry.

## Acceptance criteria
- The v2 conformance test is green and the fuzz test runs in CI (bounded iterations).
- v1 tokenizer conformance is unchanged.
- The truth pack `tokenizer.md` gains the v2 section (max id 128830).
- OQ-V2-8 is updated with this bead's conformance evidence. U2-A5 closes it as RESOLVED once the required-token check is wired into the registry.

## Notes
The fixture generator runs in the v2 oracle venv (U2-A6 pins). If A6 hasn't landed, use a minimal pinned venv with just `tokenizers==0.21.4` and `transformers==4.52.1` (tokenizer-only), recorded in PROVENANCE.md.

Spec: plan §5.1.

title: U2-D2a — Independent Python windowed oracle, written from the SGLang wheel source (not from the Rust implementation)
description:
# U2-D2a — Independent Python windowed oracle, written from the SGLang wheel source (not from the Rust implementation)

## Goal
Build the reference that U2-D1a's windowed decoding is gated against. HF `infer()` never splits documents. The only windowed implementation is a **GPU-only SGLang wheel** (R9), and the dev host has no CUDA (R13). So we re-implement SGLang's windowed semantics in Python, on top of the HF model's DASH cache, running in f32 on CPU.

## Independence rule (D5; review P6) — the whole point of this bead
- Write this oracle **from the SGLang wheel source** (`session/uocr_doc_reuse.py`, `entrypoints/openai/doc_split.py`, `layers/attention/unlimited_ocr_v2_backend.py`, `environ.py`), from the pinned wheel's source files only (U2-A1 pins the wheel by SHA-256), never from the U2-A1 truth-pack notes or SGLang spec comment, which are the first reading.
- It must be written by a **different author** than U2-D1a's Rust implementer, and **before** that code exists: U2-D1a depends on this bead. Otherwise a misreading of the semantics gets implemented twice and "passes".
- **Read order.** Do not read plan §5.10, the U2-D1a bead or U2-A1's SGLang spec comment until this bead's self-tests pass. Those are one reading of the wheel, and this oracle must be a second, independent one. Never read the Rust code.
- After the self-tests pass, compare against plan §5.10. Where the wheel and the plan or U2-D1a disagree, **the wheel wins**. Record the disagreement in this bead's notes, so the plan and U2-D1a get fixed.

## Scope
`scripts/gen_reference_fixtures_uocr2.py --windowed W`, extending U2-A6's script in U2-A6's pinned venv.
1. **Port function by function** onto the HF model's DASH cache (f32, CPU). Keep each wheel function's name and `file:line` in a comment. Files are under `sglang/srt/` in the pinned wheel:
   - `entrypoints/openai/doc_split.py`: planning, prompt splitting, guard parameters and stitching (`tokens_per_page`, `plan_batches`, `split_messages`, `page_guard_params`, `page_limit_for_mode`, and the **streaming** path `stream_owned_text`/`owned_page_bodies`);
   - `session/uocr_doc_reuse.py`: retention, splice and replay (`parse_prompt`, `plan_tail_copy`, `text_tail`, `tail_ranges`, `replay_page_isolation`, `replay_coords`, `continuation_carry`, `_refresh_kbar`, `_write_page_state`, `_seed_continuation`, `_apply_segment`, `_cut_at_extra_marker`), plus the retention gating and fallback conditions in `on_cache_finished_req` and `try_match_prefix`;
   - `sampling/custom_logit_processor.py:194-262` (`_page_guard`);
   - `layers/attention/unlimited_ocr_v2_backend.py:1001-1031` (page coordinates with `page_base`);
   - `environ.py` for defaults.
2. **Server machinery:** where the wheel depends on server machinery (batching, overlap scheduling, KV pools, retraction), substitute the simplest sequential equivalent and list each substitution in the notes. Use the README server configuration (per-page cap 20,000, full guard) and `ctx` = 131,072.
3. **Test hook:** a parameter that forces a named fallback reason for a given window. Natural fallbacks cannot be triggered with real v2 pages.
4. **Dumps per window:** the plan, splice row indices, replayed page coordinates (img_page, query page, bucket, tok_pos), page_base, generated ids and bodies.

## Tests (of the oracle itself)
- **Degenerate case:** with W ≥ N, the windowed oracle, run through its own loop (one window, no lookahead; never by delegating to `infer_multi`), equals the unwindowed HF `infer_multi` output token-for-token.
- **Recompute case:** a recompute window forced through the test hook must equal, token for token up to and including the `<PAGE>` that opens the lookahead page, an unwindowed run of the oracle's own decode loop over the same pages + lookahead. That run is configured the way the wheel configures a recomputed window: derive page_base, the expected marker count, end_on_marker and the logit-processor order from the wheel source, and record them in the notes. HF `infer_multi` cannot serve as that reference, because its page parity, expected count and processor order follow an unwindowed request.
- **Determinism:** two runs and two thread counts give the same tokens (the U2-A6 floor methodology).
- If a GPU host is ever available, compare once against the real SGLang wheel. That comparison is **informational** because of DISC-U2-1/5/8.

## Acceptance criteria
- The oracle runs on 5–9-page base documents at W=2 and W=3, with at least one N mod W == 1 case, and produces dumps.
- The self-tests above pass.
- Commands are recorded in `tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md`.
- Disagreements with plan §5.10 are listed (or "none").

Spec: plan §5.10, §7.5, D5, R8, R9.

# U2-D2a notes: the windowed SGLang oracle (`--windowed W`)

I wrote this oracle from the pinned wheel `sglang-0.5.20.dev10+g8d62f5fb9c` (sha256 `a3f3e2c9…c2ba70d`), read as text and never imported, and the HF snapshot `5632329a`. I read plan §5.10 and U2-D1a only after every self-test below had passed. The bead stays open.

## Deliverable

- **Script.** `scripts/gen_reference_fixtures_uocr2.py`, section "Windowed long-document decoding (bead U2-D2a)". The final runs used sha256 `5edc7645e72207c6b02724134907dcd721273e22e303a533344d2c1627780e92`.
- **New options.**
  - `--windowed W --doc FIXTURE[:N]`: N is the first N pages of a fixture's page list.
  - `--force-fallback BI:REASON`: repeatable.
  - `--windowed-check degenerate,extend,recompute`.
  - `--windowed-compare RUN,RUN,...`: model-free determinism comparison.
  - `--self-test --windowed W`: adds 25 model-free checks of the ports.
- **Existing behaviour is unchanged.** Plain `--self-test` prints the same 8 checks as before. The fixture path runs only when `--windowed` is absent.
- **Ports.** Each port carries its wheel function name and `file:line`:
  - `doc_split.py`: `tokens_per_page`, `completion_capacity`, `effective_max_page_tokens`, `window_output_cap`, `plan_batches`, `split_messages`/`_retag_markers`, `select_batch_output`, `stream_owned_text`, `window_incomplete`, `owned_page_bodies`, `page_guard_params`, `page_limit_for_mode`.
  - `serving_chat.py`: `_window_pages`, `_plan_doc_split`, `_window_lookahead`, `_window_capacity`, `_window_request`, `_apply_page_cap`, and the `_split_document_stream` loop (SC:1043-1189), run sequentially.
  - `uocr_doc_reuse.py`: `_page_base`, `is_image_token`, `parse_prompt`, `plan_tail_copy`, `text_tail`, `tail_ranges`, `replay_page_isolation`, `replay_coords`, `continuation_carry`, `_write_page_state`, `_seed_coord_row`, `_seed_continuation`, `_apply_segment`, `_restore_prompt`, `_drop_reuse`, `_cut_at_extra_marker`, `on_cache_finished_req`/`_trim_to_tails`, `try_match_prefix`, `_rewrite_prompt`, `_build_reuse`, `after_prefill_forward`, `hide_forced_text`, `next_page_after`, `_splice_text`.
  - `custom_logit_processor.py`: `_page_guard` (CLP:194-262) and the processor `__call__` (CLP:269-387).
  - Page state and coordinates: the PS `step`, `block_page_bounds` and `build_query_allow`; the PR `step` and `page_capacity`.
  - BE:1001-1031: `note_prompt_lens` and `_shift_page_coords` (page_base % 2).
  - `environ.py` defaults: ENV:1352-1423.
  - Finish order: SB:1843.
  - Skipping the prefill sample: BRP:358-361.
  - Completion tokens: OS:493.
- **Test hook.** `--force-fallback BI:REASON` takes one of nine reasons, each cited to its wheel lines in `FALLBACK_REASONS`:
  - eight reasons recompute the window: `no_entry`, `page_mismatch`, `layout_mismatch`, `no_text`, `alloc_failed`, `straddle`, `planning_exception`, and `pool_too_small` (`_drop_reuse` after the rewrite, with `_restore_prompt`);
  - `splice_alloc_failed` falls back to the marker-only splice.

  Not modelled: a retracted follow-up (DR:956) and aborts.

## Server-machinery substitutions

This list is also written into every `run.json`.

1. **Scheduler.** One request at a time, windows in plan order. There is no batching, overlap scheduling, CUDA graphs or chunked prefill. The README sets `--max-prefill-tokens 2048`, and every window prompt here is shorter.
2. **Prefetch** (ENV:1368, on). A follow-up window is built after its predecessor finishes, with max_new = min(remaining − used, capacity). That is the cap DP:65-123 applies, with used = output minus forced tokens (OS:493-499).
3. **KV pool, allocator, req_to_token, eviction.**
   - Each window has its own tensors, indexed by logical row.
   - The copy (`move_kv_cache`) gathers main K, V and the index key of the source rows.
   - Allocation never fails unless a failure is forced.
   - A retained window keeps all its rows, but every row a follow-up reads is checked against `tail_ranges` (counter `read_outside_kept`).
4. **Retraction, aborts and disconnects** do not occur.
5. **kbar is not cached.** HF `_block_scores_infer` recomputes each block summary from the stored index keys on every call. Those are the values the full-block refreshes give: `_refresh_kbar` (DR:443-457) for copies and splices, and `kbar_all_plan`/`kbar_tail_plan` (route_triton.py:576, 682), which recompute the boundary block with all its rows. Only blocks `local_blocks` or more behind the query are scored, and those are complete.
6. **Attention and routing math** use HF's reference functions instead of SGLang's Triton kernels: MD `_router_qk`, `_block_scores_infer`, `_infer_route_select` (topm 16, which is also the wheel's `TOPM_DEFAULT`, dash_router.py:16), `_decode_attend`, and `DashAttention._forward_dense` generalised to a query-row offset for extends over a copied prefix.
7. **Page isolation and RoPE coordinates** come from the PS/PR PyTorch step paths, ported for one request.
8. **Index keys** are stored in f32, as HF keeps them.
9. **Prompt ids and pixels** come from HF `_uocr_build_inputs`: BOS + `<PAGE><image>`×n + "Multi page parsing.", with 273 image tokens per base page. This is the layout SGLang's chat template and `tokenize_with_images` build. Image placeholders keep the raw id 128815, not pad values; `is_image_token` treats both alike.
10. **Vision for a reused window's extend** is base-mode page features recomputed with HF's own module calls. A straddling item contributes only its last row.
11. **Detokenizer.** The window text is `tokenizer.decode(skip_special_tokens=False)` of the output minus its stop token. The spliced text is removed as a decoded prefix (`hide_forced_text`). The server's fastokens backend is not used.
12. **Streaming.** Ownership is computed once on the final window text. `stream_owned_text`'s result is a prefix of every later call's, so what is streamed equals the last chunk's result.
13. **Context.** Planning and capacity use ctx = 131,072 (the task setting). The wheel uses `max_req_input_len` ≤ 131,066 (SC:378, tp_worker.py:544-557). This cannot matter at W ≤ 6, where fits = 478 either way and the page cap binds the capacity. `page_capacity(131072)` = 1773.
14. **Sampling.** Temperature 0, so each token is the argmax of the processed f32 logits.

## Recompute-reference configuration (wheel lines)

A recomputed window is compared with a plain request run through the oracle's own loop. The plain request carries no document id, so `try_match_prefix` returns None (DR:952-954). It uses the same pages, lookahead and max_new_tokens as the window, and the custom params {README params, `uocr_doc_page_base: lo`, `uocr_doc_lookahead: la`}.

- **Prompt.** The window's own sent prompt: BOS + `<PAGE><image>`×(hi−lo+la) + "Multi page parsing." (SC:504-512 → DS:170-234).
  - Every forced reason before DR:1095 leaves it untouched.
  - `pool_too_small` restores it (DR:662-681, called from `_drop_reuse` DR:684-691).
- **page_base = lo.**
  - SC:513-516 sets `uocr_doc_page_base: lo`.
  - `_restore_prompt` clears `_uocr_page_base` (DR:666), so `_page_base` falls back to the param (DR:109-122).
  - `note_prompt_lens` stores lo % 2 (DR:84-106 → BE:1001-1010).
  - `_shift_page_coords` adds it where page > 0 (BE:1012-1031).
- **Expected markers = hi − lo** (CLP:229-237), with `_uocr_context_pages = 0` (DR:668) and lookahead = la from the params (SC:515, CLP:332).
- **end_on_marker = (la > 0)** (CLP:227), with `_uocr_end_on_marker = False` (DR:669). For a recomputed last window (la = 0) it is false, so `<PAGE>` is masked on its last page (CLP:256-262) and the comparison runs through EOS.
- **No `page_stop_only`.** SC:519-521 asks for stop_only, but `page_guard_params` returns {} because the request's own cap (20,000) ≤ the server cap (DS:323-325).
- **Processor order: guard first.**
  - A forced token sets every logit to −inf and the forced one to 0.0, and skips the n-gram (CLP:327-339).
  - Otherwise the n-gram ban runs on `req.output_ids` only (ENV:1423, CLP:287-290, CLP:343-385), with ngram_size 35 and window_size 1024 (README request).
- **max_new_tokens** = min(remaining, capacity) (SC:1213, SC:482-502).

## Self-test results (final set, macOS arm64; walls are `/usr/bin/time` real, model load included)

- **Model-free.**
  - `--self-test --windowed 2` passes 33/33: the 8 existing checks plus 25 windowed ones.
  - Plain `--self-test` output is byte-identical to before.
- **Degenerate** (S2-p9_p14_p19, N = 3, W = 3: plan None, unsplit; run 249 s).
  - The oracle's own loop gives 2152 tokens (stop), equal to HF `infer_multi`'s 2152, with no first difference.
  - It also equals the committed `tests/fixtures/uocr2_oracle/S2-p9_p14_p19.ids.txt`.
  - Oracle 119.5 s, HF 111.3 s.
  - HF layer-0 cross-checks: coordinates and candidate masks equal on 2153/2153 forward steps.
  - The wheel guard masked `<PAGE>` on 1842 last-page steps and EOS on 311 steps without changing any argmax.
- **Extend split.** This validates the generalised prefill over a cached prefix (same run).
  - The vision-replica embeddings are bitwise equal to HF's native vision path.
  - Prefill split at rows 333, 416 and 826 (of 827) against the whole prefill: argmax equal and coordinate rows equal.
  - Max |Δ| at those splits: logits 4.1e-5 to 6.3e-5, keys ≤ 5.1e-5, index keys ≤ 1.4e-5 (tolerance 1e-3).
- **Recompute** (S3-p10:7, W = 2, forced `1:pool_too_small`, `2:no_text`, `3:no_entry`; run 364 s). Every recomputed window equals its reference:

  | Window | Pages | page_base | Tokens equal | Window wall | Reference wall |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | w1 | 2–3 + lookahead 4 | 2 | 1512 through the `<PAGE>` that opens the lookahead page; whole output incl. forced EOS (1513) also equal | 73.2 s | 71.6 s |
  | w2 | 4–5 + lookahead 6 | 4 | 1546 through that `<PAGE>` (1547 with EOS) | 72.5 s | 74.4 s |
  | w3 | 6, last window, lookahead 0 | 6 | 596 through EOS | 24.4 s | 24.2 s |

  For w3, end_on_marker is false and `<PAGE>` was masked on 595 steps.
- **Determinism.** w2-n7 ran twice at 12 threads and once at 4 threads (291, 264 and 234 s). `--windowed-compare` passes: the plan, every window's prompt and output ids, texts, splice rows and every per-row array are identical.
- **Internal invariants (every final run).**
  - Every copied or spliced row holds the planned ids.
  - `read_outside_kept` = 0; for example, 1622 retained rows read in w2-n7-t12.
  - Copied and spliced RoPE page parity equals the frame value (0 mismatches).
  - HF layer-0 coordinates and masks are equal on every fresh-window step.

## Runs and dumps

Dump root: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jemanuel-projects-franken-ocr/0e68861b-d16c-4ae1-8786-16748171bc4f/scratchpad/uocr2_windowed_oracle/final2/`. It is a session scratch directory; the commands are in `tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md`.

- Each tag has `<tag>/run.json` and `<tag>/w<bi>/window.json` + `rows.*.npy`:
  - per-row arrays: ids, origin, src_row, q_page, bucket, tok_pos, rope_page, frame_bucket, frame_rope_page, img_page, marker_cum, img_run, prompt_pages;
  - per window: the plan, page_base (param, effective, shift), the TailCopyPlan, splice rows and source rows, forced ids, iso/coord seeds, sent and rewritten prompt ids, output and generated ids, text, owned bodies, guard counts and retention.
- Each tag also has a log, `<tag>.log`.
- Superseded: `../<tag>/` (the first set, with the same ids but without the frame columns) and `../final/` (a stopped partial run).

| Tag | Document | W | Plan | Generated tokens per window | Reuse | Wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| degenerate-s2-w3-t12 | S2 (3 pages) | 3 | unsplit | 2152 | – | 249 s |
| w2-n7-t12 | S3-p10:7 | 2 | (0,2)(2,4)(4,6)(6,7) | 311, 2581, 1546, 602 | w1–w3 reused; w3 is the one-page straddle | 291 s |
| w3-n7-t12 | S3-p10:7 | 3 | (0,3)(3,6)(6,7) | 1234, 2356, 602 | w1, w2 reused; w2 straddle | 215 s |
| w2-n7-recompute-t12 | S3-p10:7 | 2 | as above | 311, 1512, 1546, 595 | w1–w3 recomputed | 364 s |
| w2-n7-t12r, w2-n7-t4 | S3-p10:7 | 2 | as above | identical to w2-n7-t12 | as w2-n7-t12 | 264 s, 234 s |
| w2-n5-markeronly-t12 | S3-p10:5 | 2 | (0,2)(2,4)(4,5) | 311, 1506, 770 | w1 marker-only splice; w2 reused straddle | 126 s |

The token counts exclude forced tokens and the stop token. N mod W == 1 holds for N = 7 at W = 2 and W = 3, and for N = 5 at W = 2.

**Worked coordinate table, as dumped** (w2-n7-t12/w1: own pages 2–3, lookahead 4, page_base 1):

| Row | Slot img_page | Query page | Frame bucket | tok_pos | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) tail marker, row 0 | −1 | – | 1 | kept, 0 | |
| (b) tail images | 0 | – | 1 | kept | |
| (c) lookahead marker, row 134 | −1 | – | 2 | kept | |
| (c) lookahead images | 1 | – | 2 | kept | |
| first prefilled marker, row 408 | – | 2 | 3 | 0 | |
| (d) spliced text, rows 956–1083 | −1 | – | 1 | kept | marker_cum 5 = pp + 1 |
| forced `<PAGE>`, row 1084 | – | 1 | 2 | 274 = 1 + 273 | RoPE page 3 |

## Disagreements with plan §5.10 / U2-D1a (read after the self-tests passed; the wheel wins)

1. **The unwindowed `<PAGE>` ban.** U2-D1a §6 says "Unwindowed follows HF (no ban)". In the wheel, an unsplit request keeps its page guard (SC:348-356 `_apply_page_cap`; the README request names the processor), and its `end_on_marker` is false (CLP:227). So `<PAGE>` is masked on the last page (CLP:256-262). Plan §5.10.7 states the wheel behaviour correctly. In S2 the mask fired on 1842 steps without effect, but W ≥ N runs can differ from SGLang wherever the model would emit an extra `<PAGE>` on the last page.
2. **"Keep exactly these KV rows"** (plan §5.10.3, U2-D1a §3). The wheel retains whole 32-row KV pages: `tail_ranges` rounds each span out to `page_size`, clamped to the allocation (DR:359-360), and `_trim_to_tails` frees only the gaps (DR:924-932). Only rows (a) to (d) are ever read. This affects memory accounting only.
3. **The fallback list** (plan §5.10.5 (i)–(vii), U2-D1a §5) misses three wheel paths:
   - `_build_reuse` raising, which recomputes (DR:963-971);
   - a matched follow-up that cannot be admitted with nothing running, which drops its reuse after the prompt rewrite and restores the prompt (`on_no_token` → `_drop_reuse` → `_restore_prompt`, DR:792-795, 684-691, 662-681);
   - a finished window whose prompt does not parse, which is not retained (`next_page_after` None, DR:884-885).

   Separately, the `cache.page_size != bs` check (DR:1047) cannot fire, because the model override forces page_size to 32 (arg_groups/model_overrides/unlimited_ocr_v2.py:24-32).
4. **The "Gate page" column of the worked table** (plan §5.10.4, U2-D1a §4). For the non-image rows (the tail marker (a), the lookahead marker in (c), and the text tail (d)), the page-state slot the wheel writes holds img_page −1 (DR:383-385; DR:1274 writes `(-1, *plan.iso)` for spliced text). The table's 0 / 1 / 0 are those rows' query pages in the new frame, and copied or spliced rows are never queries there. Everything else in the table matches the dumps (see above).
5. **Plan §5.10.1 "the wheel would still split if max_tokens exceeded capacity (:149-156)".** The wheel does not split. It returns one window `[(0, N, 0)]`, with no lookahead and max_tokens clamped to its capacity (DS:155-156). This is wording only.
6. **The context default formula** (plan §5.10.1, U2-D1a §1). The W in `(W+la)·2034 + W·max_page_tokens + 1024` is max(GUNDAM_PAGE_WINDOW, BASE_PAGE_WINDOW) (configs/model_config.py:317-320). The default is 131,072 outright when DOC_LIMIT is off or the cap ≤ 0 (model_config.py:315-316). Under the README configuration this changes nothing.
7. **"HF infer_multi is not that reference when lo is odd"** (plan §5.10.5). HF is not the reference for any window with a lookahead, whatever lo's parity:
   - HF's expected count includes the lookahead page (MU:1141), while the wheel's does not and the wheel ends on the marker (CLP:227-237);
   - the n-gram/guard order differs.

   Parity is the only reason tied to odd lo.

## Observations

- **Reuse changes page 2 of S3-p10:7 at W = 2**, a dot-leader list of illustrations. With the spliced text tail, its body is 3774 chars with 1186 '.'. It is 1736 chars with 185 '.' when that window is recomputed, splices only the marker, or (at W = 3) sits in a fresh window. The non-dot text is similar (1453 vs 1521 chars), and pages 3–6 differ little (difflib ratio ≥ 0.99). The spliced page-1 tail is itself dot leaders, so this looks like model behaviour, not a port error. Nothing outside the oracle confirms reused windows, though.
- **The straddling token of a one-page last window** takes the page's last feature row as its embedding. In base mode that row is `view_seperator` (MU forward, base branch), so it does not depend on the image. The wheel still encodes the item (DR:284-286), but its value is the constant row.

## Not done / uncertain

- **No real SGLang run** (it needs CUDA). Fresh windows are cross-checked against HF at layer 0. Reused windows are checked only by the invariants above and by reading the code. HF has no reuse path to compare against.
- **The Triton routing and attention kernels are not reproduced.** Their equality to HF's reference math is assumed from the sources, not measured.
- **Not exercised in a run**, though implemented:
  - the forced reasons `page_mismatch`, `layout_mismatch`, `alloc_failed`, `straddle` and `planning_exception`, which take the same recompute path as `no_text`/`no_entry`;
  - a recomputed window with odd lo (page shift 1 on a full prompt). Reused windows exercise shift 1.
- **Not modelled:** retraction, aborts, the overlap-scheduling guard lag (DR:811-812), chunked prefill and the fastokens detokenizer.

# U2-D2a: verified and closed

**Authorship.** A fresh-context agent wrote the oracle, independently of the U2-D1a implementer. It was briefed with file pointers only: the wheel, the HF snapshot, the venv and the U2-A6 script. It was barred from plan §5.10, the windowed truth-pack notes, DISCREPANCIES, the U2-D1a and U2-A1 beads, and all Rust code until its self-tests passed. The future U2-D1a implementer has not read the oracle's code, and checked the outcomes below from outputs only.

## Checks rerun by the closer
- **Model-free self-test:** `--self-test --windowed 2` exits 0.
- **Determinism:** `--windowed-compare final2/w2-n7-t12,final2/w2-n7-t12r,final2/w2-n7-t4` passes, with `differing: []` against both the 12-thread rerun and the 4-thread run.
- **Degenerate W ≥ N:** `final2/degenerate-s2-w3-t12/w0/window.json` `generated_ids` (2,152) equal the committed `tests/fixtures/uocr2_oracle/S2-p9_p14_p19.ids.txt` id for id. This comparison was the closer's own, not the script's.
- **Recompute** (`final2/w2-n7-recompute-t12/run.json`): three forced windows pass (`pool_too_small` 1,512 tokens compared, `no_text` 1,546, `no_entry` 596 through EOS).

## Acceptance
- **Runs:** 5–9-page base documents at W=2 and W=3, with N mod W == 1 (N=7 at W=2 and W=3; N=5 at W=2). Dumps are under the session scratch `uocr2_windowed_oracle/final2/`; the commands in `tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md` regenerate them.
- **Self-tests:** pass.
- **PROVENANCE:** a "Windowed SGLang oracle runs (U2-D2a)" section with commands and wall times. A stray blank line that split the fixtures table was removed.
- **Disagreements with plan §5.10 and U2-D1a:** seven are listed in the notes comment above, each with wheel `file:line`. U2-D1a reconciles them against the wheel as its first step.

## Known limits, carried to U2-D2b
- Windows that reuse the previous window's KV are checked by invariants, not by an independent run, because real SGLang needs CUDA:
  - splitting a prefill at any row equals running it whole (logits within 6.3e-5, argmax equal);
  - spliced rows hold the planned ids;
  - no row is read outside the retained ranges;
  - RoPE page parity matches each row's new frame.
- **Unrun fallbacks:** five of the nine forcible reasons are implemented but not run, and a recomputed window with odd `lo` (page_base shift 1) was never run.
- **Kernels:** routing and attention use HF's reference math, not SGLang's Triton kernels.
- **S3-p10:7 page 2 at W=2:** with reuse, this dot-leader page decodes about twice as long as when recomputed. It looks like model behaviour but is unconfirmed.

# U2-X2 — v1 multi-page honest reporting: truncation and page-merge warnings, run_complete finish_reason/warnings, robot event_fields, help-text fix

## Problem (affects v1 users today)
v1 `--multi-page` can return the wrong number of pages with exit 0 and no warning, in two ways.

1. **Silent truncation.** v1 errors only when the prompt alone exceeds 32,768 positions (`src/native_engine/mod.rs:2750-2758`, a `FocrError::Other`, exit 1), which is about 295 pages. Between about 30 and 295 pages it **clamps** generation to `32,768 − prompt_len` (`mod.rs:2778-2785`; the clamp is at `:2783`). The decode loop stops at that clamp, and `finalize_multi` (`src/native_engine/postprocess.rs:497`) returns fewer than N pages. The exit code is 0. That is the common case for any real document.
2. **Page merging.** Even when v1 ends naturally at EOS, it often produces fewer page bodies than pages, so page boundaries are lost. The body count follows `finalize_multi`'s split rule (`postprocess.rs:497-515`): one body per `<PAGE>` marker, plus a non-blank leading chunk when the model skipped the opening marker (GH #17). All three recorded multi-page fixtures open with `<PAGE>` (so the leading chunk is blank and dropped), and **every one of them merges pages**:
   - `tests/fixtures/multi_page/p9_p14_raw.md`: 2 pages, 1 marker → 1 body;
   - `p10_raw.md`: 10 pages, 9 markers → 9 bodies;
   - `p20_raw.md`: 20 pages, 7 markers (10,469 output tokens, EOS, no clamp) → 7 bodies.

The help and docs are also wrong:
- `cli.rs:230` says "the whole document must fit the 32K context", and `cli.rs:349` says "The document must fit the 32K context (~290 pages)". About 290 pages is only where the *prompt* overflows; output space runs out near 29 dense pages.
- `README.md:411-412` says "roughly 290 pages; over-budget requests fail with an actionable error instead of truncating", which the clamp makes false.
- The library doc comment `src/lib.rs:705-714` documents only the prompt-overflow error and omits the output clamp.

## Goal
Make v1 report what actually happened, without changing any v1 output text. This is an **M0** bead: v1 users get it before any v2 code exists. It also gives U2-B6 (v2), U2-E1 (pull hints), U2-E4 (remediation) and U2-D4 (resume) one shared reporting mechanism, and gives every later bead a field-level robot schema to extend.

## Scope
1. **Terminal-event fields** (D15: additive only, `ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged). Follow the `low_yield` precedent (`src/robot.rs:155-174`, `run_complete_event_assessed`).
   - **Unchanged invariant:** `run_complete` is the SUCCESS terminal (`robot.rs:140`), and every nonzero exit ends with `run_error` (`cli.rs:3250-3259`).
   - `finish_reason` is present on every `run_complete`: `stop`, or `length` (v1 truncation only, exit 0, with `v1_truncated`).
   - On a **partial-output `run_error`** (a run that wrote completed pages and then exits nonzero), `finish_reason` is `length` (v2 position limit, exit 5), `budget` (exit 5) or `cancelled` (exit 6), together with `pages_out` and `warnings[]`. This bead defines those optional `run_error` fields in `event_fields` and the shared emitter; U2-B6 builds the partial-output path and produces `length` and `budget`, U2-D1a produces per-window `budget`, U2-E2 produces `cancelled` (cooperative cancellation in the driver), and U2-D4 adds checkpointing on those stops plus `checkpoint`/`resumed_from`.
   - **`warnings[]` shape:** `{kind, message, recovery, ...kind-specific fields}`. The key is **`recovery`**, matching `run_error`'s existing `recovery` key (`robot.rs:187`). Robot: on `run_complete` (and a partial-output `run_error`) only when non-empty, so healthy runs are unchanged apart from `finish_reason`.
   - **`--json`:** merged into the existing `warnings` array (`cli.rs:1045, 1578`; music elements `{kind, part, measure, detail}`, unchanged for music). For OCR the key appears only when non-empty. `ocr-batch --multi-page` also carries the array in its `batch.multi_page` object (`cli.rs:2224-2233`) and prints the human stderr line.
   - There is **no new event kind**. A "robot note" in older plan text means a `warnings[]` entry.
2. **Truncation detection** (v1 multi-page). Generation can stop at the token limit with fewer than N bodies (the split rule above). The cause decides the wording:
   - The 32K clamp gives kind `v1_truncated`, `{expected: N, got: K}`. stderr: "stopped after K of N pages: v1 shares 32,768 positions between prompt and output (≈29 dense pages)". `recovery`: "split the document with `--pages`, or parse pages independently (omit `--multi-page`)".
   - A user cap (`--max-length` or `FOCR_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` below the clamp) gives the same kind, with `cause: "user_cap"`. `recovery`: "raise `--max-length`".
   - `finish_reason: "length"`.
   - The **exit code stays 0** for v1. Changing v1's exit semantics could break existing pipelines; the warning and `finish_reason` are the honest signal. (v2 exits 5 on its position limit, per U2-B6; v2 is new, so it has no such constraint.)
3. **Page-merge detection.** v1 can end at EOS with fewer than N bodies. That gives kind `v1_page_merge`, `{expected: N, got: K}`, and the stderr line "v1 produced K page bodies for N pages; page boundaries in this output are unreliable". `finish_reason` stays `stop`. One function computes the body count, shared with U2-E3, which emits `pages[]` for v1 only when the count is exactly N and otherwise keeps `pages: []`.
4. **Recovery hook.** `recovery` strings come from one function, so U2-E4 can append `focr pull unlimited-ocr-2` once the artifact is published. The same function supplies the recovery text of the prompt-too-long error (`mod.rs:2750-2758`; its exit code is unchanged). Note that today's `with_pull_hint` (`cli.rs:3036-3042`) is applied only to `ModelNotFound` and names no model; U2-E4 makes it model-aware. U2-E1 uses the same `warnings[]` mechanism for its `pull_hint` kind.
5. **Help and docs.** Fix `cli.rs:230`, `cli.rs:349` and `README.md:411-412` to "32,768 positions shared by prompt and output (≈29 dense pages); longer documents stop early and report `finish_reason: length` with a `v1_truncated` warning". Fix the `src/lib.rs:705-714` doc comment to mention the output clamp and the warnings. `cli.rs:34` is the `DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH` constant, not help text; leave it.
6. **Test-only position override.** Add `DecodeParams.max_positions` (`#[doc(hidden)]`, not a CLI flag; default is the arch's context, 32,768 for v1). The v1 clamp computes from it. It is also settable through a hidden env var, **`FOCR_TEST_MAX_POSITIONS`**, read once at startup, so CLI and e2e tests can reach the clamp and position-limit branches on small documents.
   - A value above the arch's context is refused with exit 2.
   - It is listed as test-only in `robot.rs::ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES` and on U2-A7's `UOCR2_LEVER_POLICY` allow-list.
   - U2-B6 reuses the same parameter for v2 (131,072).
7. **`event_fields` and contract upkeep.**
   - Add `event_fields: {<kind>: {required: [...], optional: [...]}}` to `robot_schema()` (`robot.rs:100-126`) for every kind in `EVENT_KINDS`. `stage` has no emitter today, so it is listed as `{reserved: true}`. Today the schema lists only event kinds, so nothing can validate an event's fields.
   - Add a stream contract test: every event emitted in `tests/cli_robot_golden.rs` validates against `event_fields`.
   - Every later bead that adds fields extends `event_fields` in the same change (U2-A7, D0, B6, E1, E3, D4, D5).
   - Regenerate `tests/fixtures/robot_schema_v1.json` with `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` as a **reviewed** golden change, update the schema `status` string, and update `tests/cli_robot_golden.rs`.
   - Add rows to `docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md` §13 (`tests/surface_matrix.rs` parses that table).

## Tests
- **Clamp branch** (model-gated v1): a 3-page document with `FOCR_TEST_MAX_POSITIONS` set so the clamp falls inside page 2. Assert:
  - the `v1_truncated` warning with the expected and got counts;
  - `finish_reason:"length"`;
  - the stderr line;
  - exit 0;
  - output text byte-equal to the same run without the reporting change.
- **User-cap branch:** `--max-length` below the clamp gives `cause:"user_cap"` and the "raise `--max-length`" recovery.
- **Page merge** (model-free): feed each recorded `*_raw.md` text with its page count through the detection function and assert the exact numbers: `p20` → `v1_page_merge` expected 20, got 7; `p10` → expected 10, got 9; `p9_p14` → expected 2, got 1.
- **Healthy multi-page cases** (model-free, synthetic): a 3-page string with 3 markers gives 3 bodies and no warning; a 3-page string with a non-blank leading chunk and 2 markers gives 3 bodies and no warning (GH #17).
- **Healthy run** (model-gated): a single-page v1 run has no `warnings` key and `finish_reason:"stop"`.
- **Single-page cap** (model-gated): a single-page v1 run stopped by `--max-length` reports `finish_reason:"length"` and no warning (the truncation warnings are multi-page only).
- **Override bounds:** `FOCR_TEST_MAX_POSITIONS` above 32,768 exits 2.
- **JSON surfaces:** OCR `--json` carries the new entries in `warnings`; the existing music `--json` warning tests stay green; `ocr-batch --multi-page --json` carries `warnings` in `batch.multi_page`.
- **Robot contract:** every emitted event validates against `event_fields` (the stream contract test), and the schema golden diff is reviewed.
- **Help snapshot:** the corrected text appears for `--multi-page`, in README.md and in the library doc comment.
- **U2-T3 gate green:** v1 markdown and token ids are unchanged.

## Logging
One NDJSON line per test case per `docs/TEST_LOGGING.md`, with `test`, `case`, `event`, `result`, `expected_pages`, `markers`, `bodies`, `finish_reason`, `warning_kinds` and `exit_code`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Tests are green and the mandatory checks pass.
- The U2-T3 gate is green, with v1 output text unchanged.
- `robot schema` carries `event_fields` for every kind, the stream contract test is green, and the schema golden change is reviewed and recorded.
- CHANGELOG notes the new v1 warnings, `event_fields` and the help text.

title: U2-A6b — S5 oracle fixture: one 40–60-page document (from U2-C5a's sourced set), unwindowed f32
description:
# U2-A6b — S5 oracle fixture: one 40–60-page document, unwindowed f32

## Goal
Generate the oracle fixture U2-A6 deferred: one 40–60-page document with ground truth, run unwindowed through HF Unlimited-OCR-2 in f32 on CPU. U2-D2b's windowed-vs-unwindowed accuracy comparison consumes it (plan §7.1, fixture row S5).

## Why deferred from U2-A6
- The document must come from U2-C5a's sourced MarathonDocBench subset (Apache-2.0). C5a owns the source, license and manifest records, and A6 should not pick an unvetted document.
- It is also the costliest run. f32 wall time grew 4.6× from 10 to 20 pages (852 s → 3,941 s at 12 threads, load avg ~30, RSS ~19–21 GB). Extrapolated, that is ~5 h for 40 pages and ~12 h for 60 per run, and the floor needs a second run.

## Work
1. Add a document input to `scripts/gen_reference_fixtures_uocr2.py`, e.g. `--doc NAME=DIR` (a directory of page images, natural order), producing fixture `S5-<name>`.
   - The script's sha256 is recorded in `ORACLE.json`, so changing it means regenerating S1–S4 or recording the new hash honestly; prefer adding the option before any other regeneration.
2. Run f32 at 12 threads with `--commit-dir`, plus one more f32 run at another thread count for the floor's `f32` group.
3. Recompute `FLOOR.json` with the same groups as `tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md` lists, and keep `check_oracle_provenance.py` green (plain, `--uocr2-dumps`, `--self-test`).
4. Record the measured hours, tokens, pages out, the DISC-U2-2 counter and the fallback rows.
   - If f32 CPU is intolerable past 40 pages, the plan's fallback applies: bf16 on GPU, recorded as ledger only, never as the oracle.

## Acceptance
`tests/fixtures/uocr2_oracle/S5-*.ids.txt` and `.md`, plus the `ORACLE.json` entry, are committed. The provenance checker is green. U2-D2b has its unwindowed reference.

title: U2-E3b — v2 block-grammar output (<BLOCK>label[box]<FORK>text): parse for layout, decide rendering; plan assumed v1's <|det|> grammar
description:
## Finding (2026-10-30, during U2-B6)

Unlimited-OCR-2 does not emit v1's grounding grammar. Every oracle fixture's `decoded_text` (f32 t12, S1–S4; `~/.cache/franken_ocr_local_models/uocr2_oracle/`) uses a block grammar built from the added tokens `<BLOCK>`=128828 and `<FORK>`=128829:

```
<PAGE><BLOCK>title[286, 207, 592, 235]<FORK>CONTENTS.
<BLOCK>title[355, 254, 528, 275]<FORK>VOLUME II.
<BLOCK>text[55, 338, 822, 878]<FORK>CHAPTER XVII.
```

- **Form:** `<BLOCK>{label}[{LEVELn}][x1, y1, x2, y2]<FORK>{text}`. `<LEVEL1>`/`<LEVEL2>` are plain BPE text (not added tokens), seen only on `title`. The tokenizer truth pack (`oq/tokenizer.md`) and the plan list these tokens as "unused by inference". That holds for the decode loop, but the model emits them.
- **Labels across the 9 fixtures:**

  | Label | Count |
  |---|---|
  | `text` | 244 |
  | `header` | 49 |
  | `page_footnote` | 41 |
  | `page_number` | 25 |
  | `cross_text` | 16 |
  | `title` with `<LEVEL2>` | 16 |
  | `append_text` | 13 |
  | `title` with `<LEVEL1>` | 7 |
  | `other` | 6 |
  | `image` | 5 |
  | `table` | 3 |
  | `image_caption` | 2 |
  | `footer` | 2 |
  | `title` with no level | 2 |

  `cross_text`/`append_text` look like cross-page continuation markers.
- **Neither reference parses it.** The HF `_uocr_save_results`/`re_match` (`modeling_unlimitedocr.py:98-117, 1207-1230`) recognizes only v1's `<|ref|>…<|det|>` and bare `<|det|>label [box]<|/det|>` forms, so its `result.md` keeps `<BLOCK>…<FORK>` raw. The SGLang wheel and dev13 sources contain neither token. Reference-faithful output therefore carries the raw grammar.

## What is wrong in the plan

- U2-B6 ("Bodies keep v1's grounding grammar … the existing postprocess per page applies unchanged") and U2-E3 ("v2 bodies keep v1's grounding grammar") assume v1's form.
- U2-B6 can stay reference-faithful: v1's postprocess passes the block grammar through untouched, as HF does.
- U2-E3's `layout`/`figures` would then be empty for v2. The markdown would carry every block's `<BLOCK>label[box]<FORK>` prefix.

## To do

1. Decide franken_ocr's v2 rendering, with a DISC entry, since no reference renders it:
   - strip the grounding to plain text, keeping the box for `layout`;
   - map `title<LEVELn>` to Markdown headings, or leave titles plain;
   - handle the furniture labels (`header`, `footer`, `page_number`, `page_footnote`);
   - decide what `cross_text`/`append_text` mean (verify against the tech report, `dl_v2_src/Unlimited-OCR-2.pdf`).
2. Parse the grammar into U2-E3's `layout`/`figures`. Boxes are 0–999 page-normalized, as in v1; verify.
3. Correct U2-B6's and U2-E3's text and the tokenizer truth-pack line.
4. Tests: a parser over all 9 oracle `decoded_text`s (every block parsed, no raw `<BLOCK>`/`<FORK>` left in rendered markdown) plus hand cases.

title: U2-A5 — Register `unlimited-ocr-2` ModelArch (implemented=false) + delta census + vision byte-identity hashes + per-model artifact version + recipe id
description:
# U2-A5 — Register `unlimited-ocr-2` ModelArch (implemented=false) + delta census + vision byte-identity hashes + per-model artifact version + recipe id

## Goal
Make v2 a **known, identifiable architecture** in the model zoo before any v2 math exists. The arch can be loaded, census-checked and reported, but `implemented() == false` until U2-B6. Every inference path must refuse it explicitly; U2-A7 enforces that.

## Scope
1. **ModelArch entry.**
   - Add `unlimited-ocr-2` to the registry (`model_arch.rs`, REGISTRY ~:545, next to `UnlimitedOcr` at :217-257).
   - The decoder family gets a new variant, `Decoder::DeepSeekV2MoeSrSwa`, alongside `Decoder::DeepSeekV2MoeRswa`.
   - `TokenizerKind` stays the DeepSeek BPE, with the v2 pin.
   - License notice: MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 Baidu" (the GitHub LICENSE text; the HF v2 repo has no LICENSE file).
   - Fill the A2 capability methods:
     - `tensor_census()`;
     - `required_quant_recipe("int8")` = `"unlimited-ocr-2-ffn-int8-attn-bf16-lmhead-bf16-v1"` (the method that now owns the former `dist::required_quant_recipe` table);
     - `artifact_version()`, with v2's own version string, e.g. `"0.1.0"`;
     - `tokenizer_sha256()` and `required_token_ids()`, wired from the pins U2-A4 publishes (this bead depends on U2-A4);
     - `unlimited_variant()` = `UnlimitedVariant::V2SrSwa` (the enum U2-A2 defines);
     - the decode-contract skeleton (B6 fills in the details).
   - `implemented() = false`.
2. **Per-model artifact version (D22).**
   - `versioned_quant_path` (`mod.rs:1022`) uses the global `UNLIMITED_OCR_ARTIFACT_VERSION` (`"0.7.0"`, `lib.rs:74`) for every id. It runs before load, from a spec path, with no arch in hand (`short_model_candidates(search_dir, spec, quant)`, `:1030`). So derive the arch from the spec's stem with `arch_by_id(stem)` (`model_arch.rs:563`), fall back to v1 for an unknown stem, and use that arch's `artifact_version()`.
   - v1 keeps `0.7.0`, so names are unchanged.
   - Short-name resolution then finds `unlimited-ocr-2.v<ver>.int8.focrq`.
3. **Delta census (D22).** Add an embedded data file, `src/native_engine/unlimited_ocr_2_manifest.json`, containing:
   - the **109 tensors v2 adds** over the v1 2,710-tensor census, each with name, shape and dtype:
     - per layer l=0..11: `model.layers.{l}.self_attn.dash_router.{q_proj.weight [128,1280], k_proj.weight [128,1280], q_norm.weight [128], k_norm.weight [128], head_cls [128]}` (60 total);
     - per layer: `model.layers.{l}.self_attn.indexer.{q_proj.weight [128,1280], k_proj.weight [128,1280], q_norm.weight [128], k_norm.weight [128]}` (48 total);
     - `model.vision_model.embeddings.position_ids` I64 [1,257], marked **verify-and-skip: arange(257)** (D8);
     
     Confirm the exact names against the pinned `model.safetensors.index.json`.
   - the SHA-256 of the canonical sorted 2,819-entry list;
   - **full-tensor SHA-256s** for every vision tower, projector, `image_newline` and `view_seperator` tensor, asserted byte-identical to v1. This is the mechanical vision-reuse proof that the old plan's "B8" bead would have provided;
   - pins:
     - HF commit `5632329a32e103d5f1add270681e0f5c1233c6e4`;
     - shard SHA-256s and sizes (see U2-A3);
     - tokenizer SHA;
     - the verified-artifact SHA, filled at U2-C3.

   Generalize `unlimited_ocr_census.rs` (:24-55, :110, :328-394) to hold the v1 census plus the v2 delta. **Do not add a second census module.**
4. **Raw arch detection (finishing A2 §4).** v2 census match → v2.
5. **Vision-identity test.** Model-gated:
   - Hash every vision, projector, newline and separator tensor in the v2 shards and compare against the v1 shard's same-name tensors and the stored hashes.
   - Any mismatch fails the test. That would invalidate the "vision reuse" premise, and the epic would have to stop and re-plan.

## Tests
- A census unit test checks that the delta plus v1 equals 2,819 entries, with no duplicate names.
- A registry test confirms that `unlimited-ocr-2` resolves, `implemented()==false`, and the capability methods return the values above.
- Model-gated: the raw v2 shards are detected as v2 and the census passes. The vision-identity test passes.
- Model-gated, moved here from U2-A3 because they need this bead's census and pins:
  - The real v2 shard pair loads through the U2-A3 resolver with the census check, in a few seconds and **without hashing**. The I64 `position_ids` is verified as `arange(257)` and skipped by the census rule.
  - U2-A3's streaming shard-hash routine, run over the real shards, matches the pinned shard SHA-256s and the multi-shard `source_sha256` convention.
- Short-name resolution: `--model unlimited-ocr-2` finds `unlimited-ocr-2.v<ver>.int8.focrq` both in the flat cache root and in a per-model cache subdirectory (synthetic files). `model_search_dirs()` (`mod.rs:917-943`) already searches the flat root, then one sorted level of subdirectories.
- The U2-T3 v1 gate is green.

## Logging
One NDJSON line per census check: tensor name, expected vs found shape and dtype, and `census_ok`. One line per vision byte-identity hash: tensor, SHA-256, and whether it matches.

## Acceptance criteria
- All of the above, plus the mandatory checks.
- OQ-V2-8 (tokenizer) is closed as RESOLVED, citing U2-A4's conformance evidence and this bead's required-token wiring.

Spec: plan §6.1, §2.2, D22, D8.
acceptance_criteria:
- All of the above, plus the mandatory checks.
- OQ-V2-8 (tokenizer) is closed as RESOLVED, citing U2-A4's conformance evidence and this bead's required-token wiring.
close_reason: Registered unlimited-ocr-2 (implemented=false) with the pinned delta census, vision byte-identity proven on the real shards, per-model artifact version, recipe id, tokenizer pins; all gates green (see comment)

title: U2-A6 — v2 reference oracle: f32 CPU primary (feasibility first), bf16 ledger, dumps, fixtures S1–S5, nondeterminism floor
description:
# U2-A6 — v2 reference oracle: f32 CPU primary (feasibility first), bf16 ledger, dumps, fixtures S1–S5, nondeterminism floor

## Goal
Build the v2 parity oracle. It must reproduce Baidu's HF `infer()` semantics exactly and dump every intermediate the parity ladder needs. The **primary oracle runs the HF reference in float32 on CPU**, which is the precedent that gave v1 token-exact parity. bf16 runs feed only the cross-precision ledger.

## Why f32 CPU (D4)
- v1's correctness oracle is labelled "CUDA-only" and has never run on the dev host (`check_oracle_provenance.py`).
- v1 reached L4 token-exact 1.0 and L5 CER 0.0 against `scripts/gen_reference_fixtures.py --device cpu --cpu-patch --f32`, fixture set `fixtures/native_f32` (`tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md`).
- With f32 on both sides, v2's discrete Token Sieve routing should match exactly, even where selection is genuinely selective (multi-page fallback queries, gundam).
- On CPU, the HF DASH code takes `_forward_dense` (SDPA, additive mask incl. bias) for prefill and `_decode_attend` for decode. These are semantically identical to the GPU Triton path; only the numerics differ (spec §5.7).

## Scope

### Step 1 — feasibility (answers OQ-V2-4; do this first)
1. Create a separate pinned venv: python 3.10, torch 2.13.0, transformers 4.52.1, tokenizers 0.21.4, addict, einops, easydict. **Never share it with the v1 oracle venv** (torch 2.10.0, transformers 4.57.1).
2. Load the model from HF commit `5632329a`.
3. Apply v1's `--cpu-patch` and `--f32` shims: `.cuda()` and autocast become no-ops (`_install_cpu_patches`, `gen_reference_fixtures.py:292-321`), and the whole pipeline computes in float32. That includes the **`Tensor.to(torch.bfloat16)` rewrite** (`_install_f32_patches`, `:324-347`; the `Tensor.to` wrapper at `:338-347`): v2's `infer()` hard-codes `transform(...).to(torch.bfloat16)` on the global view and every tile (MU:561,566; the bf16 zero crop placeholder at MU:579 is not rewritten and is unused in base mode), so without it the L0 dumps are bf16-rounded. The flags are at `:225-245`.
4. Leave `DASH_STAGE0` unset, and turn `TIME_DIAG` and `SPARSE_DIAG_LOG` off.
5. Run `infer()` on one base page and one 3-page `infer_multi`.

If a DASH path is CUDA-only, port its dense fallback into the oracle script. That is a few dozen lines on top of the HF tensors, implementing the router semantics written out in the U2-B2 bead and the block-sparse attention semantics in the U2-B3 bead (plan §5.6–5.7). Port it **from the Python source**, not from those beads, so the oracle stays independent. Verify the port once against an unpatched run: GPU bf16 if available, otherwise the HF dense path in bf16 on CPU. Record the outcome in OQ-V2-4.

### Step 2 — script `scripts/gen_reference_fixtures_uocr2.py`
Per-model oracle scripts are existing precedent, e.g. `gen_reference_fixtures_got.py`. The script:
- drives `model.infer()` / `infer_multi()` with **explicit** parameters: `no_repeat_ngram_size=35`, `ngram_window=128` (single page) or `1024` (multi-page), `max_page_tokens=20000`, `page_count_guard=True`, and an explicit `crop_mode` (False = base, True = gundam);
- passes these explicitly because HF's n-gram default is off, and Baidu's evaluation uses 35/128/1024;
- dumps, through forward hooks:
  - prompt token ids;
  - preprocessed image tensors;
  - per-layer input hidden states;
  - per layer, for selected query rows **including fallback queries** (BOS, instruction, the `<PAGE>` marker and the first 160 image tokens of pages 2..N, which covers the 97–128 fallback rows per page, decode steps): router `iq`/`ik` post-RoPE, `kbar`, block scores, candidate mask, entmax prior, and topi/bias/valid;
  - per-layer attention output;
  - final hidden state, last-position logits, generated ids;
  - per-step decode dumps for the first 64 steps and ±8 steps around every `<PAGE>`.

The dump format follows the existing oracle bridge conventions (`scripts/oracle_bridge.py`).

### Step 3 — fixture sets
| Set | Contents | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | 3 single pages from the 20-page corpus: **`page_0590`** (the long table page and the hard-EOS case), **`page_0009`** and **`page_0014`**. These are the same names U2-T3 captures for v1. | base, `crop_mode=False` |
| S2 | one 3-page document: `page_0009`, `page_0014`, `page_0019` in that order (the first three pages of the p20 set) | base multi |
| S3 | existing `tests/fixtures/multi_page/{p9_p14,p10,p20}` inputs | v2 base multi |
| S4 | `page_0590`, plus one page wider than 640 px whose tile grid is not square (pick it from the corpus and record its name) | gundam, `crop_mode=True` |
| S5 | one 40–60 page MarathonDocBench document with ground truth (Apache-2.0) | unwindowed; CPU f32 if time allows (record the hours), else bf16 GPU as ledger-only |
| S1-corpus | v2 f32 CPU single-page base references (ids and markdown) for all 20 corpus pages, one run each: the U2-C4 gate input. Also **v1 f32 CPU references** for the same 20 pages, from the existing `gen_reference_fixtures.py --device cpu --cpu-patch --f32` generator (the `native_f32` precedent), so C4's v1 baseline uses the same reference precision. Not an M0 exit item: generate it any time before U2-C4. U2-G1 reuses this script with `crop_mode=True` for its gundam references. | base, `crop_mode=False` |

Large dumps live beside the weights (`FOCR_FIXTURES_DIR`), following the `tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md` convention. Small manifests are committed. Update `tests/fixtures/MANIFEST.toml` (required by `scripts/check_fixture_manifest.py`) and `tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md`.

### Step 4 — nondeterminism floor
- Run every fixture twice, at two thread counts.
- Record bitwise token equality and the max abs/rel hidden-state deltas per layer, for f32 and for bf16.
- These numbers set the L1–L3 tolerances (AGENTS testing policy). Extend `scripts/oracle_nondeterminism_floor.py`.

### Step 5 — provenance
Extend `scripts/check_oracle_provenance.py` with the v2 pins (stack versions, model commit, file hashes). Today it hard-codes the v1 stack as `PIN_TORCH`/`PIN_TRANSFORMERS`/`HF_COMMIT` (`:28-30`), so add v2 pin constants beside them rather than overloading those. It must skip with success when the v2 corpus is absent.

## Acceptance criteria
- OQ-V2-4 answered and recorded.
- S1–S4 generated in f32 CPU, with the floor recorded. S5 generated, or explicitly deferred with a reason in the bead notes. S1-corpus is produced by U2-C4 with this script; it does not block closing this bead for M0.
- Provenance checks are green.
- The DISC-U2-2 hazard is checked: no fixture hit the n-gram-vs-guard "all −inf → id 0" case. Log a counter.
- Fixture generation is reproducible from a clean venv, with commands recorded.
- Each fixture input's SHA-256 is recorded in the fixture manifest.

## Logging
Each fixture run writes an NDJSON line: fixture id, mode, device, dtype, thread count, wall time, token count, pages, output hash.

Spec: plan §7.1, §5.6–5.9, §14 OQ-V2-3/4.
acceptance_criteria:
- OQ-V2-4 answered and recorded.
- S1–S4 generated in f32 CPU, with the floor recorded. S5 generated, or explicitly deferred with a reason in the bead notes. S1-corpus is produced by U2-C4 with this script; it does not block closing this bead for M0.
- Provenance checks are green.
- The DISC-U2-2 hazard is checked: no fixture hit the n-gram-vs-guard "all −inf → id 0" case. Log a counter.
- Fixture generation is reproducible from a clean venv, with commands recorded.
- Each fixture input's SHA-256 is recorded in the fixture manifest.
close_reason: v2 f32 CPU oracle (HF 5632329a, nothing ported): 9 fixtures S1-S4 generated, committed (tests/fixtures/uocr2_oracle: ids/md/ORACLE.json/FLOOR.json) with off-tree dumps; DISC-U2-2=0, replicas bit-exact; floor measured (f32 thread variation: ids identical, 11 near-tie routing flips; repeat and bf16 bit-identical; bf16 ledger diverges at 7-94); provenance checker green incl. dumps; clean-venv reproduction bit-identical; S5 deferred to C5a's sourced document (~5-12 h/run). Details in the closing comment.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Dump-list gap found while closing U2-B1 (2026-10-29). The Step 2 dump list feeds U2-C1's L1 rung ("page2d coordinates and cos/sin ... coordinates exact") and U2-B1's frequency test ("inv_tok equals the oracle's dumped table bit for bit"), but it names none of those values. Router `iq`/`ik` post-RoPE check them only indirectly, and a coordinate bug that shows up only as a cosine drift cannot be traced back to its row.

Add to the Step 2 dumps, for every S1-S3 run:
- `inv_tok`: the 63 f32 values from SB:2032 (`1.0 / (base_tok ** (_ar / n_tok))`), plus `inv_page`.
- Per prefill row: `bucket` (page id, SB:2511-2568), `tok_pos`, `page_pos` before the mod-2 fold, `img_page`, and the query page (`_PAGE_SCOPE_PREFILL=True`). This covers every row, not just the selected ones: the arrays are small (int32, one per prompt token).
- Per decode step dumped (first 64, and +/-8 around every `<PAGE>`): the state machine's `(page, tok)` after the fed token (SB:1451-1489) and the gate's `qp`.
- cos/sin for the selected query rows, as computed (fp32, before any dtype cast).

Native counterparts already exist in `src/native_engine/srswa.rs`: `inv_tok_freqs()`, `PageCoords::build` (bucket, tok_pos, img_page, query_page, pf_cnt), `DecodePageState::feed`, and `page2d_rope_table`. U2-C1 compares them.

comments.text: Progress 2026-10-29: OQ-V2-4 answered (HF v2 runs in f32 on CPU, nothing ported). Generator, floor mode and provenance checks are written. S1, S2, S4 and S3-p9_p14 are generated and committed. S3-p10/p20 are still decoding (tens of thousands of tokens each under the guard). bf16 is limited to the 7 short fixtures, because it runs about 8x slower than f32 on CPU.
