comments.text:
U2-A6 done. The v2 parity oracle is Baidu's HF reference itself, running in f32 on CPU with nothing ported.

**Step 1 — feasibility (OQ-V2-4, resolved).** HF v2 at `5632329a` loads and runs in f32 on CPU under v1's `--cpu-patch` / `--f32` shims, in a separate uv venv: Python 3.10.19, torch 2.13.0, torchvision 0.28.0, transformers 4.52.1, tokenizers 0.21.4, huggingface-hub 0.36.0. The venv is recorded in `PINNED_SOURCES.md`.
- The Triton paths require `q.is_cuda`, so prefill takes `_infer_prefill_attend` → `_forward_dense` and decode takes `_decode_attend`, both unmodified.
- `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` holds.
- `DASH_STAGE0` and the other semantic switches must be unset; the script refuses otherwise. `SPARSE_DIAG_LOG`, `TIME_DIAG` and `CODE_STAMP_LOG` are 0.
- The hooked oracle emits the same ids as a hook-free run (page_0009, the three-page document).

**Step 2 — `scripts/gen_reference_fixtures_uocr2.py`.**
- It verifies all 18 required model files against `SOURCE_HASHES.md` and asserts the pinned stack.
- It drives `model.infer()` with explicit `no_repeat_ngram_size=35`, `ngram_window` 128/1024, `max_page_tokens=20000`, `page_count_guard=True` and `crop_mode`, plus `eval_mode=True` (no streamer).
- Dumps are taken through module hooks and wrappers of module-level functions; Baidu's code is not edited:
  - L0: prompt ids, `images_ori` / `images_crop`, seq mask, tile grid.
  - L1: page2d coordinates, main and router cos/sin.
  - Per layer: the input, `iq` (post-RoPE), `ik`, `kbar`, scores, candidate mask, fallback flag, the entmax top-M input and prior, topi/bias/valid, and the attention output before and after `o_proj`.
  - The final hidden state, raw logits and ids.
  - Per-step dumps for steps 0–63 and ±8 around every generated `<PAGE>`.
  - Per-step n-gram/guard effect and the DISC-U2-2 counter.
- `kbar` and the route intermediates are recomputed with the reference's own lines. The run fails unless they reproduce its scores and topi/bias/valid bit for bit (0 mismatches on every fixture).
- It writes the v1 `FixtureLoader` layout, one NDJSON line per fixture run, and with `--commit-dir` the committed twin.

**Step 3 — fixtures (f32, CPU, 12 threads).** Each fixture's input SHA-256 is in `ORACLE.json`.
| fixture | tokens | pages out | finish | wall (t12) | token-id sha |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1-page_0590 | 2,329 | 1/1 | stop | 151 s | 4cdfda992984 |
| S1-page_0009 | 50 | 1/1 | stop | 4 s | b1c9ab8154b6 |
| S1-page_0014 | 256 | 1/1 | stop | 16 s | 0c90af2fed8d |
| S2-p9_p14_p19 | 2,152 | 3/3 | stop | 156 s | a623655879bf |
| S3-p9_p14 | 538 | 2/2 | stop | 46 s | 9c3948822e0c |
| S3-p10 | 6,272 | 10/10 | stop | 852 s | 9c541438f445 |
| S3-p20 | 16,880 | 20/20 | stop | 3,941 s | 7bf5aab98521 |
| S4-page_0590-gundam | 2,971 | 1/1 | stop | 247 s | 07d02d0408a4 |
| S4-page_0009-gundam | 78 | 1/1 | stop | 10 s | 56a1baf1ed29 |

- **Counters.**
  - DISC-U2-2 (every logit −inf after the guard) fires on 0 steps in every fixture.
  - The guard only ever banned EOS (up to 13,989 steps on S3-p20). It never forced a cap and never left EOS as the only option.
  - The n-gram ban changed the raw argmax on 0–37 steps per fixture.
- **Routing facts measured.**
  - Pages 2..N have 99–129 fallback queries each (odd values only), identical across all 12 layers. That is the marker plus 128 − (s mod 32) image rows, exactly as plan §5.6.4 derives (s, the page's first image row, is always even).
  - The first 128 rows have no remote block.
- **S5 deferred.** Its 40–60-page input must come from U2-C5a's sourced MarathonDocBench set: C5a owns the source, license and manifest records, and this bead should not pick an unvetted document. The generator has fixed sets, so S5 needs a page-list input option (for example `--doc NAME=DIR`).
  - **Cost.** Wall time grew 4.6× from 10 to 20 pages (852 s → 3,941 s at 12 threads, load avg ~30; RSS ~19–21 GB). Extrapolated, that is ~5 h for 40 pages and ~12 h for 60 per f32 run, plus a second run for the floor.
- **S1-corpus** stays with U2-C4, as the bead says.

**Step 4 — floor (`FLOOR.json`, `oracle_nondeterminism_floor.py --uocr2-group`).**
- **`f32`** (12 vs 4 threads, all 9 fixtures):
  - token ids identical on all 9 (S3-p20's 16,880 included);
  - max logit spread over the identical prefix 4.8e-4;
  - layer inputs max_rel 2.3e-4; attention outputs 6.1e-3; final hidden 2.6e-3;
  - 11 routing rows differ (topi/valid), all on S3-p10/p20 and from layer 0 on (where hidden_in differs by only 5e-6). These are near-ties, so routing parity needs a margin-aware rule, not exact set equality.
- **`f32_rerun`** (12 threads twice, 7 fixtures): bit-identical everywhere.
- **`bf16`** (12 vs 4 threads, 7 fixtures): bit-identical everywhere.
- **`ledger`** (f32 vs bf16 at 12 threads, 7 fixtures):
  - tokens diverge at positions 7–94;
  - logit spread up to 2.9 before divergence;
  - final-hidden max_rel 0.50;
  - 12,169 routing rows differ.
  - So bf16 HF is not an oracle for routing; OQ-V2-3's tolerances stay with U2-C1.

**Step 5 — provenance.** `check_oracle_provenance.py` holds the v2 pin constants beside v1's and checks they equal the generator's. It validates `ORACLE.json`:
- pins and actual stack, HF commit, every model file against `SOURCE_HASHES.md`;
- the f32/CPU/deterministic run, explicit params, DISC-U2-2 = 0, replica mismatches = 0;
- each `.ids.txt` and `.md` against its hashes, and the input pages against the corpus when present;
- `FLOOR.json`;
- with `--uocr2-dumps`, every off-tree activation file hash.

It skips with success when the twin is absent. Its self-test covers 17 rejection cases.

**Reproducible from a clean venv.** A second venv built from scratch with only the recorded pins (`uv pip freeze` identical) regenerated `S1-page_0009` and `S1-page_0014`: ids and all 392 activation arrays were bit-identical. The commands are in `tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md`.

**Gates.**
- `check_oracle_provenance.py` passes plain (9 fixtures, inputs verified against the corpus), with `--uocr2-dumps` (every activation file hash verified) and with `--self-test`.
- `check_fixture_manifest.py` passes.
- The generator's `--self-test` passes.
- `cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast` on the same tree: 1,585 passed, 0 failed.

**Hand-offs** are posted as comments on U2-C1/C2 (stages, dtypes, padding, floor), U2-B6 (prompt and decode contract, ids goldens) and U2-B7 (L0 tensors and the normalization-order note).

title: U2-A7 — Fail-closed v2 dispatch: every decode path, lever, daemon and recipe supports v2, is ignored with a warning, or refuses it before weights load
description:
# U2-A7 — Fail-closed v2 dispatch: every decode path, lever, daemon and recipe supports v2, is ignored with a warning, or refuses it before weights load

## Goal
No code path may ever run v2 weights through v1 R-SWA math. Running a v1 artifact through v2 code is equally forbidden. Every path either **supports v2 explicitly**, **ignores a lever that cannot reach the v2 path** (with a warning), or **refuses it with exit 2 before weights load**, with a message that names the lever and gives the remediation.

The refusal is a **new pre-load check** returning `FocrError::Usage` (exit 2). Do not reuse `ensure_arch_implemented` (`mod.rs:2376`): it returns `NotImplemented`, which maps to exit 1 (`error.rs:141`), and it runs inside `forward_pre` (`:2394/:2400`), after load and preprocessing. The other zoo archs keep their existing exit codes.

This must land before U2-B6 flips `implemented() = true`.

## Why (D18)
This is the worst failure a user could hit: v2 weights run through R-SWA code produce confident garbage and exit 0.

Concrete hazards found in code review:
- **Unknown ids fall through.** `forward` and `forward_dynamic` (`mod.rs:2105`, `:2137`) dispatch on id strings and fall through to the v1 `forward_pre` (`:2394`) for unknown ids. Only `ensure_arch_implemented` (`:2376`) guards them.
- **Speculative decoding.** `spec_decode_i8` (`mod.rs:4064`) is called only from `generate_cached_i8` (`:3887`, call at `:3949-3952`), which first runs `require_full_int8_authorization()` (`:3895`) and is reached only when `int8_decode_requested() || artifact_stores_gated_int8()` (`:3736`). The certified v2 path cannot reach it, but a v2 run with the full-int8 switch could. Refuse it as defense in depth.
- **Many decoder paths assume R-SWA.** About 10 decoder paths and many env levers do:
  - chunked prefill;
  - the batch spine;
  - batched int8 decode;
  - verify;
  - `FOCR_INT8_KV`;
  - `FOCR_FUSE_NGRAM_LMHEAD` (read only in `generate_cached_i8`, `mod.rs:3939`);
  - and others.

## Scope
1. **Exhaustive dispatch.**
   - `forward` and `forward_dynamic` match exhaustively on the decoder family plus `unlimited_variant()`.
   - **No `_ =>` arm** may reach the v1 forward.
   - An unknown arch is an explicit error.
2. **Path / lever matrix.** Implement exactly this:

   | Path / lever | v2 first wave |
   |---|---|
   | `generate_cached` (conservative cache: int8 FFN, f32 attention/router/lm_head) → `prefill_with_cache` / `decode_step_with_cache`. **This is the certified conservative-artifact path**: int8 FFN/expert matrices inside `DecoderWeightCache` even when it is built from raw BF16 (`decoder.rs:802-808, 1838`), everything else f32 (`mod.rs:3736-3800`). | support (implemented in B5) |
   | stateless `forward` (`decoder.rs:699`, `generate_stateless` `mod.rs:4246`, `FOCR_DECODE_STATELESS`): the only all-f32 native path, used by the f32 oracle rungs | support (B5) |
   | int8 cached `generate_cached_i8` → `prefill_with_cache_i8` / `decode_step_with_cache_i8` (`decoder.rs:2826,2956`). Reached only via `int8_decode_requested()` or `artifact_stores_gated_int8()`, i.e. the experimental full-int8 switch and the WASM int4 artifact (`mod.rs:3736`). | **refuse** |
   | experimental full-int8 triggers: `FOCR_DECODE_INT8`, `ocr-batch --experimental-full-int8` (`cli.rs:2183`), `force_int8_decode()` (`mod.rs:454`) | **refuse** |
   | `OcrModel::recognize_multi_page`, `recognize_multi_page_dynamic`, `recognize_multi_page_dynamic_streaming` (`mod.rs:2620/2654/2691`; today gated by `arch().id() != default_arch().id()` at `:2626/:2663/:2701` and by `ensure_arch_implemented` at `:2634/:2671/:2709`, both exit 1) | **refuse** until U2-B6 routes them to the v2 document loop. They must **never** let v2 into v1's 640-squash R-SWA multi-page loop. When U2-A2 rewrites these identity checks as capability calls, a naive "is Unlimited family" capability would open exactly that hole, so the matrix test pins it. |
   | chunked prefill (`decoder.rs:1198` `chunk_prefill_attention`, `decoder.rs:1287` `prefill_with_cache_chunked` when `prefill_chunk_size()` is `Some`, `decoder.rs:2842` `prefill_with_cache_i8_chunked`; `FOCR_PREFILL_CHUNK`) | **refuse** (later in F2) |
   | batched/spine: `batched_decode_step_i8*` (`decoder.rs:3211,3243`), `recognize_batch_spine` (`mod.rs:2984`), `batch_scheduler.rs:43,440,487`, `FOCR_BATCH_SPINE` | **refuse** (later in F5) |
   | spec decode/verify: `spec_decode_i8` (`mod.rs:4064`), `verify_forward*` (`decoder.rs:3495,3575`), `FOCR_SPEC_DECODE` (read only in `generate_cached_i8`, `mod.rs:3949`), `FOCR_SPEC_VERIFY` (no production reader: `verify_forward` has no production caller) | **ignored**, with an `ignored_lever` warning (unreachable from the v2 paths) |
   | `FOCR_INT8_ATTN`, `FOCR_INT8_LMHEAD` (`quant/recipe.rs:43/47`; read only by `Recipe::from_env()` in `require_experimental_full_int8_recipe`, `mod.rs:480`, i.e. only on the refused full-int8 path; convert, census and loader use `validated_default`) | **ignored**, with an `ignored_lever` warning |
   | levers that reach only v1 R-SWA or `_i8` code: `FOCR_INT8_KV`, `FOCR_ATTN_GEMM`, `FOCR_RSWA_PARALLEL_ATTN` (`rswa.rs:95/89/101`), `FOCR_QKV_FUSED` (default ON, read only in `DecoderWeightCacheI8::build`, `decoder.rs:2222-2231, 2370`), `FOCR_FUSE_NGRAM_LMHEAD` (`mod.rs:3939`, inside `generate_cached_i8`) | **ignored**, with `warnings[{kind:"ignored_lever", env}]`. Refusing them would break v1 users' exported tuning environments while guarding nothing. |
   | `RunawayGuard`, `FOCR_RUNAWAY_GUARD` (`sampler.rs:53`) | **reaches both v2 paths today**: it is built for every path at `mod.rs:3727` and checked in `generate_cached` (`:3830`) and `generate_stateless` (`:4284`). U2-B5/B6 must not build or check it on the v2 arm, because the page guard and per-page cap replace it; only then is it **ignored**, with an `ignored_lever` warning. The matrix test sets `FOCR_RUNAWAY_GUARD=1` and an invalid value and asserts v2 output is unchanged. |
   | resident daemon (`cli.rs:1650`, `resident.rs`) | **refuse** for v2 until its protocol carries v2 flags (bd-fuh2) |
   | converter recipes: the v1 WASM int4 recipe (`src/quant/convert.rs:60`; loader `artifact_stores_gated_int8` `mod.rs:3128`) | **refuse** for v2 |

   **Classify by effective state.** A value-parsed lever set to its kill-switch value (for example `FOCR_QKV_FUSED=0`) is a no-op for v2 and is ignored, never refused. Presence-based levers (`FOCR_LMHEAD_SHARD`, `FOCR_PREFILL_CHUNK`, `FOCR_FUSE_NORM_QUANT`, `FOCR_SPEC_DECODE`, `FOCR_SPEC_VERIFY`, `FOCR_FUSE_NGRAM_LMHEAD`, `FOCR_PROFILE_DECODE`) are armed by any value, including `0` (e.g. `lmhead_shard_enabled` is `var_os(..).is_some()`, `decoder.rs:2115`), so classify them by presence. The R-SWA levers (`FOCR_INT8_KV`, `FOCR_ATTN_GEMM`, `FOCR_RSWA_PARALLEL_ATTN`) are read only in `rswa::decode_attention` and `RingCache::new`; they stay ignorable only because U2-B5's SR-SWA arm never calls those. U2-X2 lands first (this bead depends on it), so its `FOCR_TEST_MAX_POSITIONS` allow-list row goes in here. Only a lever that would change v2 numerics on a reachable v2 path is refused.

   Refusal happens **before weights load**, with exit 2 (`FocrError::Usage`), and the message names the lever, for example "FOCR_PREFILL_CHUNK is not supported for unlimited-ocr-2; unset it".
   **Every other `FOCR_*` variable** read in `src/` gets an explicit row in a `UOCR2_LEVER_POLICY` table: `refuse`, `supported-exact`, `ignored` (with an `ignored_lever` warning) or `n/a`. The matrix above missed these (verified by grep on 2026-10-28):
   - `FOCR_RESAMPLE` (`preprocess/mod.rs:474, 493-505`) → **ignored**. It is a process-global v1 knob (unknown values silently fall back today); v2 hard-wires PIL bicubic per arch (U2-B7).
   - `FOCR_LMHEAD_SHARD` and `FOCR_LMHEAD_SHARD_TILES` (`decoder.rs:2098,2105`) reach `lm_head_cached` (`decoder.rs:1088-1090`) on the conservative v2 path → **refuse until U2-C2**. `FOCR_FUSE_NORM_QUANT` (`decoder.rs:1709`) is read only in `decode_step_with_cache_i8` (`decoder.rs:2990`) → **ignored**. `FOCR_MOE_SCORE_ORDER` and `FOCR_FUSE_SWIGLU` (`moe.rs`), `FOCR_SOFTMAX_COPY` (`nn.rs`), `FOCR_INT8_AUTOVEC` (`simd/arm.rs`) → first read each one's use: if it reaches only `_i8` or R-SWA code, **ignored**; otherwise **refuse until U2-C2** re-runs L4 with it on, after which C2 flips each pass to supported-exact.
   - `FOCR_BATCH_PACK`, `FOCR_BATCH_VISION` and `FOCR_BATCH_SIZE` (`batch_scheduler.rs`, `native_engine/mod.rs:620`, `decoder.rs:3073`) → refuse (batch spine; later in F5).
   - `FOCR_STREAM_VISION` and `FOCR_UNLIMITED_VISION_CACHE` (`native_engine/mod.rs`) → classify by reading their use: supported-exact if vision-only and byte-identical, else refuse.
   - `FOCR_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` (`mod.rs:374/788`) and `FOCR_NO_REPEAT_NGRAM` (`cli.rs:303`, clap `env`) → supported, **redefined for v2**: per page (U2-B6's per-page cap and generated-only 35-gram), never a global generated cap.
   - `FOCR_THREADS`, `FOCR_FORCE_ARCH` (SIMD silicon dispatch, not the model arch), `FOCR_PROFILE_DECODE` (`decoder.rs:985`), `FOCR_QUANT` (`mod.rs:336`) → supported-exact; `FOCR_INT4_GROUPS` (`convert.rs:355`) → refuse for v2 (int4 is out of scope); `FOCR_CALIB_OUT`, `FOCR_SAM_ATTN_PROBE_RUNS` → allow-list (calibration/probe tooling); `FOCR_NO_RESIDENT`, `FOCR_RESIDENT_*` → n/a while the daemon refuses v2. Note that `resident.rs:272` forwards all of `std::env::vars()`.
   - The dynamic `FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_{stage}_MS` (`lib.rs:811`, built with `format!`) → supported (U2-B6 scales the forward budget per page/window). A literal scan cannot see it, so the census enumerates it explicitly.
   - Variables added later by U2 beads each bring their own row in the same change: `FOCR_SRSWA_DENSE` (B3), `FOCR_SRSWA_DUMP` (C1), `FOCR_SRSWA_RETIRE` and `FOCR_SRSWA_ENTMAX` (B6), `FOCR_MEMORY_BUDGET` (D3), `FOCR_SRSWA_KV_DTYPE` (F4), `FOCR_TEST_MAX_POSITIONS` (X2; allow-listed as test-only).

3. **Central helper.** One function, e.g. `ensure_lever_supported(arch, lever)`, called at each entry point. Do not scatter ad-hoc checks.
4. **Implemented-false behavior.** While `implemented()==false` (before B6), *every* v2 inference path refuses, through the same pre-load check (exit 2), with "unlimited-ocr-2 is registered but not yet implemented in this build".
5. **Parity tests.** Each existing parity test gains an explicit v2 skip, or a v2 lane where supported: `batched_attention_parity`, `batched_forward_parity`, `chunked_prefill_parity`, `parity_ladder` (`:130`), `spec_decode_gate`, `spec_ring_rollback`, `spec_verify_forward_parity`, `lmhead_shard_parity`, `batched_decode_bit_identity`, `batched_moe_parity`, `batched_sampler_parity`, `batched_igemm_parity`, `int4_packed_parity`.

## Tests
- **Matrix test.** Use a synthetic v2-identified tiny artifact; no real weights are needed, since refusal happens before load. For every lever above, set the env var or flag and assert one of:
  - "refused, exit 2, message names the lever";
  - "ignored": the run reaches the implemented=false refusal without naming the lever, and stderr carries one ignored-lever line naming the env var. The `warnings[{kind:"ignored_lever"}]` assertion is re-run by U2-B6 once v2 runs, and by U2-T1a (j). This bead registers the `ignored_lever` kind in U2-X2's `event_fields`;
  - "supported" (for the supported paths, once B5 lands; until then, the implemented=false refusal).
  - Never "ran" a v1 R-SWA or `_i8` path with v2 weights.
- **Unknown arch** reaches an explicit error, never the v1 forward.
- **Multi-page entry points:** each of the three `recognize_multi_page*` methods refuses a v2 model with an explicit error. It never runs the v1 multi-page loop. U2-B6 later flips them to "supported, v2 document loop".
- **Daemon** refuses a v2 model.
- **v1 regression:** the same matrix with a v1 artifact behaves exactly as today. The U2-T3 gate is green.
- **Lever census:** a test scans `src/` for `"FOCR_[A-Z0-9_]+"` string literals, plus the explicitly enumerated dynamic `FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_{stage}_MS` names, and fails on any variable missing from `UOCR2_LEVER_POLICY`. Test-only and oracle-only variables are allow-listed. This keeps a future lever from silently reaching v2.

## Logging
One NDJSON line per (arch, lever) case per `docs/TEST_LOGGING.md`: the expected decision, the observed exit code, the message, and `weights_touched: false`.

## Acceptance criteria
- The matrix test is green and the U2-T3 gate is green.
- Close notes list each lever and its decision.
- bd-3ryl (the general task-vs-arch guard) is linked as related; this bead implements the v2 cases.

Spec: plan D18, §6.2 path matrix.
acceptance_criteria:
- The matrix test is green and the U2-T3 gate is green.
- Close notes list each lever and its decision.
- bd-3ryl (the general task-vs-arch guard) is linked as related; this bead implements the v2 cases.
close_reason: v2 fails closed at a pre-load admission (exit 2, every lever named, before sidecar and weights). UOCR2_LEVER_POLICY has 87 rows: 8 refuse, 18 ignored, 17 supported, 15 n/a, 29 allow-listed; the census test is enforced. Dispatch is exhaustive (forward_route, multi_page_route), the daemon never serves v2, ocr-batch admits v2 up front, int4 convert is refused by arch, and parity_ladder skips non-v1 subjects. The 52-case matrix and the 9-case CLI matrix are green, mutations 10/10 caught, full ltest is 1570/0, and the T3 gate is green. Per-lever decisions and deviations are in the close comment.

comments.text:
U2-A7 done. Unlimited-OCR-2 fails closed at a pre-load admission (`src/native_engine/lever_policy.rs`). It runs right after the header identifies the arch, before the tokenizer sidecar check and before any weight byte is read.

**Outcomes.** A lever that is armed and refused gives exit 2 (`FocrError::Usage`), and every lever at fault is named. The message ends "unset it" or "unset them" for variables, and "remove it" or "remove them" when `--experimental-full-int8` is among them. Ignored levers, and a refused lever set to a value that leaves it off, each produce one `ignored_lever` warning on stderr (`[focr] warning: FOCR_X has no effect on unlimited-ocr-2: … — unset it for this model's runs`). Otherwise, while `implemented()` is false, the run exits 2 with "unlimited-ocr-2 is registered but not yet implemented in this build (U2-B6); use unlimited-ocr meanwhile". At HEAD before this bead, v2 loaded all 6.7 GB and then failed in `forward_pre` with exit 1.

**Lever decisions.** `UOCR2_LEVER_POLICY` has 87 rows, one per `FOCR_*` variable in `src/` plus the dynamic `FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_FORWARD_MS`. The census test fails on a missing or stale row.
- **Refuse (8):**
  - `FOCR_BATCH_SPINE`: armed unless falsy (U2-F5).
  - `FOCR_DECODE_INT8`: armed when truthy. The same refusal covers `--experimental-full-int8` (the force flag).
  - `FOCR_PREFILL_CHUNK`: armed by presence (U2-F2).
  - `FOCR_LMHEAD_SHARD`: armed by presence (until U2-C2).
  - `FOCR_FUSE_SWIGLU`: armed by presence (until U2-C2).
  - `FOCR_MOE_SCORE_ORDER`: armed when truthy (until U2-C2).
  - `FOCR_SOFTMAX_COPY`: armed when truthy (until U2-C2).
  - `FOCR_INT8_AUTOVEC`: armed when falsy, i.e. turning autovec off (until U2-C2).
- **Ignored, with an `ignored_lever` warning (18):**
  - R-SWA only: `FOCR_ATTN_GEMM`, `FOCR_INT8_KV`, `FOCR_RSWA_PARALLEL_ATTN`.
  - All-int8 decoder only: `FOCR_FUSE_NGRAM_LMHEAD`, `FOCR_FUSE_NORM_QUANT`, `FOCR_INT8_ATTN`, `FOCR_INT8_LMHEAD`, `FOCR_QKV_FUSED`.
  - Only under the refused spine: `FOCR_BATCH_PACK`, `FOCR_BATCH_SIZE`, `FOCR_BATCH_VISION`.
  - Only under the refused `FOCR_LMHEAD_SHARD`: `FOCR_LMHEAD_SHARD_TILES`.
  - Unreachable from v2 paths: `FOCR_SPEC_DECODE`, `FOCR_SPEC_VERIFY`.
  - `FOCR_RESAMPLE`: v2 fixes its own resampling (U2-B7).
  - `FOCR_RUNAWAY_GUARD`: the per-page cap and page guard replace it (U2-B6).
  - `FOCR_STREAM_VISION`: it streams only the GOT-OCR2, OneChart and SmolVLM2 towers.
  - `FOCR_INT4_GROUPS`: a convert-time knob for a recipe v2 does not have.
- **Supported (17):**
  - `FOCR_DECODE_STATELESS`, `FOCR_FORCE_ARCH`, `FOCR_MANIFEST_URL`, `FOCR_MMAP`, `FOCR_MODEL_DIR`, `FOCR_MODEL_PATH`, `FOCR_NO_PROGRESS`, `FOCR_PROFILE_DECODE`, `FOCR_QUANT`, `FOCR_RUN_STORE`, `FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_FORWARD_MS`, `FOCR_THREADS`, `FOCR_TIMING`.
  - `FOCR_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` and `FOCR_NO_REPEAT_NGRAM`, both per page (U2-B6).
  - `FOCR_SRSWA_RETIRE`: it frees only blocks that no query can select.
  - `FOCR_UNLIMITED_VISION_CACHE`: both arms use byte-identical BF16 vision tensors.
- **n/a (15):**
  - GOT-OCR2's: `FOCR_GOT_FORMAT`, `FOCR_GOT_INT8_LMHEAD`, `FOCR_GOT_NO_REPEAT_NGRAM`, `FOCR_GOT_SEQ_ATTN`.
  - SmolVLM2's: `FOCR_SIGLIP_SEQ`, `FOCR_SMOLVLM2_QUESTION`.
  - TrOMR's: `FOCR_TROMR_SAMPLE`, `FOCR_TROMR_SEED`, `FOCR_TROMR_SPLIT`.
  - The resident transport, which never serves v2: `FOCR_NO_RESIDENT` and `FOCR_RESIDENT_*` (5 rows).
- **Allow-listed test, oracle and tooling variables (29):** among them `FOCR_TEST_MAX_POSITIONS` (X2), `FOCR_UOCR2_SOURCE_DIR`, `FOCR_UOCR2_TOKENIZER_JSON`, `FOCR_CALIB_OUT`, `FOCR_SAM_ATTN_PROBE_RUNS`, and `FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET` / `FOCR_TROMR`, two literals that are not variables.

**Deviations from the bead text, each recorded with its reason in the table:**
- `FOCR_BATCH_PACK`, `FOCR_BATCH_SIZE` and `FOCR_BATCH_VISION` are ignored, not refused. They act only under `FOCR_BATCH_SPINE`, which is refused.
- `FOCR_INT4_GROUPS` is ignored at inference. v2 int4 convert is refused by arch instead (below).
- `FOCR_STREAM_VISION` is ignored, because it reaches only zoo vision towers.
- `FOCR_FUSE_NORM_QUANT` is ignored, because it is read only in `decode_step_with_cache_i8`.
- `FOCR_INT8_AUTOVEC` is refused only when set to off, since autovec on is the default.

**Dispatch.**
- `forward` and `forward_dynamic` route through `forward_route`, which matches exhaustively on (`Decoder`, `UnlimitedVariant`); there is no wildcard. The v2 arm gives NotImplemented (U2-B5), and an unknown or unwired arch gets an explicit error.
- The three `recognize_multi_page*` methods route through `multi_page_route`; v2 gives NotImplemented (U2-B6) and never reaches v1's loop.
- The resident client skips v2 (`resident_daemon_serves`), and the daemon refuses it with kind "model".
- `ocr-batch` admits a policed model once (`load_if_policed`), so the refusal is the run's exit 2, not a per-image FAILED line.
- `focr convert --quant int4` refuses v2, and every model without an int4 recipe, through `quant::convert::ensure_int4_recipe` as soon as `--model-id` resolves.

**Parity tests.**
- `parity_ladder` skips its model-gated rungs, and logs why, when `FOCR_MODEL_PATH` identifies as another model (`native_engine::model_id_at`, a header probe). This was verified against the real v2 checkpoint (`L5_multi_page`, p10 and p9_p14).
- `batched_forward_parity`'s armed branch is a no-op; a note there requires its future wiring to skip non-v1 models (U2-F5).
- The other 11 are artifact-free kernel tests that run synthetic R-SWA or `_i8` tensors, so no v2 model can reach them:
  - `batched_attention_parity`, `chunked_prefill_parity`;
  - `spec_decode_gate`, `spec_ring_rollback`, `spec_verify_forward_parity`;
  - `lmhead_shard_parity`;
  - `batched_decode_bit_identity`, `batched_moe_parity`, `batched_sampler_parity`, `batched_igemm_parity`;
  - `int4_packed_parity`.

**Tests**, all green, with NDJSON logs validated by `scripts/check_test_logs.py` (65 unit lines, 9 CLI lines):
- `lever_policy` (7): the census, the bead MATRIX of 52 cases, every row armed alone, v1 and the zoo untouched by every lever, the force flag with several levers, an implemented v2 still refusing armed levers, and Armed matching each reader's parse.
- `v2_is_refused_after_identification_before_its_sidecar_and_weights`: a sparse two-shard census-exact stand-in, with a foreign sidecar present. The after-validation hook panics if reached. Armed, it also identifies the real v1 `.focrq` and the real v2 checkpoint by header.
- `every_arch_routes_explicitly_and_only_v1_reaches_v1`.
- `a_v2_model_refuses_every_entry_point_before_reading_its_input`: forward, forward_dynamic, recognize, recognize_batch and the three multi-page methods.
- `daemon_refuses_unlimited_ocr_2_transport_shaped`.
- `int4_refuses_unlimited_ocr_2`.
- e2e `cli_refuses_unlimited_ocr_2_before_weights_naming_each_lever` (9 cases):
  - bare;
  - prefill_chunk, decode_int8, lmhead_shard_zero;
  - batch_spine_off, ignored_levers;
  - `--robot` run_error code 2;
  - ocr-batch with `--experimental-full-int8`;
  - convert int4.

  No daemon is spawned (the resident dir stays empty).

**Mutation checks:** 10 of 10 caught, run in an isolated source copy so the live tree was never mutated:
- `policy_for` dropping v2;
- refusing regardless of the armed value;
- NotFalsy arming the empty string;
- the sharded load skipping admission;
- v2 merged into the v1 forward arm;
- v2 merged into the v1 multi-page arm;
- the daemon serving v2;
- a census row removed;
- the ocr-batch preflight removed;
- the client contacting the daemon for v2.

**Gates:**
- fmt clean.
- clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` and `--no-default-features --lib -D warnings` clean.
- Full `ltest --locked --no-fail-fast`: 33 targets, 1570 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored. `cli_robot_golden` took 600.56 s because of bd-mapo.
- U2-T3 token-id golden gate (release-perf, the real v1 int8 `.focrq`, `FOCR_THREADS=12`): 33 passed. That covers page_0009, page_0014, p9_p14 and p9_p14_stream, token-exact.
- `br dep cycles`: the 2 pre-existing cycles only.
- ubs on the 10 changed files: the only critical is the pre-existing `Command::new(current_exe)` daemon spawn. The new warnings are inventory items in test code.

**Hand-offs**, as comments on U2-B5, U2-B6 and U2-C2:
- the B5 forward arm;

title: U2-X1 — Fix multi-page streaming: page events stop permanently after a split multi-byte UTF-8 char (v1 bug); UTF-8-safe incremental decoder
description:
# U2-X1 — Fix multi-page streaming: page events stop permanently after a split multi-byte UTF-8 char (v1 bug); UTF-8-safe incremental decoder

## Problem (affects v1 users today)
During streaming multi-page decoding, the observer closure in `recognize_multi_page_pres` (`src/native_engine/mod.rs:2723`, observer at `:2786-2824`; reached from `recognize_multi_page_dynamic_streaming` at `:2691`) re-decodes the generated ids every `STREAM_CHECK_EVERY` tokens with `tok.decode(&ids)` (the observer's accumulator, `mod.rs:2808`) and feeds the text to **`postprocess::PageStream`** (`postprocess.rs:531`). This is not `batch_scheduler::PageStream` (`batch_scheduler.rs:123`), the batch spine's type, which this bead does not touch.

`tok.decode` fails on invalid UTF-8 (`FormatMismatch("decode: invalid UTF-8")`, `src/tokenizer/mod.rs:~704`). When a multi-byte character is split across BPE tokens, that error sets `stream_broken = true` **permanently** (`mod.rs:2802-2811`). After that, no `page` robot events are emitted for the rest of the run, and the end-of-decode flush is skipped too (`:2821`), so even the final page's event is lost.

- **Chinese and Japanese documents are hit routinely.** Byte-level BPE often splits CJK characters.
- **The final assembled text is still correct.** Only streaming is lost.
- **v2 makes it matter more.** MarathonDocBench is half Chinese, and v2's whole long-document UX is streaming.

## Goal
Write a **UTF-8-safe incremental detokenizer**, with tests. It holds back an incomplete trailing byte sequence until the next token completes it, and never errors on a split character. Use it in:
- **(a)** v1's PageStream, which fixes the bug for v1 users now;
- **(b)** v2's token-id page segmentation (U2-B6, D20), which splits pages on token id 128827 and decodes each page's ids with this decoder.

## Scope
1. **The decoder.** An incremental byte-level-BPE detokenizer that tracks pending bytes.
   - It emits only complete UTF-8 scalar values.
   - **Flush rule.** At end of stream, and at a v2 page boundary (`<PAGE>` id 128827, D20), any incomplete or invalid byte sequence is replaced with **U+FFFD**. This matches HF's ByteLevel decode (`errors="replace"`), which decodes each segment between added tokens separately. So a partial character immediately before `<PAGE>` becomes U+FFFD at the end of that page body; it is not carried into the next page.
     - The existing **final** v1 decode (`tok.decode`) is **unchanged**: it still errors on invalid UTF-8, because U2-T3 keeps v1 output byte-identical.
     - The streaming decoder therefore differs from v1's final decode only in a case where v1's final decode already fails the run.
   - It lives in the tokenizer module. **No new file**, unless the module's layout clearly calls for one.
2. **The observer.** Replace the `stream_broken` logic in `recognize_multi_page_pres` (`mod.rs:2802-2811`, and the flush guard at `:2821`). The observer feeds `postprocess::PageStream` the incremental decoder's complete-character text, so the stream never enters a permanent broken state, `page` events keep flowing, and the final flush always runs. `postprocess::PageStream` itself is pure string logic and stays unchanged.
3. **Invariant.** Streamed bodies are the trimmed raw split chunks, not the polished per-page markdown: terminal output runs `assemble_page` per page and joins with `"\n<PAGE>\n"` (`postprocess.rs:504-514`; `PageStream` doc `:517-529`). So the invariant is: the streamed bodies equal the trimmed `<PAGE>`-split chunks of `strip_eos(decoded)` (a non-blank leading chunk counts as page 1, GH #17), in order, and their count equals the terminal page count. The existing test `multi_page_streaming_matches_terminal_assembly_when_armed` (`tests/e2e_recognize.rs:779-840`) asserts only that the terminal result equals the plain run, plus the event count and order. Extend it to compare each streamed body against those chunks, and add a CJK case.

## Tests
- **Unit:** feed token-by-token sequences where CJK and emoji characters are split across 2–4 tokens. The decoder emits exactly the right characters, at the right time.
- **Unit, page boundary:** the first byte-token of a CJK character, then `<PAGE>`, then text. The first body ends with U+FFFD, the second starts cleanly, and the output matches HF's per-segment decode of the same ids.
- **Property:** for random token sequences from the tokenizer's vocabulary,
  - concat(incremental emits) + flush == the per-segment lossy decode of the same ids, with invalid UTF-8 → U+FFFD. The strict `tok.decode` cannot be the oracle, because it errors on invalid UTF-8 (`src/tokenizer/mod.rs:~705`);
  - no emit ever contains a partial character.
- **v1 streaming regression:** an armed multi-page streaming test on a document containing Chinese text verifies that `page` events keep coming after a split character.
- **The U2-T3 v1 gate stays green.** Final text is unchanged. Streaming events change only in the formerly-broken case; record that as a reviewed golden change if T3 captured an affected stream.
- **Human progress:** the progress sink (`cli.rs:~1887`) shares the PageStream, and it keeps advancing after a split CJK character.

## Acceptance criteria
- All tests are green, and the mandatory checks pass.
- CHANGELOG entry: "fix: multi-page streaming no longer stops emitting page events after a split multi-byte character (CJK)".

Spec: plan D20, R21.
acceptance_criteria:
- All tests are green, and the mandatory checks pass.
- CHANGELOG entry: "fix: multi-page streaming no longer stops emitting page events after a split multi-byte character (CJK)".
close_reason: Fixed: StreamDecoder emits complete UTF-8; armed CJK test fails on old code and passes on new; T3 fast gate equal; full suite green

title: Perf: native packed-int4 dot (no int8 materialization) before ANY int4 decode use
description: MEASURED 2026-06-26 (docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md bd-int4-lmhead): int4 lm_head regressed 5.8x (lm_head phase 2130->12278ms) because simd::int4::igemm_s4s8 UNPACKS nibbles to an int8 buffer in memory before the SDOT -> ~2.5x int8 memory traffic (read 0.5B packed + write 1B int8 + read 1B int8) vs int8's 1B. int4 is strictly slower than int8 for every decode GEMV with this kernel. To ever profit from int4's halved footprint at runtime, build a NATIVE packed-int4 dot: load packed bytes, unpack nibbles IN-REGISTER (NEON vshr/vand or AVX2), feed straight into SDOT/SMMLA accumulators, NEVER materialize an int8 buffer in memory. Unsafe SIMD island + bit-identical scalar fallback (doctrine #3,#6). NOTE low ROI: lm_head is ~14% of decode (perfect int4 <=~4% of a page); experts(45%)+attn(37%) are overhead/f32-bound where a bytes lever doesn't apply. Backlog until a higher-ROI lever is exhausted.
close_reason: Duplicate of bd-2ela (in-register int4->int8 unpack kernel). Measured evidence lives in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md bd-int4-lmhead: current simd::int4::igemm_s4s8 unpacks to a MEMORY buffer (not in-register) -> int4 lm_head regressed 5.8x. bd-2ela IS the fix; bd-vm88 IS the roofline bench (answer: int4 loses with the memory-materializing kernel; decode is overhead/f32-bound, not bandwidth-bound, so int4 ceiling is ~4% of a page even done right).

title: Bench: int4 vs int8 decode GEMV bandwidth + throughput, roofline check
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
int4's entire thesis is **bandwidth**, so the win must be MEASURED, not assumed (NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE doctrine: a win only counts with a head-to-head measured ratio + correctness proof). This bench quantifies the decode bandwidth/throughput win on the expert-MLP shape and checks it against the memory roofline.

## WHAT TO DO
- Criterion bench over the expert SiLU-gated MLP decode GEMV (1280↔896 ×3) and the lm_head GEMV (1280→129280), comparing int4 vs int8 weights at decode (single-token) on each arch tier (SMMLA/SDOT, VNNI/AVX2).
- **Bytes-streamed counter:** assert int4 streams ~half the weight bytes of int8 on the int4-tensor portion.
- **Roofline (§9.1):** compute the memory floor (bytes streamed ÷ DRAM bandwidth); report how close int4 decode sits to it; flag any stage >~1.3x above its floor as a named lever.
- **Fairness controls (§9.3):** best-of-N, fixed thread/allocator/precision; same git state / same `target/` / same minute; `cv_pct` reported (>5% = noise, ineligible); MT8 attribution (the win names a specific ≥0.1% frame).
- Benches skip-green (exit 0) if the model fixture is absent.
- Write the honest ratio + roofline numbers to `PERF_LEDGER.md` with the artifact-graph fields (claim_id, evidence_id, model source commit + fixture hash, CPU feature string, exact command/env, kill-switch state).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- int4 decode GEMV streams ≤ ~half the int8 weight bytes (measured); decode throughput improves with int4 (memory-bound win, §12); ratio + roofline ledgered; correctness proof (P4-int4-gemm-tests) cited alongside the perf claim.

## TESTS REQUIRED
This IS the bench bead (criterion). Pairs with P4-int4-gemm-tests for the correctness half of the keep-gate.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
- `P4-int4-gemm`: benches the kernel it depends on.

title: Phase 5 — CLI hardening + cross-platform release (production single binary, agent-ergonomics maxed)
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
Phase 5 is the productionization phase of franken_ocr — the pure-Rust, CPU-hyper-optimized runner for Baidu Unlimited-OCR (DeepSeek-OCR-derived 3B MoE VLM with R-SWA). The kernels and quant recipe (Phases 1–4) are done; Phase 5 turns the working engine into a **shippable, single static binary per target** that an AI agent (the primary user, per G5) can drive with zero context, and certifies the whole thing honest via the three-pillar gauntlet.

The over-arching goals this epic serves (plan §1.1):
- **G3 Pure-Rust single static binary, cross-platform**: one `focr` binary per target (linux x86-64/arm64, darwin x86-64/arm64, windows-msvc x86-64), no Python, no FFI, no network at inference time, no GPU required.
- **G5 Agent-ergonomic**: `robot` subcommand emitting versioned NDJSON with a self-describing `robot schema`, stable exit codes, `--json` everywhere, deterministic output under fixed sampling.
- **G6 Embeddable**: library API stays synchronous/blocking; runtime is an owned detail.
- **G7 Honest**: every accepted divergence ledgered; the release-readiness scorecard must be all-green before ship.

## WHAT TO DO (the Phase 5 task set, plan §10 Phase 5)
Goals: production single-binary release, agent-ergonomics maxed. Tasks:
1. Finalize subcommands / exit codes / env overrides (§7.2, §7.4, §7.5).
2. Robot contract tests + frozen schema (§7.3, AGENTS Agent-Ergonomics Requirements).
3. `doctor` — idempotent, reversible, capability reflection (§7.2, world-class-doctor-mode skill).
4. Per-page streaming polish (mpsc + std::thread, bounded sync_channel, recv_timeout ~40ms loop; §3.3, §7.3).
5. 5-target release build + `install.sh` + SHA-256 checksums (§7.6, /release-preparations, /installer-workmanship).
6. Agent-ergonomics audit (/agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools).
7. Release-readiness scorecard (§8.4).
8. Run the three-pillar gauntlet to convergence (§8.5) and produce the certification bundle (cross-ref E-VERIFY).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Two `[[bin]]` (`focr` short + `franken_ocr` long), both → `src/main.rs`; `fn main()` is SYNCHRONOUS (clap parse → install ctrlc ShutdownController → sync `run(cli)` → exit-code mapping). The asupersync runtime is owned by `OcrEngine` below main (§3.3, AGENTS doctrine #9). This is the franken_whisper template, proven.
- Robot mode is line-oriented NDJSON with a `ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` const on every line; human decoration NEVER mixed with machine output in robot mode (AGENTS).
- **v1 is IMAGE-ONLY** — PDF stays off the CLI surface (§7.7): a pure-Rust raster at byte-parity with pymupdf@300DPI is unscoped and any pixel mismatch blows the L0 preprocessing parity gate.
- The release build has a **real gotcha**: franken_ocr uses local `../` path deps (ft-kernel-cpu, ft-core, ft-serialize, asupersync, fsqlite). Path deps break standard GH-Actions CI (release-preparations OP-6) — the 5-target build likely needs Path B (dsr/rch local build) or vendoring. Plan for this.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- The gauntlet is the conscience: no victory-on-one-pillar-while-another-regresses; release cannot ship with a red parity cell or an unledgered divergence (§8.4, §8.5).
- Cross-compile/nightly: nightly required for stdarch i8mm/dotprod, scalar fallback must cross-compile to every target; runtime SIMD dispatch → one binary per arch.
- Determinism gate: same image+args → byte-identical output under greedy; this is a hard gate for robot mode.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (Phase 5 exit gates, plan §10)
- All 5 targets build + smoke-test.
- Robot schema stable + self-describing (`robot schema` self-describes the contract; contract test green).
- Release-readiness scorecard all-green (L0–L5 parity, surface parity, honest perf, determinism, build matrix, ledger completeness).
- `install.sh` verified (curl-pipe install, checksum-verified, idempotent).
- Agent-ergonomics score above bar.
- Three-pillar gauntlet converged (≥10 rounds, ≥2 clean) and certification bundle produced.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on **E-P4** (int4 refinement — the final quant tier must be locked so the release ships the production weights and the scorecard certifies the shipped numerics) and **E-VERIFY** (the verification gauntlet/conformance machinery — Phase 5 RUNS that machinery to convergence and packages its certification bundle; we do not rebuild it). Each child task carries its own finer-grained deps.

title: Finalize CLI subcommands, exit codes, and env overrides (the stable surface)
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The `focr` CLI is the agent-facing contract (G5). Before we can contract-test the robot schema, audit ergonomics, or certify the release, the **command surface, exit-code dictionary, and env-override set must be frozen and complete**. This is the foundational task all other Phase-5 work nests on. Earlier phases shipped stubs (`convert`/`ocr`/`doctor` in Phase 0); Phase 5 finalizes them.

## WHAT TO DO
Finalize the exact subcommand table (plan §7.2), wired in `src/cli.rs` (clap-derive `Cli`/`Command`/`Args`, `to_request()` validation) and dispatched from sync `src/main.rs`:

| Subcommand | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `focr ocr <image>` | Parse a document IMAGE → markdown (human default) or `--json`. v1 IMAGE-ONLY. |
| `focr ocr --robot` (or `focr robot run`) | Streaming NDJSON events for agents |
| `focr convert <safetensors> -o <.focrq> [--arch ...] [--quant int8\|int4]` | Offline weight transformation |
| `focr robot schema` | Self-describing event/contract schema (versioned) |
| `focr robot health` | Diagnostics: model present? arch features? threads? |
| `focr robot backends` | Detected SIMD tiers (SMMLA/SDOT/VNNI/AMX/scalar), core count |
| `focr runs [--id\|--limit\|--format plain\|json\|ndjson]` | Query run history (fsqlite) |
| `focr sync export-jsonl\|import-jsonl` | Audit export/import (locked, atomic, one-way) |
| `focr doctor` | Idempotent self-check/repair |

**Exit codes (stable, documented in `src/error.rs`; plan §7.4):** `0` success · `1` generic error · `2` usage/CLI error · `3` model not found / not resolvable · `4` input decode error (bad image/PDF) · `5` budget/timeout exceeded · `6` cancelled (Ctrl+C) · `7` format/version mismatch (`.focrq`). The `robot run_error` event MUST carry the same code in its payload.

**Env overrides (read once via `OnceLock`; plan §7.5):** `FOCR_MODEL_DIR`, `FOCR_THREADS`, `FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_<STAGE>_MS`, `FOCR_QUANT` (int8/int4/f32 select if multiple `.focrq` present), `FOCR_FORCE_ARCH` (override SIMD dispatch for testing), `FOCR_NO_REPEAT_NGRAM` (default 35). Each numerics-affecting lever is documented in its own doc-comment, defaulted by a measured A/B, and has an opt-out.

**Model resolution (`resolve_model(spec)`):** existing path OR short name searched across an ordered, env-driven list (`$FOCR_MODEL_DIR`, `~/.cache/franken_ocr/models`, …), failing with an **actionable** error listing every searched dir. `native_model_available()` does a cheap header sniff (magic bytes), no tensor load.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Exit `1` is NEVER used to mean "ran fine, no results" — that is exit `0` with an empty JSON array (agent-ergonomics Axiom 5). An agent must be able to write `case $? in 3) ...; 5) ...; esac` deterministically.
- `pdf` does NOT appear in the CLI surface in v1 (§7.7) — accepting it would over-promise; PDFs are rasterized out-of-band by the user.
- Every numerics-affecting env var is a documented, measured, opt-out-able lever (no silent numerics changes — G7).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Backwards-compat: we are pre-users with NO tech debt allowed (AGENTS) — finalize the RIGHT surface now, no compatibility shims.
- Stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics (Axiom 4) — no log line may leak into `--json`/NDJSON stdout. Honor `NO_COLOR`/non-TTY for any human decoration.
- `--version` must embed the MIT "Copyright (c) 2026 Baidu" license notice (license risk mitigation, §11).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Every subcommand in the table is wired, parses, and returns the correct documented exit code on each error class.
- `error.rs` defines the exit-code enum; a unit test asserts the numeric value of each variant matches §7.4.
- All 6 env vars resolve through a single `OnceLock`-backed config path with a doc-comment each.
- `resolve_model` failure lists every searched directory verbatim in the error.
- `pdf` is absent from `--help` output.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit: exit-code numeric stability test (asserts 0..7 mapping); env-override parsing (valid/invalid/unset → default); `resolve_model` happy/missing/ambiguous paths with the actionable-error assertion.
- Integration (P5-subcommands-tests): drive each subcommand via the built binary with structured logging of (argv, exit code, stdout/stderr split), asserting the exit-code contract end-to-end.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on **E-P4**: the final `--quant int4` path and the `.focrq` format-version must be locked so the `convert` subcommand and `FOCR_QUANT`/exit-7 (format/version mismatch) reflect the shipped reality.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## ADDENDUM (review2): per-stage budget enumeration, OnceLock read-once contract, runs/sync handoff
- **`FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_<STAGE>_MS` is a FAMILY, not one var — enumerate the closed set against §4.2.** The nine pipeline stages are: `load`/`preprocess`/`tokenize`/`vision_encode`/`connector`/`prefill`/`decode`/`postprocess`/`emit`. Document each `FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_<STAGE>_MS` lever explicitly so an agent can discover the full set (e.g. via `doctor capabilities --json` / `robot health`), and add a unit test that every §4.2 `PipelineStage` variant has a corresponding parseable budget env var (no stage silently un-budgetable). An unknown stage name in the env var must fail with an actionable error listing the valid stage names.
- **OnceLock read-once is a CONTRACT, test it.** Every numerics-/budget-affecting env var is read EXACTLY ONCE via `OnceLock` at startup — no mid-run re-read (so a streaming run cannot change behavior partway). Add a test asserting a var mutated after first read does not change in-flight behavior. This is what makes determinism (§7.3) and the robot contract stable.
- **`runs` + `sync` finalization moved to P5-r2-runs-sync-surface.** This bead's subcommand TABLE still lists `focr runs` and `focr sync export-jsonl|import-jsonl` as part of the frozen surface, but their detailed behavior, output schema, `_meta` versioned migrations, and locked/atomic/one-way semantics + tests are owned by the new bead **P5-r2-runs-sync-surface** (depends on this one). If `sync` lock-contention needs an exit code beyond the §7.4 dictionary, DECIDE it here and update §7.4 deliberately (no ad-hoc codes).
close_reason: Done-in-code (status lag; closing to unblock its dependents). Every acceptance criterion verifiable in the shipped tree: (1) every subcommand in the §7.2 table is wired, parses, and returns documented exit codes — the FULL surface (ocr/ocr-batch/convert/pull/models/robot run|schema|health|backends|selftest/runs/sync/doctor) shipped across v0.1.0-v0.3.0 and is contract-tested (cli_robot_golden 36/36 green incl exit_code_conformance + usage-vs-notimplemented splits; enumeration locked by tests/surface_matrix.rs against clap introspection). (2) error.rs exit-code enum with unit tests exit_codes_are_stable + exit_code_table_is_complete_and_unique asserting §7.4 numeric values (0..7, frozen in robot_schema_v1.json exit_codes). (3) env overrides resolve through OnceLock-backed paths with doc comments (bd-223.7 closed; FOCR_THREADS budget bd-223.2; 16 OnceLock sites across lib/cli/native_engine). (4) resolve_model failure lists every searched directory verbatim (native_engine/mod.rs:740-750 'searched directories: ...; set FOCR_MODEL_DIR'). (5) The 'pdf absent from --help' criterion is SUPERSEDED by doctrine change: native scanned-PDF input SHIPPED in v0.2.0 (bd-0a7.1-.3 closed, decompress-bomb bounded bd-2zpu) — FEATURE_PARITY §12 scores it partial (vector rasterization deferred, bd-0a7.4) instead of excluded; help output correctly documents it. Surface pillar rows for this bead's scope are present in FEATURE_PARITY.md §12 with per-row evidence (2026-07-06).

title: Integration tests for CLI subcommand surface + exit-code contract
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The exit-code dictionary and subcommand surface are the part of the contract agents branch on. A regression here silently breaks every downstream agent script, so it needs an end-to-end test that drives the actual built binary (not just the parser), with the comprehensive structured logging this project mandates.

## WHAT TO DO
In `tests/` add a CLI-surface integration test that, for each subcommand and each documented error class, invokes the compiled `focr` binary and asserts:
- the exit code matches §7.4 (`0`/`1`/`2`/`3`/`4`/`5`/`6`/`7`),
- stdout is pure data (parses as JSON when `--json`/robot; no diagnostic lines),
- stderr carries diagnostics only,
- the actionable model-not-found error (exit `3`) lists every searched dir.
Emit one NDJSON log line per case `{case, argv, exit_code, stdout_bytes, stderr_first_line, pass}` so failures are diagnosable from logs alone.

title: Release-readiness scorecard (all-green ship gate) tying every Phase-5 deliverable together
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The release-readiness scorecard is the single all-green ship gate (plan §8.4, §12). It is the convergent honest evaluation that a release cannot ship past with a red parity cell or an unledgered divergence. It aggregates every Phase-5 deliverable into one go/no-go.

## WHAT TO DO (plan §8.4, §10 Phase 5 exit gates, §12 success metrics)
Produce the scorecard with these cells, each green/red with cited evidence:
- **Parity (L0–L5)** all green — per-layer cosine ≥0.9999 (f32), decoded text exact where reference deterministic, int8/int4 CER within ledgered budget (CVaR/tail bound per AF-2, not just mean), determinism gate green. (from P5-gauntlet-to-convergence)
- **Surface parity** — CLI/contract FeatureUniverse dashboard; PDF `excluded`, every other surface `present`. (from P5-gauntlet + P5-robot-contract-tests)
- **Honest perf vs reference** — gauntlet per-stage ratios in `PERF_LEDGER.md` with §9.3 fairness controls; decode-per-token beats the Phase −1 proven CPU reference. (from P5-gauntlet)
- **Determinism** — same image+args → byte-identical output under greedy.
- **Cross-platform build matrix** — all 5 targets build + smoke-test. (from P5-release-build-matrix)
- **Installer** — install.sh verified, checksums present. (from P5-install-sh-checksums)
- **Agent-ergonomics** — audit score above bar. (from P5-agent-ergonomics-audit)
- **Robot schema** — stable + self-describing + contract-tested. (from P5-robot-schema-frozen / P5-robot-contract-tests)
- **Doctor** — idempotent + reversible + ≥700 rubric, fixtures round-trip. (from P5-doctor-fixtures)
- **Deadlock watchdog** — `many_pages_without_deadlock` green. (from P5-streaming-deadlock-watchdog)
- **Ledger completeness** — every accepted divergence in `DISCREPANCIES.md`, every rejected lever in `NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md`, certification bundle present. (from P5-certification-bundle)

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- The scorecard uses the conformal LOWER bound for the parity cell (not the point estimate) — the formal version of "parity gate first" (§8.5).
- A release cannot ship with ANY red cell or an unledgered divergence (G7) — the scorecard is a hard gate, not advisory.
- It binds the whole epic: it depends on every other Phase-5 deliverable so it cannot be green until they all are.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Correctness outranks speed (G1 > G2): a red parity cell blocks ship even if every perf cell is green.
- Vision-prefill parity-or-slower in f32 v1 is GREEN (acceptable per G2 reframing) as long as it's recorded honestly — the scorecard must encode that nuance, not flag it red.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (the Phase 5 exit gate)
- Every scorecard cell green with cited evidence (artifact path / test name / fixture).
- No unledgered divergence; certification bundle present and re-verifies.
- The scorecard is committed and reproducible (a script regenerates it from the artifacts).

## TESTS REQUIRED
- A scorecard-validation script that reads each cell's evidence artifact and asserts green; fails if any evidence is missing/stale (structured log `{cell, evidence, status}`).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
This is the capstone: depends on **P5-gauntlet-to-convergence** + **P5-certification-bundle** (parity/perf/surface/ledger cells), **P5-install-sh-checksums** (installer cell), **P5-agent-ergonomics-audit** (ergonomics cell), **P5-robot-contract-tests** (robot-schema cell), **P5-doctor-fixtures** (doctor cell), and **P5-streaming-deadlock-watchdog** (deadlock cell). It is green only when all are.
close_reason: SHIP GATE ALL-GREEN (c29a78b): gauntlet_cert --release-readiness = 13 green / 0 red / ship=true. Every cell live: parity L0-L5 armed (L4 token-exact, L5 cer=0), surface parity, perf vs reference (3.41x/2.81x cv%-gated), determinism e-processes, deadlock watchdog, robot schema, build matrix, installer, ledger completeness, agent ergonomics, doctor, certification bundle (certified cert), gauntlet convergence (11 rounds).

title: Finalize + test `focr runs` and `focr sync export-jsonl|import-jsonl` (run-history + audit-export surface)
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The §7.2 subcommand table (and the table inside `P5-subcommands-exit-env`) lists two surfaces that NO Phase-5 bead actually finalizes, specifies, or tests:
- `focr runs [--id | --limit | --format plain|json|ndjson]` — query run history from the fsqlite `RunStore` (§4.1 `storage.rs`, `_meta` versioned schema + forward migrations).
- `focr sync export-jsonl | import-jsonl` — locked, atomic, one-way audit export/import (§4.1 `sync.rs`).

`P5-subcommands-exit-env` finalizes the surface in the abstract but its TESTS REQUIRED and the integration bead `P5-subcommands-tests` enumerate cases for `ocr`/`convert`/usage/`robot schema|health|backends`/`doctor`/cancellation/budget ONLY — `runs` and `sync` are never driven, schema-checked, or contract-frozen. Because `P5-gauntlet-to-convergence` accounts EVERY CLI surface via the FeatureUniverse/SurfaceMatrix as `present|partial|missing` (and `partial` never rounds up), these two land as coverage DEBT and would block the all-green release-readiness scorecard (`P5-release-readiness-scorecard`). This bead closes that hole so the surface-parity pillar is honestly `present`.

## WHAT TO DO
### `focr runs`
- Wire `focr runs` over the `RunStore` (fsqlite, NEVER rusqlite): `--id <run-id>` (one run), `--limit N` (most-recent N), `--format plain|json|ndjson`.
- Define and FREEZE the run-record schema (run id, input path, mode base/gundam, args summary, started_at, elapsed_ms per-stage totals, exit code, output summary, model source commit/fixture-provenance hash if available). `--format json` emits one JSON document; `--format ndjson` emits one object per run carrying a `schema_version` const (reuse the robot `ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` discipline or a sibling `RUNS_SCHEMA_VERSION`).
- Empty history returns exit 0 + an EMPTY array/stream (NOT exit 1) — agent-ergonomics Axiom 5 (no-results is success).
- stdout is pure data under `--format json|ndjson`; stderr diagnostics only (Axiom 4).
- `_meta` versioned schema + forward migrations: opening an older-schema store auto-migrates forward (or fails with the §7.4 exit 7 format/version mismatch if not migratable), with a unit test for the migration path.

### `focr sync export-jsonl | import-jsonl`
- Implement the locked/atomic/one-way audit semantics (§4.1 `sync.rs`): export the run-history to JSONL under a file lock, atomically (temp-file + rename), one-way (export is the canonical direction; import is for restoring an audit trail, not bidirectional merge). Document the one-way contract explicitly so an agent never expects a two-way sync.
- Atomicity: a crash mid-export leaves either the old file intact or a complete new file — never a torn JSONL. Test with a simulated interruption.
- Idempotence: re-exporting identical history produces byte-identical JSONL (after scrubbing any timing/run-id non-determinism, per §8.6 scrubbed-golden discipline).
- Exit codes follow §7.4: lock contention → a documented code (reuse the doctor `5 concurrency lost` convention is NOT valid at top level — pick from the §7.4 dictionary, default `1` generic with an actionable message, or extend the dictionary deliberately and update `P5-subcommands-exit-env`).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- These are READ-side / audit surfaces; per the ergonomics audit (Axiom 8) every read-side command must have `--json`/structured output — `runs` already does, `sync` is inherently structured (JSONL).
- One-way is a deliberate safety choice: an audit export must not silently overwrite live history on import; import is additive/restorative and documented as such.
- Schema is frozen as a fixture so drift is a CI failure, mirroring the robot-schema discipline.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- Model-gated: `runs`/`sync` operate on the RunStore, which exists WITHOUT the 6.67 GB weights (a stub/empty store) — so these tests run green in CI with no weights. Seed the store with a synthetic run record to exercise the formats.
- The fsqlite store and its `_meta` schema are owned by Phase-0 `storage.rs`; this bead FINALIZES the query/export surface on top, it does not re-architect storage.
- Do NOT let the JSONL export leak diagnostic lines into the data stream (Axiom 4) — it must round-trip through `import-jsonl` cleanly.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `focr runs` with each `--format` emits the documented, version-stamped schema; empty history → exit 0 + empty array/stream.
- `_meta` forward-migration path tested (older store opens and migrates, or returns exit 7).
- `focr sync export-jsonl` is locked + atomic (interruption leaves a non-torn file) + one-way + idempotent (byte-identical after scrub); `import-jsonl` restores it.
- A frozen schema fixture (`tests/fixtures/runs_schema.json`) is committed and matches `runs --format json` output.
- Both surfaces are accounted `present` in the FeatureUniverse so the surface-parity pillar is all-green.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit: run-record (de)serialization round-trip; `_meta` forward-migration; empty-history → exit 0 + empty.
- Integration (drive the built binary): `runs --format plain|json|ndjson` (assert pure-data stdout, valid JSON/NDJSON, schema match); `sync export-jsonl` → `import-jsonl` round-trip (byte-identical after scrub); atomicity under simulated interruption; lock-contention behavior. Emit one NDJSON log line per case `{case, argv, exit_code, stdout_bytes, schema_ok, pass}` and a summary `{total, passed, skipped}`.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on **P5-subcommands-exit-env** (it finalizes the surface these two commands live in, the exit-code dictionary, and the env/model resolution they share). Feeds **P5-gauntlet-to-convergence** (surface-parity pillar accounts these as `present`) and is audited by **P5-agent-ergonomics-audit** (read-side `--json` requirement).
close_reason: Both surfaces finalized, frozen, and contract-tested through the REAL binary (parent epic bd-wp8 stays open for its other children — force-close per the established done-in-code protocol). focr runs: --id/--limit/--format plain|json|ndjson all exercised over a POPULATED hermetic store (seeded via the public sync import-jsonl path); empty history = exit 0 + count 0 + empty array (Axiom 5); stdout pure data under json/ndjson (Axiom 4). FROZEN contract at tests/fixtures/runs_schema.json (versioned by hand; registered in MANIFEST/PROVENANCE): the 10-field record shape shared verbatim by runs json, runs ndjson lines, and every sync export-jsonl line — one contract, three carriers — with runs_schema_contract_over_populated_store failing on drift. _meta forward-migration + too-new exit-7 refusal unit-tested (bd-223.4). focr sync: locked (.lock, contention fails fast — tested) + atomic (temp+fsync+rename, no residue) + idempotent (byte-identical re-export at storage AND CLI layers) + ONE-WAY documented on the SyncCmd help surface and in the fixture; malformed import fails loud with line number. FEATURE_PARITY rows partial→present (rollup 41/11/3, enforced by surface_matrix.rs). Drive-by: golden harness made truly hermetic (HOME/LOCALAPPDATA/USERPROFILE pinned to an empty per-process temp dir); 36/36 green. Commit aab7829.

title: Freeze the robot NDJSON event schema + self-describing `robot schema`
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
Robot mode is the primary agent interface (G5). For agents to parse it durably it must be a **stable, versioned, self-describing** contract. This task freezes the event schema and makes `focr robot schema` emit the machine-readable contract that downstream agents (and the contract test) validate against.

## WHAT TO DO (plan §7.3, AGENTS Agent-Ergonomics Requirements)
- Define the NDJSON event stream in `src/robot.rs`: one JSON object per line, **every line carrying `schema_version`** (the `ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` const). Event types and their fields:
  - `run_start` — run id, input path, mode (base/gundam), args summary, schema_version.
  - `stage` — stage name, seq, elapsed_ms, budget_ms (one of the §4.2 pipeline stages: load/preprocess/tokenize/vision_encode/connector/prefill/decode/postprocess/emit).
  - `page` — per-page text + bbox as it completes (the streaming unit).
  - `run_complete` — totals, output summary.
  - `run_error` — message + the §7.4 exit code in payload.
- Implement `focr robot schema` to emit the self-describing, machine-readable contract for ALL event types (compact single-line JSON, parseable by agents). This is the source of truth the contract test pins.
- Bump `ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` deliberately; document the version policy.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- Single-line compact JSON even for `robot schema` so simple agent parsers handle it (§7.3).
- Robot mode NEVER mixes human decoration with machine output (AGENTS): stdout is the event stream, stderr is diagnostics.
- The schema is frozen as a fixture so any drift is a CI failure, not a silent break (the `🧪 Pin-The-Contract-Test` operator from agent-ergonomics Axiom 8).

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- `page` events carry decoded text + bbox coords (`/999 → ×W/H`); under multi-page R-SWA the pages are cross-page dependent (OQ-13) — the event stream must NOT imply pages are independent; it just reports them as they complete in the single sequential pass.
- Timing fields (`elapsed_ms`) make output non-deterministic — they must be scrubbed in golden/contract comparison (see P5-robot-contract-tests).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Every emitted line carries `schema_version == ROBOT_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- `focr robot schema` emits a complete, self-describing, single-line-JSON contract covering all 5 event types and their fields.
- A frozen JSON schema fixture (`tests/fixtures/robot_schema.json`) is committed and matches the `robot schema` output.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit: schema-completeness test (every event type the engine can emit is present in `robot schema`).
- The contract test itself lives in P5-robot-contract-tests (separate bead).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on **P5-subcommands-exit-env**: `run_error` must carry the finalized §7.4 exit codes, and the `robot run`/`robot schema`/`robot health`/`robot backends` subcommands must be finalized first.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## ADDENDUM (review2): the `stage` event must enumerate the §4.2 closed stage set
- The `stage` event's `stage` field is a CLOSED enum over the nine §4.2 pipeline stages: `load`/`preprocess`/`tokenize`/`vision_encode`/`connector`/`prefill`/`decode`/`postprocess`/`emit`. The self-describing `robot schema` MUST list this closed set (not just say 'a stage name string') so an agent can branch on stages deterministically, and the schema-completeness unit test must assert every §4.2 `PipelineStage` variant appears in the schema's stage enumeration. This also lets the `FOCR_STAGE_BUDGET_<STAGE>_MS` budgets and the `stage` events share one source-of-truth stage list.
- Clarify the `run_error` exit-code field: the schema must declare the value domain as the §7.4 dictionary `{0..7}` so the contract test (P5-robot-contract-tests) can assert membership, not just integer-ness.

title: Robot contract test: validate emitted NDJSON against the frozen schema fixture
description:

A frozen schema is only enforced if a test fails when emitted events drift from it. This `robot_contract_tests.rs` is the enforcement (AGENTS: "a contract test validates emitted events against a frozen JSON schema fixture"). It is what lets agents trust the contract across versions.

  - the event sequence is well-formed: `run_start` … `stage`* / `page`* … (`run_complete` XOR `run_error`);

- Model-gated: when weights are absent, drive the well-formedness checks with a forced-error run so the test still exercises the schema path and stays green (skip-with-SUCCESS for the full-OCR case).

title: Per-page streaming polish: bounded mpsc + std::thread worker, recv_timeout loop
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
Streaming per-page results as they complete is what makes `focr` usable on dozens of pages in one pass (the "Unlimited" long-document story) and what feeds the robot `page` events. The streaming transport must be **bounded** (backpressure, never unbounded growth) and must NOT violate the deadlock rule that burned the sibling project for 5 commits.

## WHAT TO DO (plan §3.3, §7.3)
- Implement the proven transport: a worker `std::thread` runs the engine and pushes per-page results into a **bounded `std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel`**; `main` (or the robot emitter) loops on `recv_timeout(~40ms)` emitting events until `worker.is_finished()`, then drains remaining and `join()`s the worker.
- Thread a `Copy` `CancellationToken` (deadline + global `ShutdownController`) INTO the worker closure (cancellation is cooperative — `spawn_blocking` keeps running on drop), with `checkpoint()` at per-page and per-decode-step boundaries so Ctrl+C / per-page timeout aborts at the next boundary (exit 6 / exit 5 respectively).
- "Streaming per-page" = streaming the OUTPUT of a SEQUENTIALLY-processed page — never concurrent forwards. The outer page/document loop is sequential; each forward fans out across all cores internally via the kernel's own rayon pool.

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE (the load-bearing deadlock lessons)
- **NEVER nest rayon under a held lock; NEVER nest a second asupersync runtime inside a task** (AGENTS doctrine #5). Single `OcrModel` behind a cache; sequential outer loop; one live forward at a time; small `blocking_threads` (e.g. `(1,2)`) is a guard, not the mechanism. Concurrent forwards would oversubscribe rayon N× — the exact bug the frankensearch deadlock saga converged on after 5 commits.
- Bounded channel = backpressure; an unbounded channel would let a slow consumer grow memory without limit. The runtime ships a **capacity certificate** (p95/p99 queueing evidence + proof of no nested-runtime / no rayon-pool oversubscription) as a gauntlet artifact (§3.3).
- `recv_timeout(~40ms)` lets main interleave emit + liveness checks without busy-spinning.

## CONSIDERATIONS / RISKS / GOTCHAS
- The kill condition is the `many_pages_without_deadlock` CI watchdog (pages ≫ pool) — it hangs on regression. This MUST stay green.
- USL pool caps (AF-5 / §6.9): the rayon pool is pinned to physical cores and capped at its USL peak, not `num_cpus`, so the single fan-out doesn't β-dominate on a 64-core host.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Streaming uses a bounded `sync_channel`; no unbounded buffering anywhere in the path.
- `page` events emit incrementally (first page emitted before the last page is decoded).
- Ctrl+C aborts at the next checkpoint with exit 6; per-page budget overrun aborts with exit 5.
- `many_pages_without_deadlock` watchdog green.

## TESTS REQUIRED
- Unit: bounded-channel backpressure (producer blocks when buffer full; no growth).
- The deadlock watchdog is P5-streaming-deadlock-watchdog (separate bead).

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on **E-P4**: the decode path streaming wraps is the final int4 production forward; streaming behavior must be measured on the shipped numerics.

---
## REFINEMENT NOTE (deep-review pass 2)


## ADDENDUM (review2): bounded-channel capacity is the capacity-certificate input; USL pool-cap source-of-truth
- The bounded `sync_channel` CAPACITY is not arbitrary — it is the input to the §3.3 **capacity certificate** the gauntlet ships (p95/p99 queueing evidence, proof of no nested-runtime / no rayon-pool oversubscription). Document the chosen capacity and its rationale, and emit the queueing telemetry (occupancy, blocked-producer count) needed for that certificate from the streaming path itself, so `P5-gauntlet-to-convergence` can consume it as an artifact rather than re-deriving it.
- The rayon pool cap is pinned to physical cores AND capped at its **USL peak (§6.9 / AF-5)**, not `num_cpus`. That cap is owned by the Phase-3 §6.9 USL pool-sizing work (E-P3), not chosen here — this bead CONSUMES that cap. Make the dependency explicit so the streaming worker does not independently pick a pool size that contradicts the USL certificate. If §6.9's cap is not yet available, the streaming path must read it from a single config source, never hardcode.
- Reaffirm: cancellation via the `Copy` `CancellationToken` must `checkpoint()` at BOTH per-page and per-decode-step boundaries; add an explicit test that a per-decode-step Ctrl+C (mid-page) still aborts at the next decode checkpoint with exit 6 (not only at page boundaries) — otherwise a long single page is uninterruptible.

title: `many_pages_without_deadlock` CI watchdog (pages ≫ pool, hangs on regression)
description:
## BACKGROUND / WHY
The nested-rayon-under-lock / nested-runtime deadlock is the single most expensive recurring bug in the sibling lineage (the frankensearch deadlock saga, 5 commits). The durable fix is architectural (sequential outer loop, one live forward, kernel-internal fan-out), and the durable PROOF is a watchdog test that HANGS on regression so CI catches any reintroduction.

## WHAT TO DO (AGENTS doctrine #5, plan §3.3, §11)
- Add a `many_pages_without_deadlock` test that streams a number of pages **far exceeding the worker/blocking-thread pool** through the real streaming path (P5-streaming-polish), with a wall-clock timeout. If the engine ever nests rayon under a held lock or spins up a second runtime, the test hangs and CI fails (timeout → red).
- Assert: all pages stream to completion; no page is dropped; exactly one forward is live at a time (instrument a counter that must never exceed 1).
- Run it under the gauntlet `many_pages` soak to also exercise the capacity certificate (p95/p99 queueing, no oversubscription).

## KEY DESIGN DECISIONS + RATIONALE
- The test must use pages ≫ pool so any accidental concurrency or lock-nesting actually deadlocks (a small page count could pass by luck).
- Model-gated: can run with a tiny synthetic/stub forward so it stays green without the 6.67 GB weights while still exercising the orchestration topology.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Test green (completes well under its timeout) on the correct sequential-loop topology.
- Live-forward counter never exceeds 1.
- Test is wired as a CI gate (not opt-in).

## TESTS REQUIRED
This bead is the watchdog test. Structured log: `{pages, pool_size, max_concurrent_forwards, completed, elapsed_ms}`.

## DEPENDENCIES NOTE
Depends on **P5-streaming-polish** — it watchdogs exactly that streaming/orchestration topology.
